column2: After the founding of the Republic of China, Guangxi served as the base for one of the more powerful warlord cliques of China: the Old Guangxi Clique. Led by Lu Rongting, the clique had influence over neighboring Hunan and Guangdong provinces. However, Guangxi remained cautious over antagonizing the central government in Beijing during the failed Second Revolution, and as a result, that mantle fell into the hands of neighboring Yunnan. They joined Yunnan during the National Protection War, but split off after Sun Zhongshan returned from overseas. As the Constitution Protection movement, a branch of the Nationalist Party, grew in power, the Old Guangxi Clique became increasingly at odds with Sun Zhongshan. This lasted until the faction was defeated in the Guangdong-Guangxi war and was replaced by the pro-Nationalist New Guangxi Clique.
column5: Tras proclamarse la republica en 1912, la Antigua Camarilla de Guangxi, mandada por Lu Rongting, consolido su dominio en el sur extendiendose hacia Guangdong y Hunan. Pese a apoyar la Guerra de Proteccion Nacional frente a las pretensiones monarquicas de Yuan Shikai, los caudillos de Guangxi chocaron con Sun Yat-sen y el movimiento constitucionalista por el control territorial de la region.

column2: In 1939, the War of Resistance was not proceeding well. All of the most well-developed sectors of China had fallen into Japanese hands. Li Zongren was worried that a Japanese flank attack against the lightly defended city of Guangzhou would have devastating effects on the Resistance. To make matters worse, the internal squabbling amongst the warlords and the Nationalist Government was making the Chinese military inept and impotent. The entire Second Chinese United Front needed to shape up and fight together against the Japanese aggressors, and resist to the bitter end.
column5: La caida de las provincias costeras e industriales ante Japon debilita la resistencia china en 1939. Al general Li Zongren le preocupa que una ofensiva japonesa contra Guangzhou desmorone el flanco meridional. La Nueva Camarilla de Guangxi debe coordinar sus fuerzas veteranas con el Ejercito Nacional Revolucionario en el Segundo Frente Unido para resistir el embate invasor.

column2: In late 1935, tensions were rising between Nationalist China and the warlord alliance of Guangxi and Guangdong, who were stationed in southern China. Guangdong generals had been the weak point of Chiang's encirclement campaigns, which had allowed the Communists to escape. Earlier in the late 1920s, the Guangxi Clique rose in opposition to Chiang Kai-shek, but were crushed by the Generalissimo's duplicity. Chiang also used the Long March to consolidate and strenghten and expand his power base, which made him much stronger against the warlords. Guangxi, one of the few warlords with their own fleet and airforce, struggles to become the leader in the opposition against Chiang's domination of the Chinese subcontinent.
column5: A finales de 1935, la rivalidad entre el gobierno central de Nankin y la camarilla de Guangxi de Li Zongren y Bai Chongxi amenaza con reanudar las hostilidades internas. Al disponer de una administracion disciplinada, cuadros militares competentes y aviacion propia, Guangxi resiste la subordinacion completa ante Chiang Kai-shek mientras observa la creciente agresion japonesa.

column2: Founded in 1920, the Communist Party of China was initially a study group inspired by the May Fourth nationalistic movement. Given Sun Zhongshan's acceptance of all revolutionary groups, the CPC joined the KMT attempting to reform and reduce corruption from within. They participated in the Northern China Expedition fighting warlords along with the early legislature. This, sadly, led to divisions within the group. On one side stood the ideologists who believed in Marxist-Leninism and were opposed to the alliance with the KMT. The other favored moderate reforms and cooperation against imperialism. After Sun Zhongshan's death, the KMT ruptured as well with Jiang Jieshi massacring pro-cooperation members of the CPC in Nanjing while his rivals in Wuhan kept the alliance. The failure of cooperation and harsh persecution within the KMT controlled cities led to a reverse of CPC's policies. Slowly, moderates in both the KMT and CPC became silenced and disillusioned. A new leadership led by Mao Zhedong and Zhu De emerged focusing on rural support of the party, fighting corrupt warlords, and Chinese nationalism. Civil War looms on the horizon once again while crooked nepotism and Japanese aggression remain unchecked. Will the Communists manage to save the country from ruin by the ruling KMT?
column5: Tras romperse la alianza inicial con el Kuomintang en 1927 mediante las purgas anticomunistas de Chiang Kai-shek, el Partido Comunista de China abandono las ciudades para organizar bases guerrilleras campesinas. Liderado militarmente por Mao Zedong y Zhu De en el soviet de Jiangxi, el Ejercito Rojo resiste las campanas de cerco nacionalistas mientras denuncia el avance colonial japones.

column2: The early 1930's were both good times and bad times for Nationalist China. On the one hand, the Guomindang regime under Chiang Kai-Shek was at the peak of it's power, having driven Mao Tse-tung's Communists on their grueling 6,000 mile march to Shaanxi and established themselves as the most powerful force in Chinese politics. It seemed that China was at last united under a stable, modernizing regime, ready to bring the country into the 20th century after years of humiliation at the hands of stronger countries. However, it faced a severe challenge: an increasingly belligerent and imperialist Japan desiring to expand it's resource base at China's expense. Having already conceded control of Manchuria to the Japanese in 1931, China seems destined for further clashes with the island nation, yet in early 1936 Chiang shows no signs of letting up in his civil war against the Communists. The question China must now face is a sore one: when and if Japan continues her expansion, will the Nationalists fight, or will China be humiliated yet again?
column5: Tras el asedio a las bases soviéticas del sur, el Ejercito Rojo culmino la agotadora Larga Marcha hasta refugiarse en Shaanxi. Pese a las duras bajas sufridas, la direccion de Mao Zedong ha consolidado su autoridad ideologica en Yan'an. Ante el expansionismo japones en Manchuria y el norte, los comunistas reclaman el cese de la guerra civil para forjar un frente comun nacional.

column2: The glorious victory at Pingxingguan had shown the effectiveness of guerilla-like tactics. The decision was that the Red Army would work its way behind the Japanese lines and attempt to undermine the efforts in Hebei and Shandong provinces. Once that was done, Communist forces would try to occupy these provinces and wrest control free from the Nationalists. However, the Nationalists were already keeping a close eye on the Communists and effectively blockading the Communists from the west and the south, making their situation dangerous and risky.
column5: Tras la victoria de Pingxingguan, el 8.º Ejercito de Ruta y el Nuevo 4.º Ejercito priorizan la guerra de guerrillas tras las lineas de ocupacion niponas en Hebei y Shandong. Aunque integrados nominalmente en el Segundo Frente Unido, los comunistas deben eludir tanto las operaciones de castigo del ejercito imperial como los cordones de contencion politica impuestos por Nankin.

column2: The United States saw the Chinese theater as a means to tie up a large number of Japanese troops, as well as being a location for American airbases from which to strike the Japanese home islands. In 1944, as the Japanese position in the Pacific was deteriorating fast, the IJA mobilized over 400,000 men and launched their largest offensive in World War II to attack the American airbases in China and link up the railway between Manchuria and Vietnam. This brought major cities in Hunan, Henan and Guangxi under Japanese occupation. The failure of the Chinese forces to defend these areas encouraged Stilwell to attempt to gain command of the entire Chinese army, and his subsequent showdown with Chiang led to his replacement by Major General Albert Coady Wedemeyer.
column5: La vasta ofensiva japonesa Ichi-Go expuso las graves carencias defensivas del Kuomintang en el sur de China. Entre tanto, las fuerzas comunistas de Mao Zedong han expandido sus zonas liberadas y su red de milicias en el campo septentrional, preparandose para la futura disputa politica y territorial por el control de la nacion una vez concluya la contienda mundial.

column2: The dropping of the atomic bomb and the Soviet entry into the Pacific War caused Japan to surrender much more quickly than anyone in China had imagined. Now the Soviets have attacked the Western Allies. Can Soviet aid be used to bring about the War of Liberation? Can the People's Liberation Army defeat the much larger Nationalist force?
column5: La rapida rendicion del Imperio japones tras la intervencion sovietica en Manchuria precipita la lucha por el control de los arsenales y ciudades clave. Ante el nuevo escenario de fractura belica entre la URSS y las potencias occidentales, el Ejercito Popular de Liberacion se dispone a librar la guerra civil definitiva contra las divisiones nacionalistas del Kuomintang.

column2: Mao Zedong and the Communists had just come from one of the most difficult, and yet the most legendary period in the history of the Communist Party. Fighting through miles of mountains, forests, fighting through valleys and across bridges, all under enemy fire, the brave troops of the Red Army finally settled in the Yan'an Soviet, south of Mongolia, which was in the Soviet sphere of influence. However, as much as this Long March united the troops and cadres of the party, it also divided it. Mao Zedong and Zhang Guotao did not see things eye to eye, and Zhang took a large part of the army through the wilderness of the Xibei San Ma deserts to almost certain annihilation. In the beginning of 1936, the Communists were struggling to get reorganized, even when the Nationalist armies under Chiang Kai-shek attacked them from every direction, wishing to pound the Communists into a fine dust.
column5: Asentados en Yan'an tras la Larga Marcha, los cuadros comunistas de Mao Zedong y Zhu De reorganizan a los cuadros supervivientes en el norte de Shaanxi. Enfrentados a divisiones nacionalistas que buscan su aniquilacion y superadas las disensiones internas con Zhang Guotao, el Partido Comunista propone un pacto patriotico conjunto para combatir la inminente invasion japonesa.

column2: In the 1930s, The Republic of China was stronger, yet weaker, than the ill Qing Dynasty it replaced in 1911. Numerous revolutionary groups were unified by Sun Zhongshan and a new revitalized government set out to modernize a country left behind by the west. Unfortunately, the Republic of China disintegrated into countless warlord groups after Sun's death. Failed attempts were made to restore the monarchy while a newly created one by Yuan Shikai lasted only a few days. In addition, continued Japanese occupation of Chinese territory remained uncontested with little chance of foreign support despite China's participation in the Entente during the Great War. On the verge of anarchy, the Mukden Incident greatly reduced the tensions between the numerous cliques convincing most to nominally submit under the banner of Generalissimo Jiang Jieshi. Still, many problems remain as the new Nationalist Government under Jiang Jieshi attempts to eradicate the Chinese Communist Party while appeasing Japanese desires for expansion in a bid to buy time and develop the industrial capacity for full scale war. Will the 'Nanjing decade' of development continue long enough for China to sort out its internal and external problems, or will she remain a country unified only on paper?
column5: Bajo el gobierno nacionalista del generalisimo Chiang Kai-shek durante la decada de Nankin, la Republica de China intenta consolidar el estado central, modernizar la economia y someter a los caudillos militares regionales. La perdida de Manchuria en 1931 obliga al Kuomintang a contemporizar con Tokio para ganar tiempo y priorizar la eliminacion armada de los comunistas.

column2: The United States saw the Chinese theater as a means to tie up a large number of Japanese troops, as well as being a location for American airbases from which to strike the Japanese home islands. In 1944, as the Japanese position in the Pacific was deteriorating fast, the IJA mobilized over 400,000 men and launched their largest offensive in World War II to attack the American airbases in China and link up the railway between Manchuria and Vietnam. This brought major cities in Hunan, Henan and Guangxi under Japanese occupation. The failure of the Chinese forces to defend these areas encouraged Stilwell to attempt to gain command of the entire Chinese army, and his subsequent showdown with Chiang led to his replacement by Major General Albert Coady Wedemeyer.
column5: En 1944 el ejercito imperial japones lanzo la operacion Ichi-Go con 400.000 soldados para neutralizar las bases aereas aliadas y conectar las lineas ferreas hacia Indochina. Las severas derrotas en Henan, Hunan y Guangxi deterioraron la relacion entre Chiang Kai-shek y el general estadounidense Joseph Stilwell, relevado por Wedemeyer en un frente gravemente desgastado.

column2: The dropping of the atomic bomb and the Soviet entry into the Pacific War caused Japan to surrender much more quickly than anyone in China had imagined. Now the Soviets have attacked the Western Allies, raising fears that the Soviets will bring the Chinese communists into their fold. Will the truce between the Nationalist and Communists hold? What are the Soviet intentions in Asia?
column5: La precipitada derrota del Imperio japones en el Pacifico y la ocupacion sovietica de Manchuria colocan al gobierno nacionalista de Chiang Kai-shek ante una crisis inminente. Con el estallido de choques armados entre las grandes potencias, el Kuomintang debe movilizar su ejercito para desarmar guarniciones y frenar la expansion territorial del comunismo en Asia.

column2: The early 1930's were both good times and bad times for Nationalist China. On the one hand, the Guomindang regime under Chiang Kai-Shek was at the peak of it's power, having driven Mao Tse-tung's Communists on their grueling 6,000 mile march to Shaanxi and established themselves as the most powerful force in Chinese politics. It seemed that China was at last united under a stable, modernizing regime, ready to bring the country into the 20th century after years of humiliation at the hands of stronger countries. However, it faced a severe challenge: an increasingly belligerent and imperialist Japan desiring to expand it's resource base at China's expense. Having already conceded control of Manchuria to the Japanese in 1931, China seems destined for further clashes with the island nation, yet in early 1936 Chiang shows no signs of letting up in his civil war against the Communists. The question China must now face is a sore one: when and if Japan continues her expansion, will the Nationalists fight, or will China be humiliated yet again?
column5: Hacia 1936, el regimen del Kuomintang de Chiang Kai-shek ejerce el control de las zonas industriales costeras tras acosar a los comunistas hacia el interior. Pese al rearme y la cooperacion militar alemana, la ocupacion japonesa de Manchuria y el hostigamiento fronterizo situan al gobierno nacionalista ante la necesidad de poner fin a las querellas internas para resistir al invasor.

column2: After the Saltpetre War 1879 - 1883 in which Chile received the Peruvian saltpetre provinces Tarapacá and Arica in addition to the Bolivian coastal region of Antofagasta the country had command over vast copper deposits and monopolized the world trade in saltpetre
column5: Tras su victoria en la Guerra del Pacifico (1879-1883), Chile anexiono el litoral boliviano de Antofagasta y las provincias peruanas de Tarapaca y Arica. Los inmensos depositos de salitre y cobre impulsaron una era de prosperidad minera, comercio exterior y desarrollo naval en el cono sur.

column2: After the Saltpeter War 1879 - 1883 in which Chile received the Peruvian saltpeter provinces Tarapacá and Arica in addition to the Bolivian coastal region of Antofagasta the country had command over vast copper deposits and monopolized the world trade in saltpeter. A phase of economic prosperity was initiated, supported by the high demand for saltpeter at the beginning of World War One. However, the chemical processes devised during that war to artificially produce saltpeter rendered Chile's deposits worthless. Worsening economic circumstances, together with the growth of the population increased social crisis. Workers and unions gained political influence. President Arturo Alessandri y Palma (1920 -1925, 1932 - 1938) tried to overcome the social tensions. A new constitution expanded the president's powers at the cost of the congress' authority. After the military dictatorship of Carlos Ibanez del Campo (1927 -1931) fell under the pressure of the Great Depression the country slowly recovered from the recession.
column5: El auge del salitre chileno colapso con el desarrollo del sustituto sintetico y la Gran Depresion de 1929. Superada la convulsion politica y el regimen militar de Ibanez del Campo, el presidente Arturo Alessandri reestablecio el orden constitucional en 1932, apoyandose en la mineria del cobre y procurando canalizar las demandas de los crecientes movimientos obreros.

column2: Weakened by civil wars (especially 1899 - 1903), Colombia had to acknowledge U.S. rights of control over the Panama Canal in the Hay-Bunan-Varilla Treaty of 1903, ending the conflict between the two countries about the building of the Canal. Since 1850 Colombia had been exporting tobacco, after 1900 coffee and bananas were added to this list (with the aid of U.S. capital), and after 1905, petroleum.
column5: Debilitada por la Guerra de los Mil Dias, Colombia enfrento la separacion de Panama en 1903 facilitada por los Estados Unidos para construir el canal interoceanico. Apoyada en la exportacion creciente de cafe, platano y petroleo con inversiones foraneas, la administracion conservadora consolido una epoca de paz interna y modernizacion en transportes.

column2: Weakened by civil wars (especially 1899 - 1903), Colombia had to acknowledge U.S. rights of control of the Panama Canal in the Hay-Bunan-Varilla Treaty of 1903, ending the conflict between the two countries about the building of the Canal. When the Colombian Congress denied to ratify the treaty the United States forced the secession of Panama from Colombia, compensating them between 1921 and 1930 with a payment of a total 25 million Dollars. Colombia formally recognized Panama in 1921. The conservatives pursued the modernization of the country, expanding the railrod network. Since 1850 Colombia had been exporting tobacco, after 1900 coffee and bananas were added (with the aid of U.S. capital), after 1905 petroleum. The Great Depression brought the liberals into government in 1930 who enacted a land reform, dispossessing big landowners, and social reforms, easing the consequences of the economic crisis for the middle class, the workers' class and the peasants.
column5: Tras acordar indemnizaciones con Washington por Panama, Colombia encaro la decada de 1930 bajo la Hegemonia Liberal de Enrique Olaya Herrera y Alfonso Lopez Pumarejo. Las reformas constitucionales y agrarias de la Revolucion en Marcha buscaron redistribuir tierras y calmar el malestar campesino, mientras el pais afirmaba sus fronteras amazonicas en el conflicto con Peru.

column2: Costa Rica differed in several ways from other countries in Central America. Because of the largely white population there were no racial conflicts. Farming was dominated by family businesses owned by a broad middle class offering little fuel for a clash of social interests. Politically, however, influential and rivalling families called the tune and even resorted to military action to achieve their goals. Sugar and coffee were important export goods, but bananas were the most important one for which a tight railroad was built, improving the economical growth of Costa Rica. The bananas production came slowly under complete control of U.S. businesses (among others United Fruit). Parallel to this, Costa Rica has witnessed a calm democratic development with presidents elected in constitutional elections.
column5: A diferencia de sus vecinos centroamericanos, Costa Rica mantuvo un marco social estable fundamentado en la pequena propiedad agraria y el cultivo de cafe. La construccion ferroviaria hacia el Caribe propicio el auge de las plantaciones bananeras controladas por la United Fruit Company, coexistiendo un sistema de alternancia politica con la influencia de las elites exportadoras.

column2: Costa Rica differed in several ways from other countries in Middle America. Because of the largely white population there were no racial conflicts. Farming was dominated by family businesses owned by a broad middle class offering little fuel for a clash of social interests. Politically, however, influencial and rivaling families called the tune and even resorted to military action to achieve their goals. Sugar and coffee were important export goods, but bananas were the most important one for which a tight railroad was built, improving the economical growth of Costa Rica. The bananas production came slowly under complete control of U.S. businesses (among others United Fruit). Parallel to this, Costa Rica witnessed a calm democratic development with presidents elected in constitutional elections. This period was only interrupted by the short dictatorship of Frederico Tinoco Granodos (1917 - 1919).
column5: Conocida por su estabilidad institucional tras superar la breve dictadura de Tinoco en 1919, Costa Rica sostiene su economia en las exportaciones de cafe y banano bajo fuerte presencia del capital norteamericano. En 1936 el presidente electo Leon Cortes Castro lidera un pais democratico que preserva su neutralidad y carece de tensiones militares en sus fronteras.

column2: Following the attack of the Axis powers of the Kingdom of Yugoslavia in 1941, and the quick defeat of the Yugoslav army, the whole country was occupied by the Axis forces. Hitler and Mussolini installed the Croatian Ustasja extremist movement into power, forming the Independent State of Croatia.
column5: Tras la invasion alemana e italiana de Yugoslavia en abril de 1941, las potencias del Eje desmembraron el reino y crearon el Estado Independiente de Croacia bajo el mando fascista de Ante Pavelic y los ustachas. El regimen totalitario actuo como estado titere del Eje, librando una implacable lucha contrainsurgente contra los partisanos comunistas y chetniks.

column2: The war in Northern China has gone particularly poorly. Japanese forces had taken all of Shanxi-owned territory within a year of declaring war, and Yan Shanxi's forces folded like origami paper. The poor performance of the troops illicited the Generalissimo's reprimand. But was Chiang effectively sacrificing the warlords to the Japanese in order to give himself a better position after the war?
column5: La campana defensiva en el norte de China resulto devastadora para la camarilla de Yan Xishan, cuyas divisiones perdieron la mayoria de los centros urbanos de Shanxi frente al avance japones en 1937 y 1938. Atrincherado en las zonas montanosas meridionales, el senor de la guerra maniobra con desconfianza ante las directivas y presiones de Chiang Kai-shek.

column2: Yan Shanxi and the other warlords in Hebei-Chahar-Suiyuan who were settled in Northern China were in a precarious position in early 1936. To the south was the powerful Generalissimo Chiang Kai-shek, who wanted a united, Nationalist China under his rule. The ominous threat of the Japanese warmongers also loomed to the north. To compound matters, the Communists to the west were preparing to raid Shanxi for men and war materiel soon. Yan Shanxi needed to use his skills and talents as a deceptive and manipulative diplomat, or face utter and complete destruction at the hands of three foes.
column5: En 1936, el senor de la guerra Yan Xishan gobierna de forma autonoma la provincia minera y fortificada de Shanxi. Acosado por las tropas japonesas en el norte, la presion centralizadora del Kuomintang al sur y las incursiones guerrilleras del Ejercito Rojo comunista al oeste, Yan recurre a un pragmatismo calculado para salvaguardar su feudo y arsenal industrial.

column2: The explosion of the U.S. warship Maine in the port of Havana in 1898 gave the U.S.A. the opportunity to declare war on Spain, colonial masters of the Carribean island. In the Peace of Paris 1898 Spain had to cede Cuba, along with the Phillipines and Puerto Rico to the United States who in turn put the island under military administration. Formally, independence was declared in 1900, but the Platt-Amendment of 1901 restricted the autonomy again, giving the U.S. the naval bases of Bahia Honda and Guantanamo in addition to the right to intervene in the case of internal unrest. In 1902 the United States withdrew from the island, leaving the government of the first Cuban president, Tomás Estrada Palma in charge. However, already in 1906 - 1909 the U.S. intervened on the grounds of the Platt-Amendment when the liberals campaigned against President Estrada Palma. A further intervention took place in 1912.
column5: Tras la guerra hispano-estadounidense de 1898, Cuba obtuvo su independencia tutelada bajo la Enmienda Platt de 1901, que facultaba a Washington a intervenir militarmente y retener la base de Guantanamo. Marcada por las ocupaciones norteamericanas de 1906 y 1912 ante rebeliones politicas, la republica caribena desarrolla su economia en torno al cultivo del azucar.

column2: The explosion of the U.S. warship Maine in the port of Havana in 1898 gave the U.S.A. the opportunity to declare war on Spain, colonial masters of the Carribean island. In the Peace of Paris 1898 Spain had to cede Cuba, along with the Phillipines and Puerto Rico to the United States who in turn put the island under military administration. Formally, independence was declared in 1900, but the Platt-Amendment of 1901 restricted the autonomy again, giving the U.S. the naval bases of Bahia Honda and Guantanamo in addition to the right to intervene in the case of internal unrest. In 1902 the United States withdrew from the island, leaving the government of the first Cuban president, Tomás Estrada Palma in charge. However, already in 1906 - 1909 the U.S. intervened on the grounds of the Platt-Amendment when the liberals campaigned against President Estrada Palma. Further interventions took place in 1912 and between 1917 and 1919. In 1922 the last American soldiers left the island. U.S. investment, especially in sugarcane plantations, brought Cuba a quick econoimic rise. Nevertheless, the country came into economic dependency of the U.S. and her imports of tobacco and sugar. The agricultural monoculture was prone to crisis which led to economic disaster during the Great Depression 1929/30. impovering large parts of the population. Dictatorial measures taken by President Gerardo Machaldo y Porales (1925 - 1933) were answered by a military coup. Former sergeant and private secretary of Machado, Fulgencio Batista y Zaldivar held the reigns in his position of leader of that revolution and supreme commander of the army. He pushed through the appointment of Carlos Mendieta Montefur as president and achieved the lifting of the Platt-Amendment in 1934. Through the army Batista controlled the government, becoming president in 1940, and installing a dictatorial regime.
column5: Dependiente del monocultivo azucarero y afectada por la Gran Depresion, Cuba vivio la caida del dictador Machado en 1933. Tras la Revolucion de los Sargentos, el coronel Fulgencio Batista asumio el arbitraje militar y politico de la nacion, logrando la derogacion de la Enmienda Platt en 1934 y tutelando a los sucesivos gabinetes presidenciales de La Habana.

column2: 1939 saw the fall of the might of Nationalist China against the Japanese forces. The Ma warlords threw in their lot with the Second Chinese United Front and provided what assistance they could. However, when Chiang demanded a sacrifice of the warlords' sovereignties, they met with much resistance. As the years of the wars passed, the warlord domains became more impatient with Chiang's policies and started to collude with each other come war's end.
column5: En 1939, los generales musulmanes del clan Ma aportan brigadas de caballeria a la resistencia del Segundo Frente Unido contra Japon. Pese a cooperar con las autoridades de Chongqing, los caudillos de Xibei San Ma recelan de las tentativas de Chiang Kai-shek por centralizar las provincias noroccidentales a costa de la autonomia regional tradicional.

column2: In 1936, Nationalist forces had reported that a Communist army had crossed over and invaded the warlord domain of the 'Northwestern domain of the Three Mas', or Xibei San Ma. The three northwestern provinces of Gansu, Qinghai and Ningxia were all ruled by the Ma family clan, who commanded well-trained cavalry armies. Alarmed at the treatment of Muslims to the west in Xinjiang (Sinkiang), and loyal to the Nationalists, the Ma warlords are eyeing the lands of Xinjiang through the sights of their rifles.
column5: Las provincias noroccidentales de Ningxia, Gansu y Qinghai se encuentran gobernadas por los caudillos musulmanes de la familia Ma. Al mando de cuerpos de caballeria bien instruidos, la camarilla de Xibei San Ma combate el avance de las columnas comunistas hacia el oeste mientras preserva una alianza defensiva con el Kuomintang de Chiang Kai-shek.

column2: While nominally under the authority of the central government in Beijing, the province of Yunnan, Sikang, Guizhou, and Sichuan were largely autonomous during the Warlord and early Republican eras. Although the faction's lands were seemingly small and only controlled a small semi-outdated army, what Yunnan had was diplomatic clout among the various Chinese factions. The nearby governor-general of Guizhou is a long time protege of Yunnan's political system, and the southern Guangxi Clique remains on good terms with Nationalist and Progressive party elements within Yunnan. Likewise, the governor-generals of Xinjiang and San Ma clique supported Yunnan's opposition to excessive central powers. Led by the governor-general Cai E, Yunnan historically found itself as the champion of the republic during Yuan Shikai's autocratic rule when other factions failed to lead. Can this small alliance of governor-generals manage to bring a nation away from the brink of collapse and into a new era of prosperity? Or will anarchy and despotism plague the nation for years to come?
column5: En el suroeste de China, Yunnan y las provincias adyacentes conservan un alto grado de autogobierno militar bajo el gobernador Cai E. Al mantener buenas relaciones con los mandos de Guizhou, Guangxi y Xinjiang, la camarilla de Yunnan emerge como defensora de los principios republicanos ante las tendencias autocraticas del gobierno central de Beijing.

column2: In 1939, Yunnan watched as the combined forces of the Chinese subcontinent resisted against the Japanese. Things were precarious no matter what the outcome of this struggle were. If the Japanese one, that would surely mean the subjugation of Yunnan under a Japanese thumb. However, if the Nationalists won, effectively the political sovereignty of Yunnan would no doubt come to be forfeited. While her eyes were on the front lines, her hands were busy forming plans and deals with other nations to assure that come war's end, Yunnan would be ready to face up to her adversary.
column5: En 1939, Yunnan se convierte en una arteria vital para la resistencia china gracias a la construccion de la carretera de Birmania. El gobernador Long Yun aporta divisiones al frente nacional, pero protege celosamente la autonomia politica y fiscal de la provincia ante las exigencias centralizadoras de Chiang Kai-shek.

column2: In 1936, the warlord province of Yunnan in China was fighting for its survival. The Long Marches of the Communists had ended, and the Nationalists had exploited this opportunity to put the south-western provinces under his iron grip. Yunnan needed to face Chiang or face destruction. However, it needed to exercise subtlety and discretion. It did not help matters that most of the major powers saw Chiang, the leader of Nationalist China, as the true and sole ruler of all of China. Yunnan sought to establish liasons and mutual agreements with the other warlords in opposition to Chiang, but above, her goal was to be left alone.
column5: La provincia de Yunnan, gobernada con mano firme por el general Long Yun, maniobra en 1936 para preservar su independencia regional. Tras el paso de las tropas comunistas en su retirada y el consiguiente despliegue nacionalista en el sur, Kunming utiliza sus ingresos aduaneros y reservas de opio para negociar con Nankin sin perder su autogobierno.

column2: During World War II, Czechoslovakia disappeared from the map of Europe. In London, however, Czechoslovak exiles organized a government-in-exile and negotiated to obtain international recognition for the government and a renunciation of the Munich Agreement and its consequences. As Germany collapsed, the liberation of Czechoslovakia fell to the Red Army. The popular enthusiasm evoked by the Soviet armies of liberation benefited the Communist Party of Czechoslovakia. Czechoslovaks, bitterly disappointed by the West at Munich, responded favorably to both the communists and to a Soviet alliance. Stalin established a communist state subservient to Moscow, heightening tensions with the Western Allies, in the summer of 1945. Now, Stalin has launched the liberation of Western Europe and the Red Army is striking from jumping off points in Czechoslovakia into occupied Germany. What fate awaits Czechoslovakia?
column5: Desmembrada por los acuerdos de Munich y la ocupacion nazi, Checoslovaquia fue restaurada en 1945 bajo el gobierno de coalicion de Edvard Benes en Praga tras la llegada del Ejercito Rojo. La decepcion con las potencias occidentales favorecio la creciente influencia comunista y una estrecha alineacion militar y geopolitica con la Union Sovietica.

column2: After the outbreak of World War One Czech philosopher Thomás Garrigue Masaryk (1850 - 1937) and his close confidant Eduard Benes (1884 - 1948) worked for an independent state. With representatives of Slovakian immigrants in the U.S. they signed the Pittsburgh Treaty in May 1918, agreeing on the union of Czechs and Slovaks in a state to be founded. 1918, shortly before the military defeat of Austria-Hungary and Germany independent Czechoslovakia was proclaimed in Prague. Masaryk was elected first president (1918 - 1935). However, the young country suffered from two shortcomings. For one, the relationship between Czechs and Slovaks who had lived for centuries under Hungarian rule proved to be difficult. The Slovak part of the country was mainly agriculturally oriented, and its citizens felt to be at a disadvantage against their Czech countrymen. For another, over three million Germans (Sudetendeutsche) lived in the new republic and only reluctantly acknowledged the Czech dominated state power. The government in Prague, however, despite proclaiming other intent, lacked tact and will of integration in their policies towards the minority. Despite those difficulties a working parliamentary system formed after 1920 with a broad array of political parties. Since 1926 members of the most important minorities (Germans, Hungarians) had representatives in the government. However, export-oriented as the areas with Sudeten Germans were, those regions were hardest hit by the Great Depression 1929/30 and more national tensions were the consequence. After Hitler's rise to power in Germany in 1933 the Sudeten German party SdP became more and more an instrument of Nazi expansionism and it would only be a matter of time till Adolf Hitler would face the young Czechoslovakian republic with territorial claims.
column5: Surgida en 1918 bajo el liderazgo de Masaryk y Benes, Checoslovaquia se erigio en una prospera democracia industrial. No obstante, en 1936 encara graves tensiones internas con la minoria de mas de tres millones de alemanes sudetes nucleados en el partido pronazi de Konrad Henlein. Respaldada por su potente industria militar y fortificaciones, Praga vigila con alarma el expansionismo de Berlin.

column2:
In the troubled times of the early thirties, the German Communist party grew stronger, even in the forces, to try to seize power in march 1933.
 
Helped and armed by the Soviet Union, the putschist seize power after violent combats against Reichwehr's elements stayed faithfull to the former government.
 
 Today, tension rises again as Europe is wondering whether Germany will be the new spearhead of the Bolchevik Revolution...
column5: En el convulso inicio de 1933, el Partido Comunista de Alemania tomo el poder en Berlin mediante un cruento alzamiento apoyado por cuadros militares y la Union Sovietica. Tras aplastar la resistencia de sectores leales de la Reichswehr, la naciente Republica Democratica Alemana se convierte en la punta de lanza de la revolucion bolchevique en Europa central.

column2: The Danish defeat in the 2nd German-Danish War of 1864 after which Denmark had to cede Schleswig-Holstein and Oldenburg to Prussia and Austria led to the country's withdrawal into neutrality and to a pressure for reforms within. Already since 1849 Denmark had been a constitutional monarchy. Liberals and Social Democrats began strengthening the parliament starting 1901. Economically, Denmark focused on expanding its agriculture, which became the most important part of their exports.
column5: Tras ceder los ducados de Schleswig y Holstein en la guerra de 1864, Dinamarca adopto una firme politica de neutralidad exterior y reformas internas. Su monarquia constitucional consolido un sistema parlamentario estable y una economia agraria altamente competitiva y orientada a la exportacion de alimentos hacia los mercados britanico y aleman.

column2: During the Second World War, Denmark was occupied by Germany. Forced by circumstances during the German 'peaceful occupation', King Christian X and the Danish government led by the Social Democrat Thorvald Stauning chose to collaborate with the occupying power. In this way, the government hoped to create the easiest conditions for the population. In 1943, Germany intensified its demands on the collaboration. From 1943, the increasing popular resistance to the Germans created the basis for an underground movement. Now, war rages across Europe yet again. Will the Allies be able to stop the Red Army, or will Denmark face the specter of occupation once again?
column5: Ocupada por el Tercer Reich en 1940 bajo una administracion tutelada que colapso en 1943 ante la resistencia popular, Dinamarca fue liberada en mayo de 1945. La repentina ruptura de hostilidades entre las potencias occidentales y la Union Sovietica coloca de nuevo a los estrechos daneses en una encrucijada naval y estrategica crucial para el control del Baltico.

column2: The Danish defeat in the 2nd German-Danish War of 1864 after which Denmark had to cede Schleswig-Holstein and Oldenburg to Prussia and Austria led to the country's withdrawal into neutrality and to a pressure for reforms within. Already since 1849 Denmark had been a constitutional monarchy. Liberals and Social Democrats begun strengthening the parliament starting 1901. Economically, Denmark focused on expanding its agriculture which became the most important part of their exports. During World War 1 (1914 - 1918) the country remained neutral and continued the democratization process, introducing a democratic constitution in 1915.The primarily Social Democratic governments after The Great War layed the foundations for a welfare state that was patterned after the example of Sweden and up till today secures the population one of the highest standards of living in the world. The foreign politics of Denmark marked several successes. In 1920 Northern Slesvig was re-integrated into the country after a referendum had been held by rule of the Versailles Peace Treaty. In 1933 the International Court in Den Haag decided a case between Norway and Denmark over the owbership of Greenland in favor of the Danish. However, the Germans had keen eyes on the country as it is strategically important in both controlling access to the Baltic Sea and the shipping of ore from Scandinavia.
column5: Neutral en la Gran Guerra y con Schleswig Septentrional reintegrado en 1920, Dinamarca ha consolidado en 1936 un avanzado estado de bienestar agrario e industrial bajo gabinetes socialdemocratas. Pese a carecer de ambiciones belicas, su posicion geografica en los accesos al mar Baltico la convierte en un objetivo estrategico ante cualquier rearme de las potencias vecinas.

column2: In 1844 the Eastern part of the island of Hispaniola, since 1822 a part of the young country Haiti, declared its independence as Dominican Republic. Instability and foreign threats marked the early years of the new state. Restorative tendencies found the support of the oligarchy who, in the face of a border dispute with Haiti, put the country back under Spanish colonial rule in 1861 until revolts forced independence again in 1865. Economically and politically the Dominican Republic became more and more dependant on the U.S.A. who first openly intervened in 1905 to collect debts.
column5: Independizada en 1844 y brevemente anexionada a Espana entre 1861 y 1865, la Republica Dominicana sufrio decadas de inestabilidad fiscal y guerras intestinas. A partir del protocolo aduanero de 1905, los Estados Unidos asumieron el control de las finanzas y rentas del pais caribeno para garantizar el cobro de la deuda externa frente a acreedores foraneos.

column2: In 1844 the Eastern part of the island of Hispaniola, since 1822 a part of the young country Haiti, declared its independence as Dominican Republic. Instability and foreign threats marked the early years of the new state. Restorative tendencies found the support of the oligarchy who, in the face of a border dispute with Haiti, put the country back under Spanish colonial rule in 1861 until revolts forced independence again in 1865. Economically and politcally the Dominican Republic became more and more dependant on the U.S.A. who first openly intervened in 1905 to collect debts. Between 1916 and 1924 they occupied the country in order to get control over the financial and military institutions, beginning a democratization of the state. The miltary coup of General Rafael Léonidas Trujillo y Molina in 1930 abolished the 1924 constitution again. He went a forceful way to modernize and centralize the country, not looking at the social havoc this caused.
column5: Tras la ocupacion militar estadounidense de 1916 a 1924 que modernizo las fuerzas policiales, el general Rafael Leonidas Trujillo tomo el poder en 1930 mediante un golpe militar. En 1936, Trujillo gobierna la Republica Dominicana como un feudo personal dictatorial, centralizando las rentas nacionales y reprimiendo implacablemente a cualquier faccion opositora.

column2: Ecuador suffered a bumpy development after her independence in 1809. Border uncertainties led to conflicts with Peru and Colombia while the rivalling oligarchies of the conservative big landowners in the high lands and the liberal populace on the coast fought each other bitterly. A first era of relative peace was achieved under the dictatorship of the church friendly conservative President Gabriel Garcia Moreno who expanded central administration, the educational system, and the infrastructure. In 1875 Moreno was assassinated, which brought about a time of domestic turmoil once more till the liberals under General Eloy Alfaro prevailed. He forced the expansion of the traffic network and restricted church influence.
column5: Tras su independencia en 1809, Ecuador experimento un convulso desarrollo marcado por litigios fronterizos con Peru y Colombia, asi como por la pugna entre los terratenientes conservadores de la sierra y las clases liberales de la costa. El presidente Gabriel Garcia Moreno logro cierta estabilidad centralizando la administracion e infraestructura, pero su asesinato en 1875 reanudo el conflicto interno hasta el triunfo de la Revolucion Liberal de Eloy Alfaro, quien impulso el ferrocarril y la secularizacion del Estado.

He forced the expansion of the traffic network and restricted church influence. The good economic development, focusing on the increased growing of cocoa and coffee ended with the Great Depression 1929/30, destabilizing Ecuador's domestic situation again. A border conflict with Colombia was settled in 1931.
column5: Tras decadas de pugna entre conservadores serranos y liberales costenos, Ecuador vivio un auge economico basado en la exportacion de cacao y cafe que colapso con la Gran Depresion de 1929. Pese a resolver sus disputas territoriales con Colombia en 1931, el pais afronta una aguda inestabilidad politica interna y mantiene latente el litigio fronterizo con el Peru por la cuenca amazonica.

column2: In 1805, Muhammad Ali led the Egyptian army to rebellion against the Ottoman viceroy, asserting himself as the virtually independent ruler of Egypt. Muhammad Ali consolidated his power by breaking Mameluke power and smashing the 'ulama' – Egypt's Islamic notables. Egyptian control was extended further down the Nile – Khartoum was founded in 1823, and the Egyptian military was instrumental in defeating the Wahhabi sect in Central Arabia. The importance of Egypt strategically did not go unnoticed by the world's two great imperial powers – Great Britain and France. Both jostled for influence in Egypt throughout the mid nineteenth century, with the French helping to modernise the Egyptian Army, building canals – including the Suez canal under the direction of Ferdinand de Lesseps, and directing city planning on Parisian lines. On the other hand, the British introduced modern finance management and industry. Khedive Ismael, who reigned from 1863-1879 extended the modernisation programme, increased public spending lavishly whilst taking huge loans from British and French banks. Meanwhile, the Suez Canal was completed in 1869, but with Egypt's financial difficulties, Khedive Ismael was compelled to sell his 44 percent stake to Disraeli's British government in 1875. Having driven Egypt to bankruptcy while blaming it on his European ministers, Ismael was deposed in 1879 with European influence, and was replaced by Tewfik. Seen as a puppet by nationalist Egyptian army officers, Tewfik struggled to gain the confidence of his people, and in 1882, Arabi Pasha led an uprising against the Khedive's rule. Fearing that British and French finances and the Suez Canal were be at risk, the two respective governments conspired to act – the French found themselves unable, forcing Prime Minister Gladstone to act unilaterally, sending a naval squadron to bombard Alexandria and Major-General Wolseley to occupy the country, which he did after winning the Battle of Tel el Kebir. British control of Egypt tightened under the 'veiled protectorate' run by Sir Evelyn Baring, the Earl of Cromer who continued to modernise the country while moderating Egypt's financial situation. In 1883 the Mahdi rebelled against Egyptian rule in the Sudan, capturing Khartoum in 1885 and killing British officer Major-General Charles Gordon. The Mahdists continued to rule the Sudan until the Nile campaign of 1896-1898, in which Major-General Kitchener led his Anglo-Egyptian force to avenge Gordon by taking victory at Omdurman, just outside Khartoum. The subsequent crisis at Fashoda saw French influence in Egypt marginalised, allowing Cromer to make Britain the undisputed overlords of Egypt. Problematically, Khedive Abbas II (reigned from 1892) continued in his attempts to break Britain's control throughout the 1900s, yet the new British Agent-General, Lord Kitchener held him in check. By 1914, the Egyptian question remained fundamentally unresolved – many in Britain would like to see British rule in Egypt ended, with Britain simply in control of the canal. Yet many would fear that a British withdrawal would lead to the power vacuum being filled by forces hostile to the British Empire. Alternatively, putting Egypt under official British protection is seen by some as the only viable way forward.
column5: Iniciado como estado autonomo bajo Mehmet Ali en 1805, Egipto cayo bajo un protectorado britanico de facto tras la crisis de deuda del canal de Suez y la intervencion armada de 1882 en Tel el-Kebir. Pese a permanecer formalmente bajo soberania otomana, Londres ejerce el control estrategico del canal y de la administracion civil y militar a traves de su consul general, manteniendo vigilado al jedive Abbas II ante la inminente conflagracion mundial.

column2: The region now known as Egypt had been part of the gigantic Ottoman Empire until World War I. The Ottoman Empire was part of the losing side of the conflict, and after the struggle, what was left of their decaying empire was divided amongst various Allied countries. Egypt became a part of the gigantic British Empire. From 1922 onwards, Egypt enjoyed a form of autonomy within the Commonwealth, however, the decisions that mattered were still made in London, and Egypt's 'sovereignty' was in reality a very weak puppet status. Things would change radically at the end of the second World War. Egypt finally achieved a form of independence that was more than being a puppet of London. Egypt gained its de facto independence in 1946, even though formally it was still part of the British Empire. The first of these newly-empowered Egyptian governments were very weak, though, and governed over a divided country that was continually on the brink of civil war. A dramatic change of direction occurred in 1952, when a popular military coup ousted the hereditary Egyptian King Faruq I. In 1953, General Muhammad Naguib established the Republic of Egypt, an event that would change the Middle East forever. But that's another story.
column5: Declarado protectorado formal britanico en 1914 y reino nominalmente independiente desde 1922, Egipto afronta 1936 bajo una soberania condicionada por el Tratado anglo-egipcio. Aunque el joven rey Faruq asume la corona, Gran Bretana mantiene bases militares, el control de las instalaciones del canal de Suez y el condominio sobre el Sudan, en medio del creciente descontento nacionalista del partido Wafd.

column2: At the turn of the century, all appeared well for the British Empire - covering two-fifths of the world's land surface, accounting for a quarter of the world's population, policed by the most professional army in the world and guarded by the mightiest fleet ever built, the British could be confident ruling the empire 'on which the sun never set'. But beneath the assurances of imperial grandeur lay insecurity about the future: economically and industrially, the United States was outperforming the British. The 'Great Game' in Central Asia with the Russians seemed unceasing, and the Germans had commenced an ominous fleet building programme to challenge the Royal Navy's dominance of the seas. Amidst such anxiety, the British assured its status in the East by signing an alliance with Japan in 1902, before settling imperial differences with France in 1904 with the Entente Cordiale. 1906 saw Britain commission the mighty HMS Dreadnought, the world's first all big-gun battleship, a comprehensive response to Germany's naval challenge. The resulting Dreadnought race polarised Great Britain and Germany, and served to push Britain towards even closer relations with France, and by 1908, to an entente with Russia. On the continent, diplomats averted crisis after crisis. Europe had nearly been plunged into war three times: over Bosnia in 1908, Agadir in 1911 and the Balkans in 1912-3. By 1914, British attention was turned to strife in Ulster, where the controversy over Home Rule had pitted militant Unionists against their Irish nationalist adversaries, and brought them to the precipice of civil war.  Recent British continental policy had assumed the twin characteristics of neutral mediation and wariness for the balance of power.  The Foreign Secretary, Sir Edward Grey is eager to uphold the continuities of British policy as dictated by her interest - no state must become hegemonic on the continent and the channel ports must remain in friendly hands at all costs.
column5: Al frente del mayor imperio colonial del mundo y custodiada por la Royal Navy, Gran Bretana encaro el inicio de siglo sorteando el ascenso industrial aleman y estadounidense. La carrera armamentistica naval iniciada con el HMS Dreadnought acerco a Londres a Francia y Rusia mediante la Triple Entente. En 1914, mientras el Foreign Office intenta preservar el equilibrio de poder continental y la neutralidad belga, las tensiones por el autogobierno en Irlanda amenazan la estabilidad interna.

column2: While a victor in the Great War, the British Empire declined in strength in the years after. A trio of major Irish Independence achievements occurred, once in 1916, another in 1918, and once again in 1921. Britain finally acknowledge losing the Irish Isles in 1927, changing her name to the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland. Similar nationalistic movements arose throughout the empire, as Egypt gained independence in 1922 and Iraq in 1932. A short-lived postwar boom in 1919 led to a depression felt worldwide exasperated by the American economic collapse and circular debt. The decade of the twenties would be known as the lost decade as economic hardships strained the empire. Britain managed to stabilize itself and avoid a communist revolution by reducing its military spending and enacting many compromises under Stanley Baldwin's administration. Now, no longer the industrial power it once was, Britain desperately seeks a way to maintain peace through the League of Nations only to be disappointed time and time again.
column5: Vencedora exhausta de la Gran Guerra, Gran Bretana vio mermado su poder global tras la secesion del Estado Libre Irlandes y la concesion de autonomias en el Imperio. Golpeada por la Gran Depresion y las deudas contraidas, la coalicion nacional de Ramsay MacDonald y Stanley Baldwin redujo drasticamente el gasto de defensa. En 1933, Londres fia su seguridad al arbitraje de la Sociedad de Naciones mientras observa con recelo el auge de los totalitarismos europeos.

column2: The British Empire emerged from the 1914-1918 Great War larger than ever before, but the comfortable political and economic assurances of the Victorian era were gone for good. While Britain's relative industrial strength continued its slow decline, the Empire's security was threatened both internally by indigenous nationalist pressures, and externally by the resurgence of militant dictatorial powers like Italy, Germany, and Japan. At the same time, the Treasury's demands for austerity in the midst of worldwide economic turmoil meant cutting defense expenditure to the bone, with the overstretched imperial armed services consequently unable to provide satisfactory coverage east as well as west of Suez. Diplomatically, the UK had staked much on the arbitration powers of the League of Nations, but the League's ineffectiveness in Manchuria in 1931 augured ill for its future authority, and Germany's aggressive takeovers of Austria and Bohemia ended any lingering chance of a general European peace. The German attack on Poland has triggered a declaration of war from Britain and its ally France, but can they aid the Poles in time? And what of their own, far from completed defenses in the West?
column5: Tras fracasar la politica de apaciguamiento de Neville Chamberlain con la invasion alemana de Polonia en septiembre de 1939, Gran Bretana declara la guerra a Alemania junto a Francia y los dominios de la Mancomunidad. Pese a movilizar a la Fuerza Expedicionaria y desplegar a la Royal Navy en tareas de bloqueo naval, el Imperio britanico encara la contienda con un rearme incompleto y vulnerabilidades defensivas globales.

column2: When the United Kingdom declared war on Germany in September 1939 its people expected the general course of events to go the same way as the Great War twenty years earlier. A small expeditionary force was sent to France, the Royal Navy took up its blockading position athwart Germany's sea lines of communication, and the country awaited the inevitable German assault against the West. However, the Western Front has seen little fighting since then. Poland fell in 6 October 1939, and ever since no major offensives by either side against the other were launched, as German attentions focused on the valuable iron-rich depots of Norway, which it invaded in the spring 1940. However, it is doubtful this unnatural calm will last for long. Germany has surely learned from her mistakes in the previous war. Now, May 1940, with the British Empire settled in the welcome leisure of this 'Phony War', German panzer forces are poised on the border of the Low Countries, ready to unleash a new blitzkrieg campaign of an unforeseen magnitude on an unprepared France.
column5: Tras meses de calma tensa durante la 'guerra de broma' y el reves de la campana de Noruega que forzo la dimision de Chamberlain en favor de Winston Churchill, el Imperio britanico afronta en mayo de 1940 la embestida acorazada alemana contra los Paises Bajos y Francia. La Fuerza Expedicionaria Britanica debera combatir en vanguardia para evitar el colapso del frente occidental.

column2: When the United Kingdom declared war on Germany in September 1939 its people expected the general course of events to go the same way as the Great War twenty years earlier. A small expeditionary force was sent to France, the Royal Navy took up its blockading position athwart Germany's sea lines of communication, and the country awaited the inevitable German assault against the West. Initially nothing happened. Indeed for over six months scarcely any fighting took place between the combatant powers and Britain settled into the welcome leisure of the 'Phony War'. Then in May 1940 Germany's surprise Blitzkrieg offensive against France and the Low Countries shattered this unnatural calm for good. British forces were rudely ejected from the European mainland, Italy joined the war, France fell, and the United Kingdom suddenly found itself alone and facing the possibility of imminent invasion. However a heroic air defense that summer forestalled Hitler's 'Operation Sealion' attack. The summer of 1941 finds Britain in a difficult situation. British forces are in peril in North Africa, the U-Boat packs are threatening the UK's vital supply links, and Churchhill's efforts to bring America into the Allies have only resulted in limited aid. Now with the Axis at war with the Soviet Union, will Germany's attention on the Eastern Front relieve the pressure on the Britain? An Allied 'Second Front' in Europe seems years away.
column5: Sola tras la caida de Francia y victoriosa en la batalla de Inglaterra, Gran Bretana sostiene la resistencia frente al Eje a mediados de 1941. Mientras la campana submarina alemana castiga los convoyes en el Atlantico y los combates arrecia en el norte de Africa, la invasion alemana de la Union Sovietica abre un segundo frente vital que alivia la amenaza directa sobre las islas britanicas.

column2: After facing utter defeat three years ago, Britain's proud armies have returned to the fields of France to regain the honour lost at Dunkirk. They are determined to strike the final blow to the Nazi juggernaut, making good for all the lives that were lost in defeat during the early years of the war. And so British soldiers are manning the front lines on both the Italian and French fronts, grimly collecting on debts owed by the Nazis. But victory, however assured it might seem, is far from in hand, for to the east the Russians are gathering momentum to crush the German armies and claim Central Europe in the name of communism. Under such circumstances a victory over Germany would be a bitter victory, if victory at all, for an ideologically driven man like Churchill.
column5: Cuatro anos despues de la evacuacion de Dunkerque, las fuerzas britanicas y de la Mancomunidad regresan al continente con el desembarco de Normandia y la campana de Italia. Bajo el liderazgo de Winston Churchill, Gran Bretana vuelca sus recursos para derrotar al Tercer Reich, al tiempo que maniobra diplomaticamente para salvaguardar el equilibrio europeo frente al avance sovietico en el este.

column2: Churchill had feared that after V.E. Day on May 8, 1945, the Soviets could move westwards and threaten Britain. However, despite plans for 'Operation Unthinkable', a preemptive attack on the Soviet Union was discarded. Churchill, and then after his electoral defeat, Attlee attempted to confront the delicate balance of power of the opposing governmental structures, democracy and communism at the Potsdam Conference (July 17 to August 2, 1945). However, despite the agreement on the partitioning of Germany and the call for an unconditional surrender of Japan, the conference did nothing to quell the increasing tensions between the Western Allies and the Soviets. The destruction of Hiroshima and Nagasaki sealed the fate of Japan, and the surrender documents were signed on the USS Missouri on September 2nd, 1945. The attack on the Western Allies by the Soviets on October 2nd had been foreshadowed by Churchill's fears and a series of border incidents. Now, the UK faces another terrible war. Will the rest of the Commonwealth once again stand by the UK? Will Churchill once again come to center stage? Will the Western Allies hold, or will Britain once again face an occupied Europe across the Channel?
column5: Concluida la guerra contra Alemania y Japon, el gobierno laborista de Clement Attlee encara una nacion exhausta y arruinada. El subito estallido de un conflicto militar a gran escala entre los Aliados occidentales y la Union Sovietica coloca a Gran Bretana nuevamente en pie de guerra para contener la marea comunista en Europa central y salvaguardar las rutas de su vasto imperio.

While still committed to its alliance with France and sensitive to the traditional balancing of power in continental Europe, Britain in 1936 is a nation with many roles but a dwindling resource base with which to accomplish them.
column5: En 1936, el Imperio britanico abarca vastos territorios globales pero arrastra una prolongada debilidad economica y militar tras los recortes de entreguerras. Amenazado por el rearme aleman, el expansionismo italiano en Africa y las ambiciones japonesas en Asia, el gobierno de Stanley Baldwin busca mantener el statu quo mediante compromisos diplomaticos y el inicio de un cauto programa de rearme.

column2: Occupied by German troops during the war, the Russian February Revolution 1917 released powers vying for independence in Estonia. A national council was established, declaring - with German support - independence in 1918. The upper class, friendly towards the Germans, at first attempted to make the country part of Germany, but they were overruled in favor of the republic in 1919. The Soviet Union recognized the young state officially in 1920. The big landowners, sympathetic as they were towards Germany, were dispossessed.
column5: Ocupada por tropas alemanas durante la Gran Guerra, la revolucion rusa de 1917 permitio al Consejo Nacional Maapaev proclamar la independencia de Estonia en febrero de 1918. Tras repeler tanto la invasion bolchevique como los embates de los cuerpos francos germano-balticos en la Guerra de Independencia, el Tratado de Tartu de 1920 consagro el reconocimiento sovietico de la republica soberana.

column2: Occupied by German troops during World War 1, the Russian February Revolution 1917 released powers vying for independence in Estonia. A national council was established, declaring - with German support - independence in 1918. The upper class, friendly towards the Germans, at first attempted to make the country part of Germany, but they were overruled in favor of the republic in 1919. The Soviet Union recognized the young state officially in 1920. The big landowners, sympathetic as they were towards Germany, were dispossessed. The republic's stability was proved in during the Bolshevik attempt at a coup d'etat in 1924. Only with the beginning of the Great Depression in 1929 the harmonious development was disrupted by the rise of the fascist 'Front Fighters League'. Prime Minister Konstantin Päts, in power a number of times, reacted to the threat from the political right with the initiation of a dictatorial rule in 1934. In the same year, the Baltic Entente was formed with Latvia and Lithuania.
column5: Consolidada su independencia tras la guerra contra los bolcheviques en 1920, Estonia experimento una decada de estabilidad hasta que la Gran Depresion alimento el ascenso del movimiento ultranacionalista Vaps. Para frustrar su llegada al poder, Konstantin Pats establecio un regimen autoritario en 1934 e impulso la Entente Baltica junto a Letonia y Lituania para asegurar su defensa regional.

column2: In 17th century the royal central power lost more and more of its influence so that Abyssinia broke into separate provinces in 18th century. Only in 1853 could Ras Kasa restore the country's unity with a strong central government again and climbed the throne in 1855 as Theodor II (till 1868). However, his attempt to reform state and church after the pattern of European countries failed. After 1885 Abyssinia was endangered by the Mahdi Uprising against the British-Egyptian rule in Sudan, but the Mahdi warriors were repelled. New danger arose around 1895 through Italy and her attempts to build a colonial empire on the Horn of Africa. With the victory of Emperor Menelik II over an Italian expeditionary corps near Adowa in 1896 Abyssinia was the only African country besides Liberia to keep its independence during the Age of Imperialism. Domestically, Menelik II attempted a reform of the state administration and founded the new capital of Addis Ababa.
column5: Tras superar la fragmentacion feudal y unificar el imperio en el siglo XIX, Etiopia salvaguardo su soberania aplastando al cuerpo expedicionario italiano en la batalla de Adua en 1896. Consolidada bajo Menelik II desde la nueva capital de Addis Abeba, el Imperio etiope permanece en 1914 como el unico estado soberano del Cuerno de Africa, rodeado por posesiones coloniales europeas.

column2: Ethiopia has won its revenge against the Fascist powers, but now its alliance has drawn it into a new war against an implacable enemy. How will Ethiopia fare in this new conflict?
column5: Restaurada la independencia del imperio etiope tras la derrota de las fuerzas de ocupacion italianas en 1941, Haile Selassie se enfrenta a la inmediata fractura belica entre sus aliados occidentales y el bloque sovietico. Addis Abeba debera defender su soberania y modernizar sus fuerzas en un Africa oriental en crisis.

column2: In 17th century the royal central power lost more and more of its influence so that Ethiopia broke into seperate provinces in 18th century. Only in 1853 could Ras Kasa restore the country's unity with a strong central government again and climbed the throne in 1855 as Theodor II (till 1868). However, his attempt to reform state and church after the pattern of European countries failed. After 1885 Ethiopia was endangered by the Mahdi Uprising against the British-Egyptian rule in Sudan, but the Mahdi warriors were repelled. New danger arose around 1895 through Italy and her attempts to build a colonial empire on the Horn of Africa. With the victory of Emperor Menelik II over an Italian expeditionary corps near Adua in 1896 Ethiopia was the only African country besides Liberia to keep its independence during the Age of Imperialism. Domestically, Menelik II attempted a reform of the state administration and founded the new capital of Addis Abeba.With the aid of Great Britain Ras Tafari Makonnen took the rule in 1916 and was proclaimed king in 1928. After the death of Empress Zauditu in 1930 he was crowned Emperor Haile Selassie I. In the following years he attempted to turn Ethiopia, since 1930 member of the Peoples' League, into a modern country. In 1935 Fascist Italy renewed her attempts of turning Ethiopia into her colony and invaded the country
column5: Unica nacion indigena en preservar su soberania en el reparto colonial tras la historica victoria de Adua en 1896, Etiopia acometio su modernizacion bajo el emperador Haile Selassie I. Sin embargo, en 1936 el imperio libra una guerra desesperada por su supervivencia frente a la invasion de la Italia fascista de Mussolini, que emplea blindados, aviacion y armas quimicas para conquistarla.

column2: In 1809 Russia occupied Finland, and Sweden ceded the land, ending 3 centuries of Swedish rule. Russian nationalists in the 19th century strove to transform the Russian Empire's autonomous regions on the fringe like Finland into provinces Russian in character. In order to achieve this in 1898 a Russian was appointed governor of Finland and in 1899 a manifesto was published claiming the right of the Tsarist government to rule without the consent of Finland's diet and senate. Another manifesto made Russian the main language in the country's administration. The Finnish population was divided into determined opponents, the Constitutionalists, and those who favoured compliance with the policy in order to further weaken the continuing Swedish grip on society: the Compliants. The radical measures of the Russian administration however made the compliants' position untenable. When the Russians introduced a new conscription law in 1901, the Finns were determined to resist. The Russians soon found out that Finnish soldiers were, for their cause, unreliable, and exempted Finns in return for the payment of extra levies. Meanwhile, there were Finnish organizations actively resisting Russian rule. Russian Governor Nicolai Bobrikov was assassinated by one of their members in 1904. The Russian loss in the Russo-Japanese War and the Revolution of 1905 gave the Finns some reprieve. Russian pressure to intensify Russification ceased
column5: Incorporada al Imperio ruso como gran ducado autonomo en 1809 tras siglos de dominio sueco, Finlandia resistio con firmeza las campanas de rusificacion iniciadas por el gobernador Bobrikov a finales de siglo. Pese a lograr la creacion del parlamento unicameral Eduskunta en 1906, las tensiones con las autoridades zaristas persisten al estallar la Gran Guerra en 1914.

column2: With the demise of the Russian Czar's powers Finland, having been under her Eastern neighbour's rule since 1808, was granted more autonomy. In 1906 a monocameral parliament was installed along with universal suffrage for men and women alike. The parliament, the first in Europe to have a Social Democratic majority since 1916, exploited Russia's weakness after the February Revolution of 1917 and declared Finland's independence in July of the same year. The declaration of the right of self-determination proclaimed by the new Soviet government during the October Revolution strengthened the Finnish claim for independence. On December 6th, 1917, the proclamation of sovereignty was reoeated and acknowledged by the Soviet rulers in late December. An attempt of Finnish Socialists to seize power in early 1918 caused a bloody civil war in which the White Guards, supported by the German Kaiser, prevailed over the Socialist's Red Guards. After the defeat a Communist Party seperated from the Social Democrats and was declared illegal in 1930 after numerous attempts of insurgence. In 1921 Finland reached its largest expansion when the League of Nations declared the Aland islands Finnish territory. In 1932 the country signed a non-aggression pact with the USSR. The secret protocol of the Ribbentrop-Molotov Pact from August 1939 declared Finland to be a sphere of interest of the Soviet Union.
column5: Independizada en 1917 y consolidada tras una cruenta guerra civil entre blancos y rojos, Finlandia erigio una estable republica democratica. No obstante, las clausulas secretas del Pacto Ribbentrop-Molotov de agosto de 1939 asignaron el pais a la esfera de influencia sovietica. Con la demanda de concesiones territoriales en el istmo de Carelia, la amenaza de una invasion por parte del Ejercito Rojo es inminente.
