The secret protocol of the Ribbentrop-Molotov Pact from August 1939 declared Finland to be a sphere of interest of the Soviet Union. In November 1939 Stalin launched the Winter War to secure territory for the erection of fortresses to secure Leningrad. Finland held out till 1940, letting the USSR appear as a weak military power before the world. In March 1940, however, Finland agreed to peace talks to avoid engagements of British and French against the Soviets on her soil. The Soviets received parts of Karelia and Eastern Finland, the shores of Lake Ladoga and Hanko. In Fall of 1940 German troops landed in Finland and in 1941 the country joined Nazi Germany in their war against the USSR, hoping to claim back their lost territories.
column5: Tras su tenaz resistencia en la Guerra de Invierno de 1939-1940, Finlandia tuvo que ceder Carelia y Hanko a la Union Sovietica por el Tratado de Moscu. Con el inicio de la Operacion Barbarroja en junio de 1941, las fuerzas armadas finlandesas al mando de Mannerheim se unen a la ofensiva del Eje en la Guerra de Continuacion para reconquistar los territorios arrebatados y asegurar sus fronteras.

column2: After the humiliating end of the Continuation War against the Soviet Union and the forced Lapland War against former ally Germany, Finland is in a precarious position between the East and West. Her large army is completely demobilized, the communist party is trying to climb to power and army officers are hiding arms and ammunition all over the countryside. Will Finland stay neutral while the rest of Europe is engulfed by nuclear fire? Or is this the time to finally exact revenge on the Soviet Union and get the lands of Karelia back?
column5: Concluida la Guerra de Continuacion y tras expulsar a las tropas alemanas en la Guerra de Laponia, Finlandia preservo su soberania a costa de dolorosas perdidas territoriales y el desarme parcial de sus fuerzas. Atrapada entre dos bloques militares enfrentados en 1945, Helsinki debe mantener un dificil equilibrio diplomatico para no ser aplastada por la vecina Union Sovietica.

column2: With the demise of the Russian Czar's powers Finland, having been under her Eastern neighbour's rule since 1808, was granted more autonomy. In 1906 a monocameral parliament was installed along with universal suffrage for men and women alike. The parliament, the first in Europe to have a Social Democratic majority since 1916, exploited Russia's weakness after the February Revolution of 1917 and declared Finland's independence in July of the same year. The declaration of the right of self-determination proclaimed by the new Soviet government during the October Revolution strengthened the Finnish claim for independence. On December 6th, 1917, the proclamation of sovereignty was reoeated and acknowledged by the Soviet rulers in late December. An attempt of Finnish Socialists to seize power in early 1918 caused a bloody civil war in which the White Guards, supported by the German Kaiser, prevailed over the Socialist's Red Guards. After the defeat a Communist Party seperated from the Social Democrats and was declared illegal in 1930 after numerous attempts of insurgence. In 1921 Finland reached its largest expansion when the League of Nations declared the Aland islands Finnish territory. In 1932 the country signed a non-aggression pact with the USSR.
column5: Soberana desde 1917 y vencedora en su guerra civil con auxilio aleman, Finlandia construyo una solida democracia parlamentaria neutral. En 1936, respaldada por un pacto de no agresion con Moscu firmado en 1932 y su politica de cooperacion con los paises nordicos, Helsinki prioriza la defensa del istmo de Carelia y la modernizacion de su ejercito frente a cualquier expansionismo sovietico.

column2: Once the greatest Power of Europe, France is now a troubled country. Economically, she has been overtaken by many of her rivals. A declining birthrate seems to promise further decline, and in an age of mass armies might prove a fatal weakness. Politically, the Third Republic is unstable: a coup attempt in 1877 was narrowly averted, and the conservative-nationalist Boulangist movement of the 1880s also came close to seizing the state. The Dreyfus affair of 1894-1906 further laid bare the divisions within society, as monarchists, clericalists, anti-semites and conservative supporters of Army and State lined up against radicals, liberals, socialists, secularists and supporters of the Republic. On the international scene, the defeat by Prussia in 1871 and Germany's occupation of the provinces of Alsace and Lorraine is a festering sore, and demands for 'revanche' - revenge - against Germany remain strong. All is not hopeless, however. Paris, 'the City of Light', remains the fashionable, cultural and artistic capital of the world. French troops have redeemed their defeat in 1871 by establishing the world's second-largest colonial empire, and are now respected as one of the strongest, most aggressive and capable armies in Europe. Most importantly, France now has strong allies. Thanks to German diplomatic blunders and offers of French financial support, Russia was lured away from Germany's side and in 1894 signed a binding military agreement with France. Even more significant - and surprising - was the formation of the 'Entente Cordiale' in 1904 with Britain. For centuries France's traditional enemy, Britain was drawn to her side through fear of increasing German power. Although the exact terms of their commitment to France remain unclear, British friendship gives the French confidence that whatever the future might bring, they will weather the storm and emerge triumphant.
column5: Herida por la perdida de Alsacia y Lorena en 1871, la Tercera Republica Francesa forjo su doctrina exterior en torno al revanchismo contra Alemania y la construccion del segundo mayor imperio colonial del orbe. Pese a las divisiones politicas internas, Paris afianzo su seguridad mediante la alianza franco-rusa de 1894 y la Entente Cordiale con Gran Bretana en 1904, lista para librar una guerra total.

column2: After the great war, France was horrified by the devastation and sought to avoid another conflict with its neighbor Germany. Millions died in the war and much of the steel and coal producing areas of France remained in ruin. As a result, a large scale reconstruction project started funded primarily by German war reparations. In addition, work began on an 'impenetrable' Maginot Line trusted to defend France from another war and a 'paper wall' of treaties with Poland, Czechoslovakia, Romania, Yugoslavia, and Russia was established. When the stock market collapse hit, however, she was forced to abandon massive spending in favor of tax reform and a stable currency. The divided leftist groups, weakness of royalist conservatism groups, and success by centrist parties efforts to stave off a depression kept France under stable governance by the center-right pro-business Bloc national and the center-left pro-middle class Cartel des gauches. Although France avoided a crisis seen in the United States and Germany, hundreds of thousands still remained unemployed and much of the post-war growth was lost. A new revitalized socialist movement now rises led by Leon Blum challenging the status quo while ideologically opposed parties are poised to take over a vengeful Germany. Already betrayed by the futility and incompetence of the League of Nations, France remains cautious, hopeful for the future, yet prepared to defend herself once again.
column5: Devastada por el coste humano y material de la Gran Guerra, Francia oriento su doctrina militar a la defensiva con la linea Maginot y una red de alianzas en Europa oriental. Hacia 1933, mientras la Gran Depresion agrava la polarizacion interna entre el Cartel de Izquierdas y las ligas nacionalistas de derechas, Paris observa con alarma el colapso del orden de Versalles y el rearme de Alemania.

column2: When Germany invaded Poland in September 1939, France and Britain entered the war on the side of its Polish ally. However, the Polish cry for help fell in deaf ears, as the French found themselves unable or unwilling to invade German territory. As a result, Poland fell on October 1939, and a new order in Central Europe was established. However, the expected German invasion of France in 1939 didn't come. Indeed, for seven months the West has seen scarcely any fighting. As the Western Powers settled in the welcome leisure of the 'Phony War', German attentions focused elsewhere. After the Altmark incident, Norway's neutrality was compromised, which Germany regarded as a threat to herself. As such, in April 1940, German forces invaded the iron-rich areas of Norway, vital for her war effort, to prevent them from falling in British hands. Now, May 1940, German panzers are poised on the Belgian border, ready to strike at an unready France. Will France resist the German invasion like it did 1914? Or will it the pressure of both foreign and internal turmoil prove too much for the French Republic?
column5: Tras permanecer atrincherado tras la linea Maginot durante los siete meses de inaccion de la 'drole de guerre', el ejercito frances se enfrenta en mayo de 1940 a la embestida alemana a traves de las Ardenas y los Paises Bajos. La doctrina estatica y las fallas de coordinacion aliada ponen a prueba la supervivencia misma de la Tercera Republica frente a la blitzkrieg.

column2: France's manpower losses in the First World War were proportionally larger than those of any other major belligerent, and this demographic catastrophe was reflected in the shortfall of annual army conscripts (the so-called 'hollow classes') of the interwar period. With a revived Germany, a self-aggrandizing Italy, and an increasingly unstable Spain on its borders, France could not afford to accept this military weakness without abandoning its pretensions to Great Power status. To compensate, the nation threw itself into a massive fortified works project on the Franco-German frontier during the early 1930s, and tried to build new diplomatic arrangements with the 'little entente' powers of central and eastern Europe. This had mixed results. France's immediate security problems were partially resolved by its mighty Maginot Line (but what of the unprotected Belgian border?), but the West's failure to support Czechoslovakia in its hour of crisis proved fatal for any hopes of peace. The deeply divided Third Republic now finds itself at war with Germany once again, and whether it can still weather a serious military challenge as it did in 1914 remains to be seen.
column5: Lastrada por las masivas bajas de 1914-1918 y el deficit demografico de conscriptos, Francia confio su defensa a la linea Maginot y al pacto con Gran Bretana. El colapso del sistema de seguridad colectiva tras los acuerdos de Munich no pudo evitar la guerra tras la invasion nazi de Polonia en septiembre de 1939. Una Tercera Republica dividida debe movilizar sus divisiones para una nueva lucha de desgaste.

column2: In May of 1940 German forces attacked the Low Countries and then France. Their Blitzkrieg tactics succeeded in defeating the French and British armies in France. The British Expeditionary Force evacuated from Dunkirk leaving their heavy equipment behind, and the French government made a peace, which left the Germans in control of the North and the Vichy government in charge of the South. General Charles de Gaulle, a member of the French Cabinet in 1940, escaped from the German occupation in France. On June 18, 1940 De Gaulle spoke to the French people from London, via BBC radio. The British Cabinet had attempted to block the speech, but was over-ruled by Winston Churchill. De Gaulle asked French men and women to join in the fight against the Nazis. By the end of July that year, only 7,000 people had volunteered to join the Free French forces. Now in June 1941, Japan controls Indochina and France is a weak junior member of the Allies. Can France wrestle its overseas province from Vichy? When will metropolitan France be free again and what role will Free France play?
column5: Tras la humillante derrota de junio de 1940 y la particion entre la zona ocupada por el Eje y el regimen colaboracionista de Vichy, el general Charles de Gaulle alzo la bandera de la Francia Libre desde Londres. A mediados de 1941, las fuerzas galas libres combaten por el control del imperio colonial en Africa y Oriente Proximo, buscando restituir a Francia entre las principales potencias aliadas.

column2: Four years after their crushing defeat, the French have hope again. With the landings by Allied forces in Normandy, the expulsion of the German oppressor from French soil seems now only a matter of time. But after the years of hardships and fighting from colonies and foreign soil, Free French forces under De Gaulle are determined to carry the war into Germany with their allies, to restore the honour of the French nation, and to get rid of Hitler and Nazism once and for all.
column5: Cuatro anos despues de la ocupacion alemana, el desembarco aliado en Normandia y la resistencia interior abren el camino hacia la liberacion metropolitana. El Ejercito de Liberacion frances del general De Gaulle combate junto a estadounidenses y britanicos para reconquistar Paris, limpiar el territorio nacional y llevar la ofensiva final al corazon del Tercer Reich.

column2: On May 8, 1945, the Allies accepted German surrender terms at the conclusion of the European conflict of World War II. France's long struggle for survival was over and focus could be shifted to rebuilding its empire. The destruction of Hiroshima and Nagasaki sealed the fate of Japan, and the surrender documents were signed on the USS Missouri on September 2nd, 1945. Now, Stalin has launched an attack on the Western Allies. Will the French communists support the Soviets? Will France be occupied yet again?
column5: Con la victoria aliada sobre el Eje y restaurada su posicion como gran potencia ocupante, Francia encara en el otono de 1945 la urgente reconstruccion interna y la defensa de su imperio colonial. La repentina ruptura belica entre los Aliados y la Union Sovietica pone a prueba la cohesion de la nacion ante el fuerte arraigo del Partido Comunista Frances y la cercania de los frentes.

column2: France's manpower losses in the First World War were proportionally larger than those of any other major belligerent, and this demographic catastrophe was reflected in the shortfall of annual army conscripts , the so-called 'hollow classes' - of the interwar period. With a revived Germany, a self-aggrandizing Italy, and an increasingly unstable Spain on its borders, France could not afford to accept this military weakness without abandoning its pretensions to Great Power status. To compensate, the nation threw itself into a massive fortified works project on the Franco-German frontier during the early 1930s, and tried to build new diplomatic arrangements with the 'little entente' powers of central and eastern Europe. By 1936, this has had mixed results. France's immediate security problems have been partially resolved by its mighty Maginot Line (but what of the unprotected Belgian border?), and it has warm relations with the Czechs and Poles - and even a developing rapprochement with the Soviet Union. But the Third Republic is a deeply divided nation, with a brittle and unsteady political system, and whether it can still weather a serious challenge for the hegemony of the continent remains to be seen.
column5: En 1936, la Tercera Republica Francesa sufre la sangria demografica de la Gran Guerra y una aguda inestabilidad politica parlamentaria. Mientras el gobierno del Frente Popular de Leon Blum emprende reformas laborales, el Estado Mayor se atrinchera tras la imponente linea Maginot, buscando coordinar alianzas con Gran Bretana, Polonia y la URSS ante el rearme de la Alemania de Hitler.

column2: The mountainous Kingdom of Georgia was a Christian enclave on the borders of Asia for over a thousand years. In 1801, however, the country was conquered and annexed by Russia. An extensive programme of Russification followed, as Georgian culture was suppressed. During the late 19th century this led to widespread popular unrest, a major peasant uprising in 1905, and the rise to influence of the far-left Social Democratic Party (where Josef Stalin had his political apprenticeship). When Lenin's Bolsheviks seized power in Russia, Georgia took the opportunity to proclaim its independence once again. However, the new state faces threats from both the Turks to the south and the warring Russian factions to the north. Relations with Georgia's immediate neighbours, Armenia and Azerbaijan, are more complex. Should the three small countries combine their strengths to resist outside invasion? Or will they fall prey to their own age-old feuds and rivalries?
column5: Enclave cristiano en el Caucaso durante siglos, Georgia fue anexionada por el Imperio ruso en 1801 e intensamente rusificada. Tras decadas de agitacion campesina y el auge menchevique, el colapso zarista y la revolucion bolchevique de 1917 permitieron proclamar la Republica Democratica de Georgia. El joven estado afronta la amenaza del avance otomano por el sur y la guerra civil rusa por el norte, mientras gestiona complejas disputas fronterizas con Armenia y Azerbaiyan para preservar su independencia.

column2: The German people had long suffered betrayals throughout the early twentieth century, first at the hands of Italy in the Great War, then by his own citizens in the Dolchstoßlegende. The people spoke up, and revolution began! But before the revolution fully took hold, Germany was betrayed once again by the leftists, the Social Democratic Party. As a result of the Weimar Republic, Germany lay in ruins after the war suffering under the Tyranny of Versailles and forced to unfairly admit blame for a war. As an insult to injury, the victorious entente then offered 'aid' in reconstruction only to withdraw it a moment later and demand war reparations. The people could only watch as the hated French took over the Ruhr in 1923 while the government did nothing. The traitorous Weimar Republic seemed to collapse as Communists and National Socialists both rallied the people to revolt, given promises by the army of support. They were nothing but empty words. Now, it has been another ten years under the Weimar Republic. Another ten years of economic ruin, famine, mismanagement, and humiliation. The people can not take anymore injustice. The country is at a standstill, with daily skirmishes and protests organized by Communist and Nationalist Socialist militias. Both ideologically opposed parties now find themselves in a position to lead the Reichstag. Will Germany embrace communism and overturn the unjust Bourgeoisie societies that ruined him? Will Germany be drawn in by the charismatic Hitler who promises law and order in a new German Reich? Or, worse, will Germany be betrayed once again in another Dolchstoßlegende?
column5: Marcada por la derrota de 1918, la crisis economica y las duras clausulas del Tratado de Versalles, la Republica de Weimar se halla sumida en una profunda paralisis institucional. El desempleo masivo, las secuelas de la Gran Depresion de 1929 y los constantes choques callejeros entre milicias comunistas y nacionalsocialistas han erosionado la autoridad gubernamental. En 1933, ante la polarizacion politica extrema, Alemania se encuentra ante la encrucijada definitiva de encumbrar al Partido Nacionalsocialista de Adolf Hitler o sucumbir a una revolucion socialista de corte sovietico.

column2: Germany's defeat in 1918 ushered in its first democratic government, as well as a legacy of economic misery and irredentist resentment against the 'slave treaty' of Versailles. Shorn of its colonies and its Polish provinces, burdened with reparations payments and an artificially weakened army, treated as a pariah state for its alleged responsibility for the war, Germany's political path throughout the Weimar Republican years was a tragic spiral of violence and extremism. The ascent of Adolf Hitler's National Socialist Party in 1933 marked a turning point in Germany's historical development. Representative government, comprehensive civil rights and a free press were quickly swept away by the incoming Nazis, who embarked on an increasingly vicious campaign of repression against the nation's 'undesirables', such as Jews, Communists, Trade Unionists, and other opponents of the regime. But Hitler also revitalized Germany's languishing economy and promised to end the inequities of Versailles. German diplomatic triumphs followed one by one: the remilitarization of the Rhineland, the long-awaited Anschluss with Austria, and the absorption of Czechoslovakia. But Britain and France refused to cave in over Germany's challenge to Poland, and now the Reich unexpectedly finds itself at war with three encircling powers. Can the still-modest German war machine defeat such a formidable array of enemies? Only the enigmatic ruler in Berlin knows for sure.
column5: Tras el colapso de la Republica de Weimar y el ascenso del Partido Nacionalsocialista en 1933, Adolf Hitler instauro una ferrea dictadura totalitaria, desmantelando los limites de Versalles y relanzando la produccion militar. Tras la remilitarizacion de Renania, el Anschluss austriaco y la desmembracion de Checoslovaquia, la invasion de Polonia en septiembre de 1939 desata la declaracion de guerra de Gran Bretana y Francia, abriendo un nuevo conflicto a gran escala para el Tercer Reich.

column2: In the aftermath of the joint German-Soviet invasion of Poland, the country was partitioned between both powers under the secret clauses of the Molotov-Ribbentrop Pact. Now, seven months later, German and Allied soldiers still face each other on the Western Front, with no major engagement fought by either side. But while its frontier with France remains quiet, German attentions focused elsewhere. In a bold strike, Germany invaded Denmark and Norway in April 1940 in order to secure the iron-rich areas of Scandinavia, vital for the German war effort. The Danish surrendered without a fight, and it is just a matter of time before Norway also falls to the advancing German Wehrmacht. Now, the Phoney War is about to end. Chamberlain had been so confident he had boasted a month earlier that 'He (Hitler) had missed the bus', but in fact he hadn't. The Wehrmacht has already turned its eyes and armies toward the west, to strike at the Allies. The German Panzer troops are poised on the border of the Low Countries, ready to unleash a new blitzkrieg campaign on an unprepared France. All that would be left would be blood, toil, tears and sweat.
column5: Tras la fulgurante campana de Polonia y el posterior reparto territorial con la Union Sovietica, el frente occidental vivio meses de inaccion durante la llamada 'guerra de broma'. Sin embargo, la ocupacion relampago de Dinamarca y Noruega en la primavera de 1940 aseguro el suministro estrategico de hierro sueco para el esfuerzo militar aleman. En mayo de 1940, la Wehrmacht concentra sus divisiones blindadas frente a las fronteras de los Paises Bajos y Belgica, dispuesta a lanzar una devastadora ofensiva blitzkrieg contra Francia.

column2: Germany's rapid victory over Poland in September 1939 with the assistance of its temporary Soviet ally proved the worth of the new 'lightning' armored warfare tactics advanced by innovative military thinkers like Heinz Guderian. During the temporary lull in the fighting the German High Command adopted an ambitious plan of conquest against France and the Low Countries, instead of beating their heads uselessly against the formidable Maginot defenses or trying a re-run of the 1914 Schlieffen Plan German forces would break through the weak French positions along the Ardennes forest and attempt a massive encirclement of the northern Anglo-French line. In May 1940 this plan masterminded by General von Manstein succeeded beyond anyone's wildest expectations, France surrendered after only six weeks' fighting and the British were forced to evacuate their troops at Dunkirk. This left Germany master of Europe but also left a grand strategic dilemma. The UK was subdued but undefeated and after the failure of the Luftwaffe in the Battle of Britain no realistic seaborne invasion could be attempted for some time. Instead Hitler turned his attention eastwards to the USSR the natural target for his dreams of pan-European 'Lebensraum'. Now Operation Barbarossa is prepared to unleash a whirlwind of destruction against Stalin's army. Will Operation Barbarossa succeed and ensure German mastery of the Continent? Will the Afrika Korps seize the Suez canal and split the British Empire? Will the German wolfpacks starve Britain into submission?
column5: Tras el arrollador exito del plan Manstein en mayo de 1940, Francia capitulo en seis semanas y el contingente britanico fue evacuado en Dunkerque, dejando al Tercer Reich como amo militar de Europa occidental. Sin embargo, la resistencia aerea britanica obligo a cancelar la Operacion Leon Marino. En junio de 1941, Adolf Hitler vuelve sus ejercitos hacia el este para iniciar la colosal Operacion Barbarroja contra la Union Sovietica, persiguiendo el dominio continental y la conquista del espacio vital germano.

column2: After nearly five years of uninterrupted war, Germany's fortunes have sunk low. In the east, the bulk of the Wehrmacht is desperately trying to hold an enormous front that stretches from the Arctic Sea in the north to the Black Sea in the south. The German armies remain deep inside Russia, but the last winter brought defeats at Kursk and in the Ukraine and the loss of much of the army's vaunted Panzer forces. In the west, the Allies have forced a landing in Normandy and are preparing to break out into the vast, nearly unguarded space of occupied France, while in Italy Rome has fallen and the Allies threaten to break through into Austria and southern Germany. How long can Germany hold up under the pressure of this three-front war, combined with an ever-intensifying strategic bombing campaign?
column5: Hacia el verano de 1944, la posicion estrategica de Alemania se deteriora rapidamente. En el frente oriental, las derrotas de Kursk y el contraataque sovietico en Ucrania han desgastado gravemente a las divisiones panzer, que retroceden ante la marea del Ejercito Rojo. En el oeste, el desembarco aliado en Normandia y la liberacion de Roma amenazan con cercar al Reich en una implacable guerra en multiples frentes bajo el asedio constante del bombardeo estrategico aliado.

column2: Germany's defeat in 1918 ushered in its first democratic government, as well as a legacy of economic misery and irredentist resentment against the 'slave treaty' of Versailles. Shorn of its colonies and its Polish provinces, burdened with reparations payments and an artificially weakened army, treated as a pariah state for its alleged responsibility for the war, Germany's political path throughout the Weimar Republican years was a tragic spiral of violence and extremism. The ascent of Adolf Hitler's National Socialist Party in 1933 marked a turning point in Germany's historical development. Representative government, comprehensive civil rights and a free press were quickly swept away by the incoming Nazis, who embarked on an increasingly vicious campaign of repression against the nation's 'undesirables' , Jews, Communists, Trade Unionists, and other opponents of the regime. But Hitler also revitalized Germany's languishing economy and promised to end the inequities of Versailles. By 1936, Germans wonder what their Fuehrer's first major step will be on the international stage. The remilitarization of the Rhineland? The long-awaited Anschluss with Austria? A showdown with Czechoslovakia or Poland over their disputed German-majority provinces? Only the enigmatic ruler in Berlin knows for sure.
column5: Tras la derrota en la Gran Guerra y los anos de convulsion social de la Republica de Weimar, Adolf Hitler asumio el poder en 1933, suprimiendo las libertades constitucionales e iniciando un rearme masivo. En 1936, con la economia reactivada bajo la direccion del Estado y el rearme en plena aceleracion, el Tercer Reich desafia el orden de Versalles, comenzando a planificar la expansion territorial y la remilitarizacion de las fronteras renanas.

column2: Greece's independence from Ottoman rule was officially declared in 1829/30, with the Peace of Adrianople, ending the 6th Russian-Turkish War, and the London Protocol. However, the country was not stabilized until the Danish Prince Wilhelm climbed the Greek throne as Georg I in 1863. Under his rule the country became a parliamentary monarchy with limited powers for the monarch. In 1864 Ionian Islands were brought under Greek rule and in 1881 Thessaly and parts of Epirus. Despite a defeat against the Ottomans in 1897 when Greece supported the Cretan uprising the island could - by pressure of the major powers - jpin the state territory. Macedonia was conquered in the Second Balkans War (1912/13) from Bulgaria, leading to continuously bad relations between the two countries. Now, King Konstantin I favours neutrality or even alliance with Germany, but Prime Minister Eleutherios Venizelos backs an agreement with the Entente to gain aid against Bulgaria and the Ottoman Empire.
column5: Consolidada su independencia del Imperio otomano en el siglo XIX, Grecia expandio sus fronteras incorporando Tesalia, Creta y zonas de Epiro. Tras duplicar su territorio con la conquista de Macedonia a costa de Bulgaria en las guerras balcanicas de 1912-1913, el reino vive en 1914 una profunda fractura entre el rey Constantino I, de postura neutral y afin a Alemania, y el primer ministro Eleftherios Venizelos, partidario de una alianza decidida con la Entente.

column2: Greece is a deeply divided country. The Greek government, supported by the USA and the UK, has been effectively embroiled in a civil war with the communist partisan army, ELAS. Now Stalin has attacked the West and it seems only a matter of time before the Red Army advances on Greece. Will the USA and the UK provide troops to defend Greece?
column5: Tras anos de dura ocupacion del Eje y una cruenta resistencia interna, Grecia quedo sumida en una guerra civil entre el gobierno monarquico, respaldado por Gran Bretana y los Estados Unidos, y las guerrillas comunistas del ELAS. En el convulso otono de 1945, la creciente confrontacion entre las potencias occidentales y la Union Sovietica convierte a los Balcanes en un punto critico para la contencion estrategica aliada.

column2: Greece's independence from Ottoman rule was officially declared in 1829/30, with the Peace of Adrianople, ending the 6th Russian-Turkish War, and the London Protocol. However, the country was not stabilized until the Danish Prince Wilhelm climbed the Greek throne as Georg I in 1863. Under his rule the country became a parliamentary monarchy with limited powers for the monarch. Also in 1863 were brought under Greek rule, in 1881 Thessaly and parts of Epirus. Despite a defeat against the Ottomans in 1897 when Greece supported the Cretan uprising the island could - by pressure of the major powers - jpin the state territory. Macedonia was conquered in the Second Balkans War (1912/13) from Bulgaria, leading to continuously bad relations between the two countries. During World War One King Konstantin I saw to it that his country remained neutral at first, but pressure from the Entente and Prime Minister Eleutherios Venizelos forced him to abdicate in 1917, and Greece joined the war against the Middle Powers. With the occupation of Smyrna 1919, Greece provoked a war against Turkey. A crushing defeat in 1922 was the result, and over a million Greek fled from Asia Minor to the Hellenistic mainland. This intake of people facilitated a land reform that would end the dominance of big landowners. The supporters of Venizelos urged to turn the state into a republic, and indeed succeeded with their effort between 1924 and 1935. In 1935 the royalists prevailed one more time, bringing Georg II back onto the throne. The fascist regime of Ioannis Mataxas from 1936 on would factually leave the king powerless, though.
column5: Tras la Gran Guerra y la desastrosa campana de Asia Menor de 1922, que provoco la expulsion masiva de la poblacion griega de Turquia, la politica helena alterno entre golpes militares y el efimero ensayo republicano. Restaurada la monarquia en 1935 con el regreso de Jorge II, el general Ioannis Metaxas instaura en 1936 el regimen autoritario del 4 de Agosto, reforzando la defensa nacional ante el expansionismo italiano en el Mediterraneo.

column2: After the liberal revolution of 1871 Justo Rufino Barrios (1873 - 1885) reformed the country politically and economically. The privileges of the Catholic Church were largely removed. The Jesuits were expelled, monasteries were secularised, and schools came under state control. State and church were separated, free choice of religion was introduced as well as direct elections. The infrastructure was expanded, bringing economic rise. The export of Cochenille became obsolete with the development of chemical dyes, and so the economy shifted towards coffee and bananas. Soon the coffee trade was under German control, the bananas production under U.S. control. The Indians remained without rights. The properties (indígenas) were dispossessed to expand the areas for the growth of coffee and bananas. Under General Manuel Estrada Carrera (1899 - 1820), who brought the country closer to the U.S.A., the influence of the United Fruit Company grew. The U.S. companies increasingly meddled with the domestic politics of Guatemala.
column5: La Revolucion Liberal de 1871 implanto profundas reformas en Guatemala, limitando el poder de la Iglesia y fomentando el monocultivo agroexportador de cafe y banano a costa de las tierras comunales indigenas. column2: After the liberal revolution of 1871 Justo Rufino Barrios (1873 - 1885) reformed the country politcally and economically. The privileges of the catholic church were largely removed. The Jesuites were expelled, monasteries were secularized, and schools came under state control. State and chruch were seperated, free choice of religion was introduced as well as direct elections. The infrastructure was expanded, bringing economic rise. The export of Cochenille became obsolete with the development of chemical dyes, and so the economy shifted towards coffee and bananas. Soon the coffee trade was under German control, the bananas production under U.S. control. The Indians remained without rights. The properties (indígenas) were dispossessed to expand the areas for the growth of coffee and bananas. Under General Manuel Estrada Carrera (1899 - 1820), who brought the country closer to the U.S.A., the influence of the United Fruit Company grew. The U.S. companies increasingly meddled with the domestic politics of Guatemala. Conservatives, military, and workers' movement (Movimiento Unionista) opposed this American influence and in 1920 overthrew the Carrera government. Henceforth, the military had great influence on the various short-lived governments who were not able to restrict the influence of United Fruit. column5: Dominada por el monocultivo de cafe y banano bajo el monopolio de la United Fruit Company, Guatemala vivio anos de inestabilidad politica tras la caida de Estrada Cabrera en 1920. column5: Primera republica negra independiente del continente proclamada en 1804 tras una triunfal insurreccion de esclavos contra Francia, Haiti arrastro un largo historial de inestabilidad civil, tensiones entre la elite mulata y la mayoria rural creol, y graves crisis de deuda externa. column2: While preserving European neutrality (the struggle against Belgium was declared an internal conflict) the Netherlands faced all the fiercer challenges in their colonies. Their grip over the banana trade, which made up for over two-thirds of Honduran exports, led to the phrase 'Banana Republic' being coined in reference to Honduras. The fall of banana prices during the Great Depression would lead to a period of instability culminating in an insurrection by liberals in protest of the (surprisingly fair) election of the pro-military Tiburcio Carías Andino. The resulting crackdown would soon put an end not only to those who had risen against Carías, but also to any form of political dissent. Honduras, like so many other Latin American countries of the period, was now in the hands of a rabidly anti-communist, pseudo-fascist dictator.
column5: La caida de las exportaciones bananeras durante la Gran Depresion desestabilizo la politica hondurena, culminando con la eleccion en 1932 del caudillo nacionalista Tiburcio Carias Andino. En 1936, Carias encabeza una dictadura militar personalista que suprime a los sindicatos y partidos de oposicion, garantizando la proteccion de los intereses fruteros estadounidenses a cambio de orden y estabilidad interior.

column2: Following closely after the armistice of November 1918 a democratic national council under Prime Minister Mihály Count Károlyi declared Hungary an independent republic. The neighboring countries, especially Romania and the new Kingdom of Serbs, Slovenes, and Croats, seized the opportunity for territorial conquests. Domestic disputes about the future design of the republic forced the government Károlyi to resign, and the Socialist Party of Hungary, a coalition of Communists and Social Democrats, took power. Under the leadership of Béla Kun a council republic was established. Their attempts at forced social reforms soon led to violent conflicts, however. With the aid of Czech and Romanian troops the forces of restoration managed to crush the republic within a matter of months, at first leading to 'white terror', costing the lives of many suporters of the political left. The situation remained unclear. After the 1920 elections a constitution containing both autoicratic and parliamentary elements was ratified. The question of whether or not the last Habsburg, Karl IV, was to become KIng of Hungary was solved with a compromise. An administrator was appointed instead of a monarch, with former navy admiral Miklós Horthy heeding the call. In the peace treaty of Trianon 1920 Hungary acknowledged formally many territorial claims: the Czechoslovakian for Slovakia, the Romanian for Siebenbürgen, and the Yugoslavian for Croatia and Slovenia. Hungary had lost 70 percent of her territory and 65 percent of her population. Two coup attempts in 1921 to bring Karl IV onto the throne failed while Horthy exploited his position for taking power from the parliament and persecuting democratic forces. To the Great Depression and the social tensions accompanying it Horthy reacted by appointing the ultra conservative Gyula Hömbös as prime minister (1932 - 1936) who would conduct the conducted Hungary's rapprochement towards Nazi Germany and Fascist Italy. The dreams of a Greater 'Hungary' were hardly fulfilled. The Munich Treaty 1938 brought no advantages and the later agreement between Germany and Italy were only minor revisions. Only after the dissolution of Czechoslovakia in 1939 did Hungary achieve minor expansion.
column5: Desmembrada tras la Primera Guerra Mundial por el Tratado de Trianon de 1920, Hungria perdio dos tercios de su territorio y poblacion. Bajo la regencia autoritaria del almirante Miklos Horthy y la influencia del primer ministro Gyula Gombos, el pais oriento su diplomacia hacia la Italia fascista y la Alemania nazi para revertir las clausulas de paz. Gracias a los Arbitrajes de Viena y la particion de Checoslovaquia en 1939, Budapest comenzo a materializar sus anhelos irredentistas.

column2: In January 1943, the Red Army turned the tide with a counteroffensive at Stalingrad and destroyed Hungary's Second Army in February. In September 1944, the Red Army crossed the border, and on October 15 Hungary had signed an armistice with the Soviet Union. However, the Germans staged a coup and installed a pro Axis government. In the aftermath of World War II, Stalin succeeded in forcing its political, social, and economic system on Hungary despite a previously negotiated influence scheme with Britain, further exasperating tensions between east and west. column2: Iceland was settled by Norwegian Vikings over the period of 870-830. After a period of independence, the Norwegian king forced Iceland into a monarchical union in the early 1260s. In 1397, Norway lost its independence to Denmark. The 18th century was truly a devastating century for Iceland, three times the population fell below 40,000 due to famine, small-pox and natural disasters. In 1904 Iceland gained home-rule. After the fall of Denmark, Great Britain sent a military force to defend the island from possible German attack, and this was replaced in July 1941 by U.S. forces under a U.S.-Icelandic defence agreement. The large number of British and American troops had given a boost to the economy, increasing calls for independence. The Icelandic Republic was established on June 17, 1944, after a national referendum where 97 percent of the population voted for a split with the Danish crown. Now, the small Icelandic Coast Guard is the only defense force, and Iceland relies on the USA for defense. What path forward should Iceland take?
column5: Ocupada preventivamente por tropas britanicas en 1940 y transferida a la custodia militar estadounidense en 1941 para proteger las rutas de convoyes atlanticas, Islandia proclamo la republica soberana el 17 de junio de 1944 tras romper sus vinculos con la corona danesa. Carente de ejercito y con una modesta guardia costera, la isla basa su defensa en acuerdos estrategicos con Washington ante el estallido de un nuevo conflicto global.

column2: The Indian Mutiny of 1857 was much more than the name suggests – in reality, it was a full blown rebellion in the north of Britain's most prestigious imperial possession. Large sections of the Indian army, supported by peasants and land-owning 'zamindars', incensed at the condescending and moralising nature of Britain's rule attempted to throw off the imperial yoke. Horrified at the brutality of the mutiny, the perpetrators were dealt with ferociously by the British, who proceeded to change the style of their rule in India. The government took administrative responsibility from the East India Company, and attempts to 'Christianise' the country ceased as British policy changed to govern with, rather than against the grain of Indian tradition. Additionally, Prime Minister Disraeli styled Victoria as 'Empress of India', to consolidate the symbolic nature of British rule in 1877. Importantly, the Indian army was also reformed – British regular units were placed in India with greater frequency, Indian artillery regiments were disbanded, and Indian troops were armed with discarded British rifles. Funded by the Indian taxpayer, the Indian army was one of two pillars upon which British rule rested – as Lord Salisbury described, India was 'an English barrack in the Oriental Seas from which we may draw any number of troops without paying from them'. Before 1914, Indian troops would serve in more than a dozen imperial campaigns, perhaps most spectacularly and efficiently in the Anglo-Abyssinian war of 1868 – a demonstration of the significance of India in Britain's imperial setup. In the 1900s, Lord Kitchener made further reforms to render it capable of repelling invasion, quelling internal unrest and in providing support beyond India's borders. The other great pillar of British rule in India was the Civil Service – nearly 400 million Indians were ruled by no more than a thousand civil servants, making it the most efficient bureaucracy in the world. The ICS attested to Britain's skill in ruling with local Indian support, enjoying the relative indifference – or consent – of the people at large. British rule in India allowed for a great leap forward with regards to infrastructure, irrigation and industry, with the government investing £400 million into India by 1914, and a public health generally improving despite the occurrence of two disastrous famines in the mid to late nineteenth century. The early twentieth century would see the British Raj at its zenith as well as the beginning of underlying dissent. Viceroy Curzon (ruled 1898 to 1905) partitioned Bengal to create a Muslim majority, sparked outrage from Indian nationalists, whilst putting governmental trust in benevolent Indian rulers. Curzon also restored the Taj Mahal, as well as instituting the ultimate symbol of the power and prestige of the British Raj – the Dehli Durbar – the first of which was in 1903. The ceremony to crown Edward VII as the Emperor of India would be rerun in 1911 for George V, was a spectacular display of pomp and ceremony in which the various Maharajas, Princes and Governors swore allegiance to the Emperor. For all the glamour of British rule, by 1914 violence by Indian nationalist terrorists was an increasing problem for British officials – only the year previously, Viceroy Hardinge narrowly survived an assassination attempt.
column5: Tras la rebelion de 1857, la corona britanica asumio el gobierno directo del Raj Britanico, consolidando su dominio mediante una eficiente administracion civil y un disciplinado Ejercito de la India financiado por impuestos locales. Como joya del Imperio britanico y fuente inagotable de tropas expedicionarias, la India encaro reformas militares bajo Lord Kitchener a comienzos del siglo XX, mientras surgen las primeras protestas nacionalistas contra el dominio colonial de Londres.

column2: India has perhaps one of the most fascinating and richest histories of the world. The wealthy peninsula was ruled by many strong dynasties throughout history, the Mughal Empire being the best known of these. During the middle of the second millennium, many strong European nations established colonies on the Indian coastline. England, France, the Netherlands and Portugal all took their piece of the pie. It was the British, however, that lingered the longest and in the end (through diplomacy, and backed by the British army) established British sovereignty over the entire peninsula. The Indian & Pakistani rulers became puppets as a British Governor-General ruled India. Early in the 20th century, a largely non-violent struggle for independence, the Indian Independence Movement, began under the charismatic leadership of Mahatma Gandhi. More than once, the British government opposed Gandhi and even arrested him on various occasions. The Independence Movement had its victory, however, when on August 15th, 1947 it finally gained independence from London.
column5: Sometida al dominio de la corona britanica desde la disolucion de la Compania de las Indias Orientales, la India constituye el nucleo del poder colonial britanico en Asia. En 1936, el movimiento nacionalista encabezado por el Congreso Nacional Indio y el liderazgo de Mahatma Gandhi intensifica sus campanas de desobediencia civil no violenta, demandando el autogobierno frente a una administracion colonial que intenta mantener el control estrategico de la peninsula.

column2: The islands of Indonesia were always rich in spices, sugar, coffee and tea. Many European countries established colonies there during the Colonization Era: the Netherlands, Portugal and the United Kingdom. It was the Dutch, however, who consolidated most of the region under a central administration, the Dutch East India Company. The Dutch government would have its share of problems in the East Indies. The region was very heterogeneous in religion, culture and language. On more than one occasion, the Dutch officials in the region had to resort to military action to maintain peace. During World War II, Indonesia became the target of various Japanese military campaigns. The Empire of Japan needed the resource-rich islands to keep its military machine rolling. The Dutch military presence was routed by Japanese forces. When Japan began to suffer defeats, however, they had to withdraw a lot of troops from the island chain. This created a power vacuum that was promptly filled by Indonesian Nationalists, under the leadership of the young Sukarno. The Nationalists took up arms against the Dutch after World War II ended. The Indonesian War of Independence would rage between 1945 and 1949. In the end, Indonesia became the first third-world country to gain its independence from a colonial power. Unsurprisingly, the catalyst behind the independence -- Sukarno -- would become the first Indonesian president, and his rule would last until 1966 when he was ousted by communist general Suharto.
column5: Ricas en caucho, petroleo y productos agricolas, las Indias Orientales Neerlandesas fueron conquistadas por Japon en 1942 para sostener su maquinaria de guerra. La capitulacion nipona creo un vacio de poder que los nacionalistas indonesios aprovecharon para proclamar la republica en agosto de 1945 bajo el liderazgo de Sukarno, iniciando una dura guerra de independencia frente a los intentos holandeses de restablecer el orden colonial.

column2: In the mid-19th century the Emerald Isle was economically weak and easily troubled by crisis. Between 1846 and 1849 the potato harvest had been completely destroyed and a famine ravaged the land, leading to mass immigration of Irish to the U.S.A. Gradually, voices grew louder in Great Britain, calling for an independence of Ireland from the British Crown. The Liberal Prime Minister William E. Gladstone initiated the separation of the island from the Anglican church in 1869 and a land reform in 1870. He failed in his attempts of pushing through a Home Rule for Ireland, however. The political resistance in Ireland kept growing. The Home Rule League and the Irish Land League fought for autonomy as a first step towards independence.
column5: Tras la devastadora Gran Hambruna de 1846-1849 y la emigracion masiva hacia Norteamerica, Irlanda reclamo con insistencia su autogobierno frente a la corona britanica. Aunque los gabinetes liberales de Gladstone impulsaron la reforma agraria y la desvinculacion eclesiastica, los proyectos de Home Rule encallaron reiteradamente en Westminster. En 1914, mientras la aprobacion del autogobierno queda suspendida por el estallido de la Gran Guerra, la polarizacion entre los Voluntarios Irlandeses y los unionistas armados del Ulster situa a la isla al borde de la guerra civil.

A bloody civil war between opponents and supporters of the compromise followed in 1922/23. Only Eamon de Valera managed to cut the last ties to Great Britain from 1932 on.
column5: Tras el Alzamiento de Pascua de 1916 y la Guerra de Independencia, el Tratado angloirlandes de 1921 establecio el Estado Libre Irlandes como dominio britanico, desatando una cruenta guerra civil fratricida y la particion de los condados de Irlanda del Norte. Con la llegada al poder de Eamon de Valera y el partido Fianna Fail en 1932, Dublin avanzo resueltamente en el desmantelamiento de los ultimos vinculos constitucionales con Londres, preparando en 1936 una nueva constitucion republicana y una estricta politica de neutralidad exterior.

column2: Iraq is a new nation in the world community. Though it broke free from the Ottoman empire in the wake of that empire's collapse following the Great War, the League of Nations disregarded Britain's promised support of Arab independence and assigned large tracts of the Middle East to European mandates. The result was a costly uprising for the British, and a new plan for Britain's new mandate. The British imposed a monarchy, and prepared for the future independence of Iraq, to be ruled by the Hashemite family. However, the state lacked legitimacy, not only was it imposed from outside of the country, it was clearly a British puppet regime which wrote it's constitution according to British 'advice' and drew it's territorial boundaries according to British wishes (and with little regard to tribal or ethnic frontiers.) Nevertheless, it's willingness to cooperate with Britain meant that it was one of the first mandates to end, being granted full sovereignty in 1932 and joining the League of Nations in October of that same year, as well as being one of the founding members of the League of Arab States. Yet, in 1936, the instability of the old regime led to a military coup d'etat led by General Bakr Sidqi, placing the military forever after on the Iraqi political scene. Sidqi's government was to be short-lived, due to his brutal excesses, and he was murdered by the military in August 1937. In September 1939, Iraq is still facing stability problems, but remains outside of the conflict which has just begun in Europe. Though strongly pro-British as the war begins, the country itself remains neutral.
column5: Surgido del colapso otomano y tutelado bajo mandato britanico, el Reino de Irak obtuvo la independencia formal en 1932 bajo la dinastia hachemita. Sin embargo, el protectorado de facto de Londres, el control de las concesiones petroliferas y la continua intromision castrense desataron gran inestabilidad tras el golpe militar de Bakr Sidqi en 1936. En septiembre de 1939, bajo la regencia del emir Abd al-Ilah, Bagdad preserva una precaria neutralidad oficial mientras crecen las corrientes nacionalistas y anticoloniales en el ejercito.

column2: Iraq is a new nation in the world community. Though it broke free from the Ottoman empire in the wake of that empire's collapse following the Great War, the League of Nations disregarded Britain's promised support of Arab independence and assigned large tracts of the Middle East to European mandates. The result was a costly uprising for the British, and a new plan for Britain's new mandate. The British imposed a monarchy, and prepared for the future independence of Iraq, to be ruled by the Hashemite family. However, the state lacked legitimacy, not only was it imposed from outside of the country, it was clearly a British puppet regime which wrote it's constitution according to British 'advice' and drew it's territorial boundaries according to British wishes (and with little regard to tribal or ethnic frontiers.) Nevertheless, it's willingness to cooperate with Britain meant that it was one of the first mandates to end, being granted full sovereignty in 1932 and joining the League of Nations in October of that same year, as well as being one of the founding members of the League of Arab States. Yet, in 1936, the instability of the old regime led to a military coup d'etat led by General Bakr Sidqi, placing the military forever after on the Iraqi political scene. Yet, Iraq's stabilities problems were not over, an Anglophobic Arab nationalist by the name of Rashid Ali Al-Gaylani became prime minister in 1941, and promptly tried to curtail Britain's continued domination of the region by seeking aid from Germany. When ministers still loyal to the British pressed him to resign, yet another coup d'etat was organized, with Al-Gaylani supported by four pro-Axis generals known as the 'Golden Square.' It didn't take Britain long to react, and the short-lived Al-Gaylani regime was toppled within a month by the arrival of British troops, sending Al-Gaylani to exile in Germany. By the end of 1941, Iraq is firmly under British control.
column5: En la primavera de 1941, el nacionalista panarabista Rashid Ali al-Gailani y la faccion militar progermana del Cuadrado Dorado tomaron el poder en Bagdad, amenazando las vitales rutas petroliferas de Oriente Proximo. La inmediata intervencion angloindia en la corta guerra angloiraki restablecio la tutela de Londres y la regencia hachemita en junio de 1941, afianzando la presencia militar aliada en la region frente a las intrigas del Eje.
