Nevertheless, it's willingness to cooperate with Britain meant that it was one of the first mandates to end, being granted full sovereignty in 1932 and joining the League of Nations in October of that same year, as well as being one of the founding members of the League of Arab States. By 1936, the regime still faces the problem of legitimacy and there is grumbling amongst the military, but how Iraq will fare in the years to come remains unknown.
column5: Establecido como monarquia hachemita tras sofocar la gran rebelion de 1920 y admitido en la Sociedad de Naciones en 1932, Irak vive en 1936 una fragil soberania. Pese a la administracion del rey Ghazi I, el Reino Unido conserva bases aereas estrategicas y un monopolio crucial sobre la extraccion de crudo, mientras las elites castrenses y tribales cuestionan la legitimidad de un regimen fuertemente dependiente de Londres.

column2: At the start of the 19th century Italy was a mere 'geographical expression.' However, thanks to the efforts of the Piedmontese statesman Cavour and the nationalist leaders Mazzini and Garibaldi, all that changed during the Risorgimento of 1859-70. With French help, Piedmont-Sardinia fought two wars against Austria to recapture provinces held by the Hapsburgs, while popular uprisings broke out in the other Italian principalities. In 1861, the Kingdom of Italy was proclaimed, and in 1870 Italian troops occupied Rome and declared it the capital of a united country. However, several Italian-speaking provinces remained in Austrian hands, and this territory - 'Italia irredenta' - was regarded by many Italian patriots as unfinished business. For the moment, though, such nationalist aspirations were put on hold as Italy aligned herself with Bismarck's Germany in the Triple Alliance. Instead, Italian ambition was turned towards establishing a colonial empire. Some settlements were established in the horn of Africa, but Italy's humiliating defeat at Adowa in 1896 against Abyssinian tribesmen left her the laughing-stock of Europe. Burning for revenge, Italy next turned on the weakened Ottoman Empire, seizing the province of Libya and several Mediterranean islands from the Turks in 1911-12. On the domestic front, Italy is a divided country. The north is a modern industrial society, but plagued by the activities of revolutionary socialists. The south seems to belong to an earlier age, with primitive peasant agriculture, blood feuds and secret societies. Many solutions are offered for the turmoil: liberal reform, a Marxist reorganisation of society, or the adoption of an aggressive nationalist policy to direct peoples' attention outwards. As war clouds gather over Europe, though, the question is who will Italy support? Should she stand by the old alliance with Germany, or join the Entente powers to reclaim the lost Italian lands from Austria? Or perhaps Italy should steer her own independent course in the world?
column5: A comienzos del siglo XIX, Italia no era más que una mera 'expresión geográfica'. Sin embargo, gracias a los esfuerzos del estadista piamontés Cavour y de los líderes nacionalistas Mazzini y Garibaldi, todo cambió durante el Risorgimento de 1859-1870. Con ayuda francesa, Piamonte-Cerdeña libró dos guerras contra Austria para recuperar las provincias en poder de los Habsburgo, mientras estallaban levantamientos populares en los demás principados italianos. En 1861 se proclamó el Reino de Italia, y en 1870 las tropas italianas ocuparon Roma y la declararon capital de un país unido. No obstante, varias provincias de habla italiana permanecieron en manos austriacas, y este territorio -la 'Italia irredenta'- era considerado por muchos patriotas italianos una cuestión pendiente. Por el momento, sin embargo, tales aspiraciones nacionalistas quedaron aparcadas cuando Italia se alineó con la Alemania de Bismarck en la Triple Alianza. En su lugar, la ambición italiana se orientó hacia la creación de un imperio colonial. Se establecieron algunos enclaves en el Cuerno de África, pero la humillante derrota de Italia en Adua en 1896 frente a las tribus abisinias la convirtió en el hazmerreír de Europa. Ansiosa de revancha, Italia se volvió entonces contra el debilitado Imperio otomano y arrebató a los turcos la provincia de Libia y varias islas del Mediterráneo en 1911-1912. En el plano interno, Italia es un país dividido. El norte es una sociedad industrial moderna, aunque sacudida por la actividad de los socialistas revolucionarios. El sur parece pertenecer a una época anterior, con una agricultura campesina primitiva, venganzas de sangre y sociedades secretas. Se proponen muchas soluciones para la agitación: reformas liberales, una reorganización marxista de la sociedad o la adopción de una política nacionalista agresiva que desvíe la atención popular hacia el exterior. Sin embargo, mientras los nubarrones de guerra se ciernen sobre Europa, la cuestión es a quién apoyará Italia. ¿Mantendrá su antigua alianza con Alemania, o se unirá a las potencias de la Entente para reclamar a Austria las tierras italianas perdidas? ¿O quizá debería Italia trazar su propio rumbo independiente en el mundo?
column6: Culminado el Risorgimento con la toma de Roma en 1870, el Reino de Italia consolido su desarrollo industrial en el norte, contrastando con el atraso agrario meridional. Tras la humillacion de Adua en 1896 y la conquista de Libia y el Dodecaneso frente a los otomanos en 1912, Roma encara 1914 como miembro formal de la Triple Alianza con Alemania y Austria-Hungria. No obstante, las profundas reivindicaciones territoriales sobre el Trentino, Trieste y la costa adriatica abren el debate sobre una posible intervencion junto a la Entente.

column2: Italy did not do well out of the Great War. For the 650,000 dead and nearly 1,000,000 wounded that she suffered, the territorial gains awarded at the peace tables of Versailles and St. Germain fell far short of what had been promised to attract her to the Allies' cause. The result was disillusion and resentment, not just of Britain and France, but also of a government that was seen to have demanded great sacrifice for very small benefit. A consequence of this, in turn, was Benito Mussolini. Mussolini was brought to power on the back of prolonged inflation, high food prices (partly the result of the large number of peasant farmers killed or crippled), political polarisation fed by a growing communist constituency, and government torpor accentuated by the introduction of proportional representation. He achieved power with the famous march on Rome by 40,000 of his Blackshirts. From the moment that the army declined to oppose the march the fate of Italy was effectively in his hands, and through a series of political manoeuvres he ensured that it would deliver him a totalitarian dictatorship by 1926. Formerly a socialist, through the late 20s and early 30s Mussolini evolved the principles of Fascism. These specifically rejected the 'doctrine of Pacifism' and affirmed 'the immutable, beneficial, and fruitful inequality of mankind, which can never be permanently leveled through the mere operation of a mechanical process such as universal suffrage'. For the individual, these expressed themselves in the deprivation of all 'useless and possibly harmful freedom', and for the State in the expansion of the nation and the growth of empire. Wedged between these was a social policy maintaining the State's responsibility to improve the lot of its citizens (manifested in a series of major public works), and a 'flexibility' of dogma that permitted the early transfer of many public industries to private ownership and the later movement of those same industries back under strict government control. By 1933, while the Fascist Party was still in an unassailable position electorally, Mussolini's personal popularity was slowly beginning to decline. This was in large part due to inefficiencies and scandals plaguing many of the programs he had pioneered and championed. Not least of these was the rearmament effort where indecision and production failures were to have serious long-term consequences.
column5: Amparado en el descontento popular por la victoria mutilada de 1918 y la severa crisis de posguerra, Benito Mussolini accedio al poder tras la Marcha sobre Roma de 1922 y transformo al reino en un estado corporativo totalitario. Hacia 1933, el regimen fascista consolida su control interno y proyecta sus ambiciones de hegemonia en el Mediterraneo, buscando canalizar el descontento obrero hacia un acelerado rearme militar y una agresiva expansion exterior.

column2: Italy entered the First World War with high expectations of gaining territory in the Alps and along the Adriatic shoreline from the Austro-Hungarians, and perhaps taking part in the carve-up of the moribund Ottoman Empire. Its actual performance in that war was disappointing, however, and it received less than expected from the Versailles settlement following the Armistice. This further weakened the country's already unstable parliamentary democracy and paved the way for Benito Mussolini's famous 'March on Rome' in 1922, which helped establish Europe's first fascist dictatorship. To help bolster the popularity of his autocratic regime Mussolini was pledged to return Italy to Great Power status, to build up formidable land, sea and air forces, and to expand the Italian colonial empire. In 1936 his successful offensive against the Abyssinians removed the ignominious stain of Italy's 1898 defeat at Adowa, but the attack permanently alienated Italy from the West. Now, as war clouds loom over Europe, should Italy throw its hat into the ring? The booty of conquest beckons, but it is far from clear whether Italy's modest industrial resources are capable of extended war. The fate of the Italian fascist experiment is uncertain.
column5: Tras imponer la dictadura fascista en la decada de 1920 y completar la cruenta conquista de Etiopia en 1936, Benito Mussolini consumo su alejamiento de las democracias occidentales y rubrico el Pacto de Acero con la Alemania de Hitler. Sin embargo, el esfuerzo belico en Africa y la intervencion armada en Espana han agotado los arsenales y divisas italianas. En septiembre de 1939, Roma proclama la no beligerancia, consciente de que su industria carece de recursos para afrontar una guerra prolongada.

column2: Italy has not had a happy war. In June 1940 flushed with confidence after Germany's rapid success against France and Britain in the Ardennes offensive, Mussolini declared war on the West in the hopes of joining in the rich harvest. But despite France's surrender Italian victories have been frustratingly few. In North and Eastern Africa a series of initial Italian assaults against British colonial territory were vigorously rebuffed, Italy has been ejected from East Africa, and Mussolini was forced to request German aid in North Africa. The daring British attack on the fleet at Taranto set back Italy's hopes of challenging the Royal Navy's maritime supremacy in the Mediterranean. And an abortive attack on Greece was thwarted so effectively by the defenders that Germany had to bail out Italy in the Balkans. The conquered Greek and Yugoslavian provinces remain a hotbed of resistance a constant security burden for the overstretched Italians. Also, now Italy is at war with the Soviet Union. Italy does have some advantages, the British are weak in Africa and could easily be ejected from Egypt with some tactical skill. Now with German attentions focused almost exclusively on the Eastern Front Mussolini must decide how he can remove Italy from the shadow of its larger Axis partner and forge a truly independent military strategy.
column5: Animado por la caida de Francia, Mussolini entro en guerra en junio de 1940 buscando un botin rapido en el Mediterraneo. No obstante, los duros reveses en Grecia, la perdida de Africa Oriental y el bombardeo naval britanico en Tarento evidenciaron las carencias del ejercito italiano, forzando la intervencion de la Wehrmacht en los Balcanes y del Afrika Korps en Libia. A mediados de 1941, Roma depende militarmente de Berlin mientras empena sus divisiones en el norte de Africa y la invasion de la Union Sovietica.

column2: The new government of Italy is fragile, and many of its supporters are Communists who resisted the Fascist regime. Now, the Soviet Union has declared war on the Allies. Will Italy be able to withstand the Communist tide, and keep its own Communist movement from taking power?
column5: Tras el derrocamiento del fascismo y dos anos de sangrienta ocupacion militar y guerra partisana en la peninsula, Italia emerge en 1945 con una administracion democratica sumamente fragil. La abrupta ruptura belica entre los Aliados occidentales y la Union Sovietica desata la alarma en Roma, donde la enorme influencia del Partido Comunista Italiano y la devastacion de posguerra amenazan con desestabilizar el orden institucional.

column2: Italy entered the First World War with high expectations of gaining territory in the Alps and along the Adriatic shoreline from the Austro-Hungarians, and perhaps taking part in the carve-up of the moribund Ottoman Empire. Its actual performance in that war was disappointing, however, and it received less than expected from the Versailles settlement following the Armistice. This further weakened the country's already unstable parliamentary democracy and paved the way for Benito Mussolini's famous 'March on Rome' in 1922, which helped establish Europe's first fascist dictatorship. To help bolster the popularity of his autocratic regime Mussolini was pledged to return Italy to Great Power status, to build up formidable land, sea and air forces, and to expand the Italian colonial empire. In 1936 he is poised to conduct his first major step in this campaign, an offensive against the Abyssinians which will (he hopes) remove the ignominious stain of Italy's 1898 defeat at Adowa. But this attack is bound to be diplomatically controversial, and it is far from clear whether Italy's modest industrial resources are capable of extended war. The fate of the Italian fascist experiment is uncertain.
column5: Tras instaurar la dictadura fascista y desmantelar el sistema parlamentario en la decada de 1920, Benito Mussolini proyecta convertir a Italia en la potencia hegemonica del Mediterraneo. A comienzos de 1936, el regimen se halla inmerso en la invasion de Etiopia para vengar el desastre de Adua de 1896, desafiando las sanciones de la Sociedad de Naciones y forzando un viraje diplomatico y militar hacia un pacto estrecho con la Alemania nazi.

column2: When Commodore Perry's warships entered Tokyo Bay in 1853 to demand international trading rights with Japan, the long policy of isolationism that had held sway under the rule of the Tokagawa Shogunate was effectively put to an end. Continued western meddling convinced the Japanese of a necessity to modernise, if only to save the country from falling under European domination, a fate which had befallen China. With the Meiji Restoration (1868-9) came the reform that Japan needed to survive: politically, socially and economically the workings of the country were reformed - the nation was divided into organised prefectures, a centralised bureaucracy was introduced, a new constitution was initiated, railways were built and modern industries were constructed. Alongside Japan's entry onto the world stage came an active foreign policy of territorial expansion and the wielding of the country's new found might to accompany the rapidly growing Japanese economy. In 1894 Japan, fearful that Chinese influence in Korea - 'the dagger pointed at Japan's heart' was growing, declared war on China, claiming the island of Formosa in the process. In 1902, Japan secured their status as a great power by signing an alliance with Great Britain, motivated by the two countries' animosity towards Russia. Relations with Russia, already strained after their occupation of Manchuria in 1897 and growing influence in Korea, spilled over into war in 1904, when the Japanese fleet launched a surprise attack upon Port Arthur. The army won a string of successes in Southern Manchuria, and the victory was rounded off when Admiral Togo annihilated the Russian Baltic Fleet in the straits of Tsushima on 17th May 1905. By 1914, despite having obtained local hegemony, Japan remains nervous: Russia steadily recovers from its defeat of 1905, China is moving towards reform and unification, and the United States' influence in the region grows yet further. How events develop in Europe will surely dictate Japan's policy in the upcoming decade.
column5: Iniciada su transformacion moderna con la Restauracion Meiji en 1868, el Imperio del Japon emergio como la principal potencia del Lejano Oriente tras derrotar a China en 1895 y a Rusia en 1905, incorporando Formosa, Corea y Port Arthur. Respaldada por su alianza naval con Gran Bretana desde 1902, Tokio observa en 1914 el estallido del conflicto europeo como una oportunidad estrategica inmejorable para apoderarse de las posesiones coloniales alemanas en el Pacifico y afianzar su predominio en Asia.

column2: Japan, despite it's small landmass, was the leader in Asia during the 1930s. Successfully modernizing in the Meiji Restoration, she grew into a regional power under the rule of Emperor Taisho. During this time, Japan experienced years of prosperity under increased democratic reforms accompanying the 123rd Emperor's rule. Out of this new sense of national pride rose the Kodoha and Toseiha factions, ultra nationalists who advocated a new era for Japan, one dominated by Shintoism and Imperialism. Spurred by the strength of the Army, weakness of her neighbors, and a sense of letdown by the Treaty of Versailles, Japan rapidly expanded to include the realms of Manchuria and Korea justified under the phrase 'Asia for Asians'. Unfortunately, the demands of continued development and conflicts required minerals and resources simply not found in the nation. In addition, aggressive diplomacy by the West, fearing a rival in the Pacific Theater, made trade near impossible. To make matter worse, elements within the Imperial Army now considered themselves above civilian rule, often instigating wars, albeit victorious, with her neighbors again and again without authorization. The new 124th Emperor of Japan, Showa, faces a critical decision. Does he allow the nationalist factions within the army continued free reign, even if they believe in an end to Imperial authority and a return to the Shogunate system? Or will he support the Imperial Navy still loyal to the monarchy, repair relations with Japan's neighbors, risk an army mutiny, and lose honor among the Japanese populace by criticizing the triumphant but out of control Army?
column5: Consolidado como potencia industrial en Asia, Japon sufrio en la decada de 1920 graves fracturas sociales y la crisis economica de 1929, facilitando el ascenso de facciones militaristas ultranacionalistas como la Kodoha y la Toseiha. Tras la ocupacion no autorizada de Manchuria en 1931 y la creacion del estado satelite de Manchukuo, el Estado Mayor imperial se impuso sobre la autoridad civil, desafiando a la Sociedad de Naciones para asegurar por la fuerza las materias primas que demandaba su industria armamentistica.

column2: The only non-western country to successfully negotiate the transition from a traditional economy and society to an advanced industrial nation-state, Japan did well out of the First World War, occupying the former German Pacific island chains and clearly advancing its claim to be the preeminent power in Asia. But financial misfortunes during the 1920s destabilized Japan's civilian parliamentary government, and led the way for a series of bloody coups and assassinations by extreme nationalist military leaders. An increasing concern at the country's poor raw materials base, essential for the subjugation of further colonial territory, led the military to attack Manchuria in 1931 in pursuit of Japan's long-standing aim of achieving hegemony over China. This brought material rewards but also loud complaints from the western democracies, which now seemed increasingly hostile towards Japan's strategic goals. A further full-scale attack on China began in 1937, but despite many battlefield triumphs an end to the conflict still seems far off. As war breaks out in far-off Europe, Japan stands at a crossroads with many options but no straightforward path. Is an offensive against Soviet Siberia a better long-term plan than the Chinese quagmire? Or how about the oil and rubber-rich provinces of South East Asia? The Americans may prove dangerous foes, they too must be taken into account.
column5: Tras invadir Manchuria en 1931 y desatar la invasion a gran escala de China en 1937, el Imperio del Japon se halla atascado en una desgastante guerra de desgaste continental. Ante las sanciones comerciales occidentales y la escasez de petroleo y caucho, el alto mando en Tokio debate en septiembre de 1939 si concentrar sus divisiones en una ofensiva septentrional contra la Union Sovietica tras el choque de Nomonhan o avanzar hacia las ricas colonias europeas del sudeste asiatico.

column2: Japan saw the outbreak of the European war as an opportunity in the Pacific. While British French and Dutch attentions were occupied elsewhere the Japanese might be able to harvest the rich resources of the colonial empires of South East Asia, badly needed resources like rubber and oil could be found in plenty in Malaya, Indo-China, and the East Indies. Not long after France's surrender to Hitler, Japanese troops, with the acquiescence of the Vichy Government, had moved into French Indochina. In September 1940, Germany, Italy, and Japan concluded the Tripartite pact, and the following April, Russia and Japan reached agreement and signed a neutrality pact. Only this way thought the Japanese military elite, now ruling the country, would Japan be able to finally end its sluggish battle of attrition in China and assert its predominance across the eastern world. However, the plan had one chief obstacle--the attitude of the United States. The Roosevelt administration was clearly not prepared to countenance any Japanese actions in SE Asia without a fight as it proved when America embargoed sales of oil in protest at Japan's takeover of Vichy French territory in Vietnam and Cambodia. Only by removing the American military threat concluded the generals could Japan be free to act in the Pacific. To this end Japan's most formidable strategic planner Yamamoto is preparing a plan to attack the US Pacific Fleet at its Pearl Harbor base and so damage American confidence that the country would be bound to sue for peace. Could this great gamble against the overwhelming industrial power of America pay off? Or, would a strike at the Soviet Union, known to the Japanese High Command as the Northern Resource Area, be the best course of action?
column5: Acosado por el embargo petrolero angloestadounidense tras su despliegue en Indochina y ligado al Eje por el Pacto Tripartito, el Imperio del Japon decidio romper el cerco economico mediante una audaz ofensiva aeronaval. Tras el sorpresivo ataque a Pearl Harbor en diciembre de 1941, las fuerzas imperiales lanzan invasiones simultaneas sobre Malasia, Filipinas y las Indias Orientales Neerlandesas para asegurar el petroleo y recursos necesarios para sostener su hegemonia en el Pacifico.

column2: After three years of war with the world's greatest economy and its allies, the Empire of the Rising Sun is exhausted materially and morally. Its once-proud navy has been severly mauled, and its invicible armies have been beaten in the Pacific Island Campaign. Yet there is still hope. Japanese soldiers are still unswervingly loyal to the Emperor and will fight to the death in his defense. There remains a ring of protective forces around the Home Islands, yet that ring is slowly and steadily shrinking, as American and Allied armies inexorably close in, ultimately reaaching the very shores of Japan itself.
column5: Tras anos de feroz contienda aeronaval contra la abrumadora industria militar de los Estados Unidos, el Imperio del Japon se halla al borde del colapso material. Diezmada la flota combinada en el mar de Filipinas y perdidas las posiciones defensivas clave del Pacifico central tras sangrientas batallas insulares, las fuerzas imperiales preparan la defensa fanatica del archipielago nacional ante el inexorable avance anfibio y aeronaval aliado hacia sus costas.

column2: The only non-western country to successfully negotiate the transition from a traditional economy and society to an advanced industrial nation-state, Japan did well out of the First World War, occupying the former German Pacific island chains and clearly advancing its claim to be the preeminent power in Asia. But financial misfortunes during the 1920s destabilized Japan's civilian parliamentary government, and led the way for a series of bloody coups and assassinations by extreme nationalist military leaders. An increasing concern at the country's poor raw materials base, essential for the subjugation of further colonial territory, led the military to attack Manchuria in 1931 – part of Japan's long-standing aim of achieving hegemony over China. This brought material rewards but also loud complaints from the western democracies, which now seemed increasingly hostile towards Japan's strategic goals. Japan in 1936 stands at a crossroads with many options but no straightforward path. Should it press ahead with a full-scale assault on China, regardless of how vast a task that might be? Is an offensive against Soviet Siberia a better long-term plan? Or how about the oil and rubber-rich provinces of South East Asia? The Americans may prove dangerous foes, they too must be taken into account.
column5: Consolidado el dominio sobre Corea y el estado satelite de Manchukuo, el Japon de 1936 se halla bajo el tutelaje de las camarillas castrenses del Ejercito y la Marina. Ante el deficit cronico de petroleo y minerales, el alto mando imperial debate entre la doctrina de expansion septentrional hacia Siberia o el avance meridional hacia los ricos recursos del sudeste asiatico, mientras prepara las condiciones para someter definitivamente al gigante chino.

column2: In Latvia, German forces which took control of the region in early 1918 were welcomed by the local nobility, who were of German descent. It was proposed to create a Duchy, to include both Latvia and Estonia, which would be a member-state of the German Empire. This state was finally proclaimed in September 1918, and power given to a Regency Council of German landowners. However, with the defeat of Germany two rival groups also declared Latvian independence: the Latvian People's Council under Ulmanis on 18 November and the Latvian Soviet on 17 December. A three-way civil war ensued. Ulmanis' Nationalist faction managed to defeat the Soviets by early 1919, but meanwhile the German landowners had raised an army and in turn defeated the Nationalists, setting up a government under Niedra. However, Ulmanis sought help from Estonia and by June 1919 had re-established control. He then pursued a policy of reconciliation to win German support for his régime.
column5: Ocupada por tropas alemanas en 1918, Letonia fue escenario de la creacion del efimero Ducado Baltico bajo la nobleza terrateniente germana. Tras el armisticio de noviembre, el Consejo Popular de Karlis Ulmanis proclamo la independencia, debiendo librar una cruenta contienda a tres bandas contra los bolcheviques letones y los cuerpos francos alemanes. Con auxilio militar de Estonia y de la Royal Navy, el gobierno de Ulmanis afianzo el control territorial en 1919 y establecio una republica soberana.

column2: During World War 1 German troops occupied Latvia, then part of Czarist Russia, and German plans of annexing the country led to anti-German sentiments. Nevertheless, when Latvian Bolsheviks attempted to re-integrate the state into the newly Founded Soviet Union, German free corps helped defending the young country's independence in 1918. After the external threat was over, the eternal conflict between Latvians and Baltic Germans who were making up a notable part of the upper class flared up again. Eventually, the Germans were dispossessed of their belongings in 1922, breaking the predominance of the old elites. After Hitler's rise to office in 1933 Latvia found herself between two expansionist powers. With Estonia and Lithuania the Baltic Entente was formed in 1934. The former leader of the independence movement, Karlis Ulmanis, began turning Latvia into a dictatorship in 1936.
column5: Tras alcanzar la independencia en 1920 y completar una amplia reforma agraria que expropio los latifundios de la nobleza germano-baltica, Letonia desarrollo una solida republica parlamentaria. Sin embargo, el impacto de la Gran Depresion alimento tensiones sociales que llevaron al primer ministro Karlis Ulmanis a encabezar un golpe de estado en 1934 e instaurar un regimen autoritario corporativo, integrando en 1936 la Entente Baltica para coordinar su defensa ante la URSS y Alemania.

column2: Following the collapse of the Ottoman Empire after World War I, the League of Nations mandated the five provinces that make up Lebanon to France. After the Vichy government assumed power in France in 1940, the Vichy government controlled Lebanon. The Vichy government's control ended when its forces were unable to halt the advance of British and Free French troops into Lebanon and Syria. As a result of national and international pressure, on November 26, 1941, France proclaimed the independence of Lebanon. The United States, Britain, the Soviet Union and other governments recognized Lebanon's independence. However, even though the French technically recognized Lebanon's independence, the French authorities maintained control and linked the Lebanese currency to the depreciating French franc, tying the Lebanese economy to that of France. When will Lebanon truly be free?
column5: Asignado a Francia bajo mandato de la Sociedad de Naciones tras la particion del Imperio otomano, el Libano quedo bajo control del regimen de Vichy en 1940 hasta su liberacion por tropas britanicas y de la Francia Libre en 1941. Aunque la independencia fue proclamada formalmente ese mismo ano, las autoridades galas preservaron una ferrea tutela monetaria y administrativa hasta la retirada definitiva de sus tropas, consagrando un sistema institucional basado en el pacto confesional.

column2: The Treaty of Lausanne, signed in the aftermath of the Italo-Turkish war, in 1912 resulted in the Ottoman Empire ceding Cyrenaica and Tripoli to the victorious Italians. To many Muslims in Libya, the surrender of territory to a Christian Empire was a betrayal to Islam, and many Bedouin tribesmen ignored the Treaty's outcome and took up arms against the new Italian occupiers. From his powerbase in Fezzan, Southern Tripolitania, the inspiring Ahmad ash-Sharif galvanises his followers into resisting Italian rule - fortunately for the Sanusis, a total lack of infrastructure means that Italy's grip on southern Tripolitania is virtually nonexistant. Similarly, the Sanusian campaign is not only hampered by the Bedouins technological inferiority in comparison to their Italian foes, but by their isolation from separate resistance movements occurring in Northern Tripolitania. Additionally, the Sanusis do not have the backing of wealthy Tripolitanian urban elites, who now seek to reach a compromise agreement with the Italians.
column5: Tras la guerra italo-turca de 1911-1912 y el Tratado de Lausana, el Imperio otomano cedio Tripolitania y Cirenaica al Reino de Italia. Sin embargo, las tribus beduinas del interior y la orden sufi de los senusies, acaudilladas por Ahmad al-Sharif desde el Fezzan, rechazaron la ocupacion y desataron una prolongada guerra de guerrillas que redujo el control italiano a una precaria franja litoral.

column2: Created in the early 19th century by freed African-Americans who either wanted to return to Africa to start a new life or were forced to leave, Liberia was to eventually earn the honour, alongside Abyssinia, of being the only independent countries in Africa. Since their declaration of independence from Great Britain in 1846, Liberia has dealt peacefully with several border conflicts over the years with both France and Britain. The twentieth century so far has seen years of tension between the African-American colonists and the indigenous peoples.
column5: Fundada en el siglo XIX por libertos afroamericanos retornados bajo los auspicios de la Sociedad Americana de Colonizacion, Liberia proclamo su independencia en 1847. Como unico estado soberano del Africa occidental en la era del reparto colonial, la republica negocio sus limites fronterizos con Francia y Gran Bretana, mientras la minoria americo-liberiana de Monrovia mantenia un rigido predominio politico y social sobre las etnias autoctonas del interior.

column2: Created in the early 19th century by freed African-Americans who either wanted to return to Africa to start a new life or were forced to leave, Liberia was to eventually earn the honor, alongside Ethiopia, of being the only independent countries in Africa. Since their declaration of independence from the Great Britain in 1846, Liberia has dealt peacefully with several border conflicts over the years with both France and Britain. The twentieth century has seen for Liberia many years of tension between the African-American colonists and the indigenous peoples of the area, with an international commission from the League of Nations investigating charges of slavery and forced labor in 1929. In the coming conflict Liberia will be an important part of the Allied war effort, as its rubber supply could be vital.
column5: Unica republica soberana del Africa negra junto a Etiopia, Liberia preservo su independencia a costa de una profunda subordinacion economica hacia los Estados Unidos y la compania Firestone, explotadora de sus ricas plantaciones de caucho. Tras superar la crisis institucional y las denuncias internacionales de 1930 por trabajo forzado indigena, el presidente Edwin Barclay busca modernizar la administracion y posicionar al pais como un proveedor estrategico para los Aliados.

column2: The region of Lithuania was under German military occupation in 1917. However, following the Bolshevik coup in Russia the Lithuanian National Council declared itself an independent state, on 11 December 1917. The German authorities were willing to recognise limited Lithuanian independence under their hegemony, and during 1918 negotiations proceeded over installing a German princeling as king of Lithuania. However, the German defeat in November 1918 allowed the Lithuanian National Council to claim full independence.
column5: Ocupada por el ejercito imperial aleman en la Gran Guerra, Lituania vio a su consejo nacional, el Taryba, proclamar la independencia en febrero de 1918. Tras frustrarse los planes de erigir una monarquia tutelada bajo un noble aleman tras el armisticio de noviembre, el naciente gobierno republicano debio organizar apresuradamente sus fuerzas para combatir la invasion del Ejercito Rojo bolchevique y los embates de los cuerpos francos germano-rusos en el Baltico.

column2: As the power of Czarist Russia dwindled, Lithuania slowly made steps towards independence. In 1905/07 they recieved partial autonomy and called for a constitutional assembly. During World War 1 the country was occupied by the Germans, and, after successful Russian Revolution declared independence in 1918 as a democratic republic. This caused the Red Army to march into Vilnius to bring the young state back into Russia, but the intervention of German and Polish troops preserved Lithuania's integrity. Poland nevertheless annexed Vilnius during the Russian-Polish War of 1920. This annexion was recognized by a referendum in 1922. In 1923 Lithuania annexed the Memel area which had till 1919 been under Prussian rule and had been under administration by the Allies since then. The conference of the Allies' ambassadors acknowledged the annexion but insisted of internal autonomy for the region. The time after The Great War was marked by internal crisis in Lithuania. The government decided a land reform in 1922, taking land from the big landowners and robbing them also fo their political and economical leadership. Social tension kept increasing and thus permitted the toppling of the government in 1926 by the army and the right-wing Tautinenkae party. The republican constitution was repealed and an authoritarian regime under Antanas Smetona was installed. In 1934, the Baltic Entente was formed with Latvia and Estonia.
column5: Tras consolidar su independencia en 1918, Lituania perdio su capital historica de Vilna ante Polonia en la campana de 1920 y anexiono la region autonoma de Memel en 1923. La inestabilidad parlamentaria culmino en el golpe militar de 1926 que encumbro a Antanas Smetona en una presidencia autoritaria nacionalista. En 1936, Kaunas procura modernizar sus defensas y mantener la Entente Baltica, atrapada entre el expansionismo nazi en Prusia Oriental y la presion de la Union Sovietica.

column2: The Vienna Congress 1814/15 proclaimed Luxemburg a Grand Duchy and made it part of the Kingdom of the Netherlands. The Dutch King, was, as Grand Duke of Luxemburg at the same time member of the German League. After the Belgian independence in 1831 had to grant its Wallonic territories to Belgium by rule of the London Protocol of 1839. The Dutch attempts to sell the Grand Duchy to the French after the end of the German League 1866 caused the Luxemburg Crisis which ended when the small country was formally granted its independence and neutrality. The personal union with the Netherlands ended in 1890 with the death of Wilhelm III, the last male heir of the house Orania-Nassau. The Salian law of Luxemburg did not allow for female heirs to the crown.
column5: Elevado a Gran Ducado por el Congreso de Viena y con su neutralidad desmilitarizada garantizada por el Tratado de Londres de 1867, Luxemburgo rompio su union dinastica con los Paises Bajos en 1890 al extinguirse la linea masculina de la casa de Orange. Aunque su economia minera y siderurgica quedo integrada en la union aduanera alemana Zollverein, el pequeno estado procura en 1914 que su condicion neutral sea respetada por los beligerantes continentales.

column5: Garantizada su neutralidad perpetua tras la crisis internacional de 1867, Luxemburgo sufrio la ocupacion militar alemana durante la Gran Guerra de 1914 a 1918. Superada la agitacion de posguerra y consolidada la monarquia constitucional bajo la gran duquesa Carlota, el pais integro en 1922 una union economica con Belgica, convirtiendose en 1936 en una prospera potencia siderurgica europea desprovista de fuerzas armadas ofensivas.

column2: Manchuria had been the home of a nomadic people, the Jurchen, many centuries ago, but after they had conquered China and established the Qing Dynasty in 1644, they sought to give legitimacy to their rule by becoming increasingly sinicised. The Manchus grew to admire Confucianism and use Chinese script, and by the time the Dynasty collapsed in 1912, the area was populated by Han Chinese as well as sinicised Manchus. The territories north of the Amur River were lost to Russia in 1858, and the lands east of the Amur, including the port of Vladivostok, were lost in 1861. Today, Russia has interests in northern Manchuria, and Japan has interests in the south. Manchuria is hence important not only to China for historical reasons, but also in a broader geopolitical sense, as it is rich in natural resources and is an important industrial centre in the Far East. Warlord Zhang Zuolin, now in charge of Manchuria, remains nominally loyal to the Beijing regime, but for all practical purposes is a despot in his own kingdom. Naturally, the Beijing government would also like to re-exert control over the region. Surrounded by three powers, how will Manchuria fare?
column5: Cuna de la dinastia Qing que domino China hasta la revolucion de 1911, Manchuria se transformo a comienzos del siglo XX en un codiciado escenario geopolitico disputado por los imperios ruso y japones tras la cesion de Port Arthur y el control ferroviario. Bajo el gobierno militar del caudillo Zhang Zuolin, la Camarilla de Fengtian administra las ricas minas y llanuras septentrionales con total autonomia, maniobrando pragmaticamente frente a Tokio y al gobierno de Beijing.

column2: The Manchu dynasty ruled China until the revolution in 1911 caused the abdication of the final Manhurian Emperor Hsuan T'ung. In 1931, Chinese Nationalists began to challenge the growing influence over Manchuria that the Japanese had been exerting.  In response the Kwangtung Army occupied Manchuria.  In 1932 Japan declared that the region, would be an independent Manchu state, named Manchukuo.  The final Manchu Dynasty emperor, now called K'ang Te was installed as emperor of Manchukuo in 1934.  The Japanese millitary maintained tight control of Manchukuo and few foriegners were allowed into the nation, while the Japanese greatly expanded the regions industrial capacity
column5: Tras el incidente de Mukden en 1931 y la ocupacion militar del Ejercito de Kwantung, el Imperio del Japon separo a Manchuria de la Republica de China y proclamo en 1932 el estado satelite de Manchukuo. Coronado en 1934 el ultimo emperador Qing, Puyi, como monarca nominal, el territorio opera en 1936 como una colonia industrial militarizada, aportando acero, carbon y bases logisticas a las fuerzas armadas niponas en la frontera con la Union Sovietica.

column2: In 1937, open war broke out between China and Japan. On December 8, 1937, Mongolian Prince Teh Wang declared the independence of Inner Mongolia as Mengkukuo and signed close agreements with Manchukuo and Japan, thereby turning Inner Mongolia to a puppet of the Japanese Empire. The capital was established at Chan Pei, near Kalgan, with the puppet government's control extending around Hohhot.
column5: Tras el estallido de la segunda guerra sino-japonesa en 1937, el principe mongol Demchugdongrub proclamo la independencia de la Mongolia Interior como Mengjiang (Mengkukuo) con respaldo militar del Ejercito de Kwantung. Con capital en Zhangjiakou (Kalgan), este gobierno satelite dependiente del Imperio del Japon organiza tropas de caballeria autoctonas para guarnecer la frontera septentrional china frente a las fuerzas comunistas y la Republica Popular de Mongolia.

column2: Mexico gained its independence from Spain in 1821, but its early history was a troubled one - with over 36 different governments in its first 30 years of existence. Even worse was to come at the hands of the overbearing neighbour to the north however. First, in 1836, the English-speaking settlers in the province of Texas managed to successfully rebel. Then, in 1846, the USA provoked a war which led to humiliating Mexican defeat and the loss of over 40 percent of her territory, including California, Arizona and New Mexico. Defeat led to tensions in Mexican society, and in 1858 President Juarez launched an attack on the status and power of the Church and the Army. This triggered a three-year civil war, and the European powers intervened to protect their financial interests. In 1863 France took the opportunity to set up Maximilian of Austria as Emperor of Mexico, supported by French troops. The USA was unwilling to see any power (other than themselves) intervening in Central America, however, and forced France to withdraw. The French puppet Maximilian was executed in 1867, and Juarez regained power. His successor as the dominant force in Mexican politics was Porfirio Diaz, who ruled (with some interruptions) from 1877 until 1911. During this long period, the traditional urban and rural elites endeavoured to strengthen their grip on society, in the face of mounting opposition from democratic and radical forces. Diaz relied heavily on support from Britain and the USA, offering great privileges to foreign investors who took control over significant portions of the Mexican economy. All this caused much unrest, and in 1910 a peasant uprising began, led by Pancho Villa in the northern provinces and Emiliano Zapata in the south. In 1911 a radical northern landowner, Francisco Madero, made alliance with the rebels and overthrew Diaz. He in turn was murdered in 1913, and the military strongman General Huerta took over the government. With the support of the conservative factions in society, the Mexican government must now fight to suppress the revolutionaries and their northern allies, who since the death of Madero are now led by Venustiano Carranza. The support of the USA may well be vital in crushing the revolt, but there is no guarantee that the Yanquis will maintain their support for the Huerta regime - many in Washington favour Carranza as a better ally. Still, for all its problems Mexico is potentially a powerful nation, with a dense population and a prosperous new oil industry. If this civil war can be won, then all sorts of opportunities could arise.
column5: Tras perder mas del 40 por ciento de su territorio en la guerra con Estados Unidos y superar la intervencion francesa con Benito Juarez, Mexico vivio decadas de orden y desarrollo economico desigual bajo el Porfiriato. El estallido de la Revolucion en 1910 y el derrocamiento de Porfirio Diaz derivaron en una sangrienta guerra civil tras el asesinato de Madero en 1913. En 1914, la dictadura militar de Victoriano Huerta lucha por sofocar a las fuerzas constitucionalistas de Venustiano Carranza, Pancho Villa y Emiliano Zapata, en medio de tensiones diplomaticas con Washington y un inmenso potencial petrolero.

column2: Wracked by years of revolution, rebellion, and repeated coups against corrupt governments, Mexico was finally on the path to recovery. Under the control of Plutarco Elías Calles in fact if not in name for the past decade, Mexico had gained a stable but corrupt government under the National Revolutionary Party, whose successive presidents were almost completely under Calles' thumb. By 1934, the increasingly conservative Calles was forced to make concessions to left-wing members of his party by agreeing to the nomination of Lázaro Cárdenas as the NPR's canditate for the presidency. It was to prove a fateful choice, Cárdenas was a scrupulously honest politician who refused to be controlled, and disputed with Calles on numerous issues. By the beginning of 1936, the political environment was growing increasingly volatile between the former strong man and this new rival for power. The only question was who would make the first move......
column5: Tras decadas de conflicto revolucionario y la hegemonia de Plutarco Elias Calles durante el Maximato a traves del Partido Nacional Revolucionario, Mexico encaro una nueva etapa con la eleccion de Lazaro Cardenas en 1934. Decidido a ejercer un mandato autonomo, Cardenas comenzo a desmantelar la tutela de Calles y a impulsar la reforma agraria y los derechos laborales. A comienzos de 1936, la pugna politica entre el general Cardenas y el antiguo Jefe Maximo alcanza su punto culminante, decidiendo el rumbo soberano de la nacion.

column5: Enclavada entre los imperios de Rusia y China, Mongolia aprovecho el colapso de la dinastia Qing en 1911 para proclamar su independencia bajo el Bogd Khan. Ante la negativa de la nueva Republica de China a reconocer su soberania, Urga busco el protectorado diplomatico y militar del Imperio ruso para preservar su territorio y evitar una reconquista china.

column2: Stuck between the gigantic empires of Russia and China, the land of Genghis Khan has long had to struggle for it's independence. Though freed from Chinese rule following the collapse of the ruling Manchu dynasty in 1911, Mongolia's independence was not recognized by the new Republic of China, and therefore Mongolia increasingly turned to Russia for it's continued survival. Yet, the unexpected Russian Revolution of 1917 placed Mongolia in a vulnearable position, with the Russian Civil War soon spilling over the border into it's protectorate. After suffering from an invasion by a Chinese warlord army, a counter-invasion by White Russian forces under Baron Roman Nicolaus von Ungern-Sternberg, an uprising by the Mongolian Partisan Army of Sukhe Bator, and finally a coup that toppled the old Monarchy entirely, Mongolia emerged as the second Communist state in the world and the Soviet Union's only ally, though under tight Soviet control. Though finally stable by 1924, Mongolian history was henceforth to reflect all the tragedies that consumed their larger neighbor to the north. Purges were conducted throughout the 1920's to rid the country of 'capitalist' elements, Buddhist monks and religion were actively suppressed, and the power of the old feudal lords was destroyed. By 1939, however, the Socialist revolution is being tuned down in the face of a new threat from an expansionist Japan. The start of fighting between the Japanese Kwangtung Army and the Soviets along the Khalkhyn Gol river in May has dragged Mongolia into the fighting on the side of the Soviets, but the battle now seems to be winding down to a decisive Soviet victory and Japan is retreating to lick its wounds. At present, the country appears to be safe.
column5: Proclamada como la segunda republica socialista del mundo en 1924 tras la intervencion del Ejercito Rojo contra las fuerzas blancas de Ungern-Sternberg, Mongolia quedo estrechamente alineada con Moscu. Tras anos de colectivizacion forzosa y purgas antirreligiosas bajo Khorloogiin Choibalsan, el pais enfrento la agresion japonesa en la primavera de 1939. La contundente victoria sovietico-mongola en la batalla de Jaljin Gol alejo temporalmente la amenaza del ejercito de Kwantung.

column5: Aliada incondicional de la Union Sovietica y consolidada bajo el regimen comunista de Choibalsan, la Republica Popular de Mongolia observa con alarma la invasion alemana de la URSS en 1941. Aunque la victoria previa en Jaljin Gol y la apertura del frente del Pacifico desviaron la presion japonesa hacia el sur, el destino de la nacion mongola depende por completo de la supervivencia del Ejercito Rojo en el frente oriental.

column5: Establecida como el segundo estado socialista del mundo tras la revolucion de 1921 liderada por Suje-Bator y el auxilio sovietico, Mongolia experimento profundas transformaciones sociales, purgas politicas y la represion del budismo tradicional. En 1936, estrechamente subordinada a las directivas de Moscu, la Republica Popular refuerza su preparacion defensiva y su tratado de asistencia mutua ante el agresivo expansionismo militar japones en Manchukuo e Interior de Mongolia.

column2: The Congress of Berlin formally recognized Montenegro as a state in 1878. However, the heart of Montenegro, known as Old Montenegro in the area around the historical capital of Cetinje, had been the only part of the Balkans never to fully succumb to the Ottoman Empire. In 1516, Montenegro came under the rule of the prince-bishop (Vladika) of Cetinje, a position held from 1697 by the Petrovic family. Daniel I (1851-1860) secularized the country in 1852, separating the spiritual and secular powers of the Vladika. The reign of Nicholas I (1860 - 1918) saw the doubling of Montenegro's territory and international recognition of her independence (1878), the country's first constitution (1905), the ruler's elevation to the rank of King (1910), and further territorial gains following the Balkan Wars (1913). When Austria-Hungary annexed Bosnia and Herzegovina in October, 1908, and thereby annihilated the dreams of Montenegro and Serbia of a united empire, Montenegro protested along with Serbia and, encouraged by Russia, demanded from Austria the annulment of Article 29 of the Treaty of Berlin and the evacuation of Spizza. Ever since, the relations with their powerful neighbour have been deteriorating at a fast rate. The year is 1914, Montenegro is more powerful than it has ever been but it is still a tiny land, and there is talk of war. Could Montenegro defend itself, as it has done for centuries, or could this be its end?
column5: Reconocida su independencia formal en el Congreso de Berlín de 1878 tras siglos de resistencia frente al Imperio otomano, Montenegro se modernizó y consolidó bajo el largo reinado de Nicolás I. Tras aprobar su primera constitución y erigirse en reino en 1910, el país expandió sus fronteras en las guerras balcánicas. En 1914, tras el deterioro de las relaciones provocado por la crisis de anexión bosnia, el pequeño estado eslavo se ampara en su alianza con Serbia y Rusia ante la inminente amenaza militar de Austria-Hungría.

column2: After successful campaigning against Tibet in the late 18th century, the ruling Gurkhas in Nepal were shown their limits when their attacks on British India between 1814 and 1816 led to them having to recognize a factual British protectorate over their territory. A permanent Resident of the British Crown was sent to Nepal after the Peace of Segauli, and he remained in there till 1923. In return, the British acknowledged the today still valid borders of Nepal and the rule of the Gurkhas. From 1850 on Nepal provided the British Colonial Army with the famous Gurkha regiments who were first employed during the Sepoy Uprising in 1857.
column5: Tras la guerra anglo-nepalesa de 1814-1816 y el Tratado de Sugauli, Nepal tuvo que aceptar un protectorado británico de facto mediante el asentamiento de un Residente permanente, obteniendo a cambio el reconocimiento de sus fronteras. A partir de 1850, el país del Himalaya inició una estrecha colaboración militar con Londres, suministrando al ejército colonial sus célebres y feroces regimientos de soldados gurkas.

The domestic politics after 1775 were dominated by power struggles between the kings and the nobility. Three underage kings in a row (1775 till 1832) who were dominated by aristocratic families vying for power additionally weakened the Shah Dynasty. The most influential family were at first the Thapa (1806 - 1837) before the Rana family prevailed. 1846, after the king's nephew, Jang Bahadur Rana (1846 - 1877), had massacred the opposition on Kot Square, the Rana family took power for the following 104 years, making the office of Prime Minister hereditary, reducing the king's power to a minimum.
column5: Sometido a un protectorado británico de facto en 1816, Nepal estrechó su alianza con Londres mediante el tratado de amistad de 1923 tras la valiosa participación de los regimientos gurkas en la Gran Guerra. En el ámbito interno, el poder efectivo reside desde 1846 en la dinastía hereditaria de los primeros ministros de la familia Rana, quienes han marginado a los monarcas de la dinastía Shah a un rol puramente ceremonial, gobernando el país con mano de hierro.

column2: The liberal President José Santos Zalaya (1894 - 1909), who had pursued a course of modernisation of Nicaragua, was overthrown with the help of the U.S.A. who saw their interests in the Panama Canal endangered by Zalaya's expansionist politics. The United States also intervened directly in 1912 in the conflict between conservatives and liberals.
column5: Las reformas modernizadoras y la política expansionista del presidente liberal José Santos Zelaya despertaron los recelos de Estados Unidos, temerosos por la seguridad del Canal de Panamá. Tras apoyar su derrocamiento en 1909, Washington intervino militarmente en 1912 enviando a los marines para sofocar el conflicto interno entre liberales y conservadores, instaurando una ocupación armada de facto para controlar la región.

column5: Liberada la región ártica de Finnmark por el Ejército Rojo a finales de 1944 y restaurada su soberanía tras cinco duros años de ocupación nazi, Noruega inicia la reconstrucción bajo el rey Haakon VII. The transition of from an agricultural country to a modern industrial state brought with it inflation and unemployment after The Great War, leading to a radicalization of the Worker's Party which had been founded in 1887. column2: By 1941, the soldiers of New Zealand have fought alongside their Australian comrades throughout the Mediterranean, first facing defeat in Greece and Creek, then a brief taste of victory in North Africa, followed by more defeat at the hands of Erwin Rommel's Afrika Korps. column5: Tras haber combatido ferozmente en las amargas campañas de Grecia, Creta y el norte de África frente al Afrika Korps, las divisiones de Nueva Zelanda enfrentan un peligro aún mayor. column2: New Zealand was granted its dominion status in 1907, and since then has remained linked closely both with it's mother country Britain and it's larger neighbor Australia. In fact, New Zealand's experiences mirrored those of Australia in many ways, New Zealanders served in the ANZAC (Australian and New Zealand Army Corps), and fought with great distinction from Flanders to Gallipoli to Egypt and Turkey. As a result, they took disproportionate casualties for such a small nation, with over 18,000 of an original overseas force of 100,000 killed in action. Nevertheless, they earned a reputation for ferocity in battle which has never faded. By the 1930's, the Great Depression hit New Zealand's economy hard, with export prices plummeting and lay-offs souring. By 1935, despite the best efforts of the National Party to remedy the situation, New Zealand's economy was in shambles and the Labor party was brought to power as a result. New Zealand is by no means ready for war in 1936, but if it comes, like her larger neighbor, her soldiers can be counted on to support Britain.
column5: Elevada a dominio británico en 1907 y forjada trágicamente en la Gran Guerra mediante el colosal sacrificio de sus cuerpos del ANZAC, Nueva Zelanda vio su economía agropecuaria devastada por la Gran Depresión. La crisis aupó al poder al Partido Laborista en 1935, que comenzó a cimentar un Estado de bienestar pionero. Aunque militarmente mermada en 1936, su inquebrantable lealtad a la corona británica garantiza su participación ante cualquier conflicto.

column2: When Ahmad Al Bu Sa'id rose to power in 1749, Oman embarked upon an age of expansion. For approximately a hundred years Great Britain tolerated their maritime empire which reached from the coasts of East Africa and as far as China, with slave trading and the export of spices formed the primary sources of income. Between 1789 and 1805 rivalries for the throne between factions within the Al Sa'id Dynasty preluded Oman's demise as a major power in the east. Steadily, the country came under the influence of the British Empire without ever becoming a formal colony. During this feud, Muscat on the sea formed a sultanate while the inner country became a relgiously oriented imamate. The growing dominance of the British increased Oman's political and economic dependency. Not only had they lost the rich island of Zanzibar to the British, recieving in exchange the Zanzibar Subsidy, but the opening of the Suez Canal and the prohibition of slave and weapons trade without a viable alternative had completely crippled their economy.
column5: Atrás quedaron los días en que el Imperio marítimo omaní dominaba el comercio desde África Oriental hasta Asia. Lastrado por disputas dinásticas y dividido entre el sultanato costero de Mascate y el imanato tradicional del interior, el país cayó progresivamente bajo la hegemonía británica. Sin la isla de Zanzíbar y con su economía mercantil arruinada tras la apertura del Canal de Suez y el fin del comercio de esclavos, Omán afronta 1936 como un protectorado informal dependiente de Londres.

column2: The Ottoman state was founded by Osman around 1300 AD, and at the apex if its power and prestige in the sixteenth century, the Ottoman Empire stretched from the gates of Vienna to the Indian Ocean and from Algiers to the Crimea. However, by the eighteenth century the empire was shrinking with its power eroded by a loss of internal authority and the expansionist ambitions of the European powers. The nineteenth century and early twentieth century saw attempts at reform, including the creation of an executive branch, centralised government, constitutional guarantees and secularised schools, but also witnessed the Ottoman Empire's substantial territorial decline: Greece became independent (1830), France seized Tunisia (1881), Britain took Egypt (1882), Austria-Hungary annexed Bosnia-Herzegovina (1908) and Italy won control of Tripolitania and Cyrenaica (1911). Meanwhile, the Turkish government was largely unable to collect its own taxes and the empire's communications and infrastructure remained primitive, causing many to refer to Turkey as the 'sick man of Europe'. The inability of the Sublime Porte to modernise caused the Committe of Union and Progress - the 'Young Turks' to rebel and bring about Sultan Abdul Hamid II's abdication in 1908. By 1913, the C.U.P. had come to power in Constantinople with the aim of throwing off Europe's economic and political dominance over the empire and a desire to speed up Turkey's programme of modernisation. It was realised, however, that in order to progress, a European protector was needed so that the expanionist ambitions of Russia, Italy, Austria-Hungary, Greece and Bulgaria could be countered. Traditionally, the Ottoman Empire's chief ally throughout the nineteenth century had been Great Britain, who had sought to limit Russian expansion south. Recently however, Britain has proved to be unreliable as a supporter of Turkey, perhaps best exemplified by the 1907 Anglo-Russian entente, in which the two countries settled their differences over Asia. Alternatively, relations with Germany have been growing warmer and have been made better still by the building of the Berlin-to-Baghdad railway. As it turns 1914, the Ottoman Empire is still in search of a protector: an alliance with Germany will alienate France and Great Britain, but an alliance with those countries will force Constantinople into conceding to Russia's extensive demands in the Black Sea and the Caucasus. Can the Ottoman Empire modernise and survive or will it pass into the bygone era to where many argue it belongs?
column5: Conocido como el "enfermo de Europa" tras perder vastas posesiones en el norte de África y los Balcanes, el decadente Imperio otomano es ahora gobernado por los Jóvenes Turcos del Comité de Unión y Progreso. Frustrados por el constante declive e imperialismo de Rusia y Gran Bretaña, las élites otomanas han estrechado vínculos militares e infraestructurales con el Imperio alemán. En 1914, Constantinopla busca revertir su colapso forjando una alianza definitiva que garantice su supervivencia.

column5: La génesis de Panamá está inextricablemente ligada a la construcción de su célebre Canal. Al redactarse su independencia bajo el auspicio de Estados Unidos, la nueva república cedió los derechos a perpetuidad de la Zona del Canal, convirtiéndose en un protectorado de facto esencial para la estrategia comercial y naval norteamericana.

While still firmly in the grip of the United States, these measures may not be able to still the budding tides of Panamanian anti-Yankee nationalism.
column5: Forjada como nación en 1903 mediante la intervención estadounidense para construir el Canal interoceánico, Panamá operó durante décadas como un protectorado. column2: Dictator José Gasparo Rodriguez (1811/14 - 1840) preserved Paraguay's integrity against Argentinian and Brazilian claims through a self-sufficient economy and cutting off his country politically. column5: Tras mantener una celosa política de aislamiento bajo la dictadura del doctor Francia, Paraguay intentó forzar una salida al mar bajo Francisco Solano López, lo que desembocó en la catastrófica Guerra de la Triple Alianza (1865-1870). Internally the elements of reform and westernization conflict with an increasingly conservative clergy. Internationally Persia was split, in 1907, into a Russian northern sphere and a British south, although it would never be a formal colony of either power. After several attempts at a constitutional monarchy in the first decades of the 20th Century, Persia was thrown into social, political, and economic chaos. Reza Khan, an army officer, finally staged a successful coup against the corrupt Qajar Dynasty in 1921. Though the intent was originally to proclaim a republic, pressure from the conservative clergy (who feared being left out of any republican power structure) convinced now Prime Minister Reza Khan to crown himself Reza Shah Pahlavi. Strongly authoritarian and nationalistic, Reza Shah soon began a vigorous program of industrialization and secular reform, establishing universities, improving infrastructure, establishing public education, laying the foundations for a modern, secular Iranian state. Just as important as modernization and secularizing, however, was his determination that Persia maintain its independence in the face of Soviet expansion and British interests in his country's oil reserves. In 1937 Persia entered into a regional alliance known as the Saadabad Pact along with other neutral countries of the region, namely Turkey, Iraq, and Afghanistan. With the outbreak of hostilities in Europe the new Trans-Iranian railway could be a tempting target for the allies, should the Soviet Union ever be in need of supply.
column5: Tras derrocar a la dinastía Qajar en 1921, el oficial Reza Kan se coronó como el sah Reza Pahlaví, impulsando un ambicioso proyecto nacionalista, secular y autoritario para modernizar Irán. Salvaguardando celosamente sus vastos recursos petroleros frente a la injerencia británica y soviética, en 1939 Teherán ampara su seguridad en el Pacto de Saadabad junto a otras naciones islámicas neutrales. Sin embargo, la guerra europea amenaza con convertir sus líneas ferroviarias en un objetivo vital para el suministro logístico de las grandes potencias.

column2: The new government of Persia is under British control, but the Soviets still hold much of the north. With the Soviet Union marching to war, can Persia withstand the onslaught - and win back its lands from Stalin's grasp?
column5: Invadida conjuntamente por fuerzas británicas y soviéticas para asegurar su ruta de suministros durante el conflicto mundial, la administración iraní se halla bajo el estricto control de Londres, mientras el Ejército Rojo rehúsa evacuar las provincias del norte. Ante la repentina guerra entre los Aliados y Moscú, Irán lucha por recuperar su plena soberanía territorial de las garras de Stalin.
