column5: Sinkiang fue una pieza clave en el «Gran Juego» anglo-ruso por el dominio de Asia Central. Durante el siglo XIX, los tratados desiguales forzaron a la corte Qing a ceder territorios y conceder consulados a Rusia. Tras el aplastamiento de la revuelta de Yaqub Beg en 1877 y la resolución del conflicto del valle del Ilí en San Petersburgo, la región fue anexada formalmente como provincia en 1884. Sin embargo, el anhelo autonomista de la población túrquica persistió, desembocando en 1933 en la proclamación en Kashgar de la efímera República del Turquestán Oriental frente a la tutela del señor de la guerra Sheng Shicai.

column2: In 1938, the Sudetenland was allocated to Germany by the Munich Dictat, the Vienna Arbitrage allocated the southern parts of Slovakia to Hungary, Poland claimed smaller parts of northern Slovakia, and Slovakia and Sub-Carpathian Ukraine acquired autonomy in a delimited Czechoslovakia. However this situation was short-lived. Under Hitler's pressure, on 14 March 1939, the autonomous Parliament proclaimed the independent Slovak State headed by Jozef Tiso. It was soon re-named the Slovak Republic. The new state's foreign policy and economy was heavily dependent on Nazi Germany, which also limited its domestic policy. This totalitarian regime was dependent on the government of one political party, one ideology and the principle of one leader. On the other hand, the outbreak of war aided the growth of the economy. New cultural, scientific and education institutions, such as today's Slovak Academy of Science and the Slovak Technical University, were established.
column5: Los Acuerdos de Múnich de 1938 y el Primer Arbitraje de Viena desmembraron Checoslovaquia, otorgando el sur eslovaco a Hungría y partes septentrionales a Polonia. Bajo directa coacción alemana, el parlamento de Bratislava proclamó el 14 de marzo de 1939 el Estado Eslovaco independiente bajo el mando del monseñor Jozef Tiso. Subordinada económica y diplomáticamente a Berlín, la nueva república adoptó un régimen de partido único y corte autoritario. Pese a su sumisión al Tercer Reich, el esfuerzo bélico reactivó la industria y se fundaron las principales instituciones científicas y técnicas de la nación.

column2: Seeing the continuing discrimination of their people under the double monarchy of Austria-Hungary Slovakian politicians and intellectuals were convinced that only joining with the Czechs would lead the way out of their national misery. Representatives of immigrated Slovaks in the U.S.A. agreed with the Czech nationalists Thomás Garrigue Masaryk and Eduard Benes on a united state of the Czechs and the Slovaks. This new country was proclaimed as independent republic by the name of Czechoslovakia in Prague 1918. After over 1000 years of foreign rule the Slovaks, making up around 30 percent of the total Czechoslovakian population together with the Czechs as equals in an autonomous state. But soon unrest stirred about the predominance of the Czechs which found, among others, its expression in the establishing of centralized strcutures. Main power of the anti-Czech resistance was the catholic conservative Slovakian People's Party (SPP), calling for extensive autonomy. When after trhe Munich Treaty of 1938 Czechoslovakia the Sudeten regions were ceded to Germany the SPP seized the opportunity and exploited the acute weakness of the government in Prague and achieved a federalization of Czechoslovakia. In March 1939 Germany broke the Munich Treaty and occupied the Czeck part of the country, turning it into the 'Reichsprotektorat Böhmen und Mähren' (Protectorate Bohemia and Moravia). A day earlier, by call of Adolf Hitler, Slovakia had declared her independence. Formally independent, Slovakia was de facto a vassall of Germany, although the new country was recognized by 25 statesm among the Great Britain, France, and the Soviet Union. The government of Prime Minister Jozef Tisos, a catholic priest, followed, under close watch from Berlin, a conservative authoritarian policy.
column5: Tras siglos bajo dominio de la Corona húngara, los líderes eslovacos pactaron en 1918 fundar Checoslovaquia junto a Masaryk y Beneš. No obstante, el rígido centralismo de Praga marginó a la población eslovaca (un 30 por ciento del Estado), impulsando el auge del conservador Partido Popular Eslovaco en su lucha por la autonomía. Tras la crisis de Múnich en 1938, el desmoronamiento de la autoridad central propició una federación transitoria. En marzo de 1939, bajo la presión directa del Tercer Reich, Bratislava proclamó su independencia formal bajo el gobierno autoritario y católico de Jozef Tiso, quedando constituida de facto como Estado satélite de Alemania.

column2: The Great War was a disaster for Russia. Outfought on the front lines, the real defeat came from within, as the economy crumbled, factories stood idle and the people starved in the streets. The Tsar's government, no longer able to command the loyalty of the army or people, collapsed. However, the well-meaning liberal politicians who followed were equally unable to cope with the crisis. Only the radical parties of the far Left, with their simple slogan of 'Peace, land and bread', seemed to offer a solution. Popular councils, or 'soviets', sprang up all over Russia to offer a self-government alternative to the official regime, and under their guidance the peasants began to seize and share out land from the local nobility, and the soldiers simply quit fighting and went home. In this turmoil, Lenin's Bolshevik party saw its opportunity to seize power and establish the world's first Communist state. Acting through the soviets and in their name, they legitimised the land seizures and, to many Russians, seemed to offer the best hope of a truly fair, effective and popular government. Others, however, took note of the Bolsheviks' unwillingness to share power and their hostility to dissent, and accused them of corrupting the ideals of socialism and democracy. Challenged from the left by these democratic Greens, and from the right by the liberal and monarchist Whites, the Reds would face a long and bloody struggle to establish who would control the destiny of Russia - and, perhaps, the world.
column5: La Gran Guerra causó el desmoronamiento de Rusia. La derrota en el frente y la ruina económica precipitaron la caída del zarismo. El gobierno provisional liberal fue incapaz de aplacar el descontento, abriendo paso a la agitación bolchevique bajo el lema de «Paz, pan y tierra». Organizados en sóviets de obreros y soldados, los revolucionarios de Lenin asaltaron el poder en octubre de 1917, legitimando el reparto agrario e instaurando el primer régimen comunista de la historia. Enfrentados en una brutal guerra civil a las tropas contrarrevolucionarias Blancas y a la insurgencia campesina Verde, los Bolcheviques deberán combatir a sangre y fuego para consolidar el control sobre el antiguo imperio.

column2: Formerly known as the Empire of Russia, the Soviet Union is a conglomerate of four Soviets formed in the aftermath of the Great War. Weakened by German invasion and post-war revolutions, the Bolsheviks under Vladimir Lenin consolidated its hold over the Soviet Duma, turning what was once a multi Soviet party republic into an one party authoritarian rule. Thankfully, Lenin was a capable and pragmatic ruler. He recognized the need for private enterprise to exist alongside government spending and started the New Economic Plan. While capitalist countries suffered during the Great Depression, the USSR managed to expand and managed for the first time to provide electricity through the entire country. The next leader of the USSR would prove to be a mixed blessing. While managing to rapidly industrialize an otherwise rural country, Stalin's Five Year Plans abandoned the New Economic Policy and reversed many of Lenin's achievements. Millions died to famine in the years that ensued while the new Stalinist faction slowly purged dissidents who were once old friends. Now, with her hold over the country firm and empowered to spread communism abroad, Stalinist Russia looks west toward disillusioned communists within Germany and east toward in hopes of a communist China.
column5: La Unión Soviética surgió de la victoria bolchevique tras la Gran Guerra y la invasión extranjera. Lenin consolidó la hegemonía del Partido Comunista y estabilizó la economía mediante la NEP, facilitando la electrificación y la recuperación agraria mientras Occidente caía en la Gran Depresión. Tras sucederle, Stalin impuso la colectivización forzosa y los Planes Quinquenales, industrializando a marchas forzadas a un país eminentemente agrario a costa de devastadoras hambrunas y severas purgas políticas. Con el poder central afianzado con puño de hierro, Moscú vigila con atención a los comunistas descontentos en Alemania y alienta el avance revolucionario en el Extremo Oriente.

column2: No other nation suffered such domestic political turmoil as Russia during the Great War, which saw the ancient throne of the Romanov Tsars toppled and the vast empire of Peter the Great and Alexander II fall into the hands of a mass revolutionary movement  the Bolshevik Marxists of Vladimir Illych Lenin. Renamed the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics (USSR), the country was rededicated to the spread of revolutionary communist ideology across the world, making it a pariah amongst the decadent capitalist economies of Europe. After Lenin's death and a series of behind-the-scenes intrigues, his lieutenant Josef Stalin emerged as the heir to the Bolshevik legacy. By a ferocious policy of industrialization and an equally uncompromising attitude towards political foes, Stalin consolidated his position as supreme ruler of the USSR and returned the once-battered and ignored Russian state to the diplomatic table as a major power. But many strategic dilemmas continue to haunt him. The surprise rapprochement with Communism's bitterest ideological foe, Nazi Germany, gives the USSR a chance to expand in Eastern Europe while Hitler is busy fighting the British and French. But whether this artificial peace can be sustained for long is questionable. And never forget Japan, far to the East.
column5: La caída de la dinastía Románov en 1917 situó a Rusia en el centro de la revolución bolchevique guiada por Lenin. Tras su muerte, Iósif Stalin consolidó la jefatura absoluta del Estado mediante una feroz industrialización pesada y la sistemática purga del aparato estatal y militar. En vísperas de 1939, la URSS ha recuperado su estatus de superpotencia en el tablero diplomático internacional. El pacto de no agresión suscrito con el Tercer Reich brinda una tregua estratégica para expandir las fronteras soviéticas en Europa del Este mientras las potencias capitalistas combaten entre sí, aunque la sombra de una invasión nazi y la amenaza militar japonesa en Manchuria siguen latentes.

column2: When Molotov brokered his surprise deal with his German counterpart von Ribbentrop in the summer of 1939 few observers expected the unnatural partnership between the Nazis and the Soviets to last for long. Indeed Stalin saw the non-aggression treaty as a breathing space which he could use to build up his military forces and expand his territorial buffer zone in Eastern Europe. But while the USSR took over the Baltic States and large parts of Romania without difficulty, Finland's stubborn resistance against overwhelming Russian opposition in the 'Winter War' of 1939-1940 humiliated the Red Army, and Germany's faster-than-expected triumph in France left Stalin's timetable of rearmament lagging dangerously behind. Now June 1941, Hitler has unleashed a massive massive continent-wide onslaught stunning Stalin and the Red Army. Can Red Army overcome the disastrous effects of the purges? Will General Winter come to the rescue again? Will the New Soviet Man rally around Mother Russia and turn the tide?
column5: En el verano de 1939, el Pacto Ribbentrop-Mólotov concedió a Stalin un valioso margen temporal para ocupar los Estados Bálticos, Besarabia y levantar un cordón de seguridad en Europa Oriental. Sin embargo, la agónica campaña en Finlandia durante la Guerra de Invierno evidenció las graves secuelas de las purgas en el Ejército Rojo, mientras la fulgurante victoria alemana en Francia dejó desfasado el calendario del rearme soviético. En junio de 1941, las divisiones acorazadas del Eje desencadenan la Operación Barbarroja. Desbordado en el frente, el mando soviético debe resistir el embate y movilizar todos sus recursos humanos e industriales para salvar a la Patria.

column2: It is the third year in the 'Great Patriotic War', as it would be referred to later. Following up on the victories at Moscow, Stalingrad and Kursk, the Red Army has swept the fascists out of the Ukraine and is now preparing to liberate the last sections of Mother Russia from German occupation. But it is clear that Stalin will not be content with anything but the ultimate conquest of Berlin and Germany, carrying the war into all of eastern and central Europe. Can the Red Army overcome the Wehrmacht's very best in the East and beat the Western Allies to the conquest of Berlin, and then Germany? Will the Red Banner of Communism fly over Europe? Only time will tell.
column5: En el tercer año de la Gran Guerra Patria, tras los decisivos triunfos defensivos y operativos en Moscú, Stalingrado y el saliente de Kursk, el Ejército Rojo ha expulsado a la Wehrmacht de Ucrania y se prepara para limpiar de ocupantes el suelo patrio. Los planes del Stavka van mucho más allá de las fronteras de 1941: Stalin pretende empujar las líneas del frente a través de Europa Central y Oriental hasta forzar la capitulación incondicional en Berlín. Con una aplastante masa de blindados y artillería, la maquinaria bélica soviética compite frente a los Aliados occidentales por definir el nuevo orden territorial del continente.

column2: On May 8, 1945, Germany surrendered, bringing to a close the Great Patriotic War. The Potsdam Conference (July 17 to August 2, 1945) attempted to confront the delicate balance of power of the opposing governmental structures, democracy and communism. However despite the agreement on the partitioning of Germany and the call for an unconditional surrender of Japan, the conference did nothing to quell the increasing tensions between the Western Allies and the Soviets. The Red Army's attack on Manchuria sealed the fate of Japan, and the surrender documents were signed on the USS Missouri on September 2nd, 1945. Realizing the power of the Red Army vastly outweighed the American and British forces, and due in part to the provocative stationing of B-29 bombers with atomic weapons in Turkey, Stalin launched a bold bid to liberate Western Europe from the yoke of imperialism on October 2nd, 1945. Can the Red Army be victorious? Will the many communists in the West rise up to support the liberation? Will Stalin's gambit to strike before the US can ramp up the production of A-Bombs prove correct?
column5: La capitulación del Tercer Reich puso fin a la Gran Guerra Patria, pero la Conferencia de Potsdam evidenció la fractura irreconciliable entre la URSS y los Aliados occidentales. Tras la fulgurante campaña de Manchuria que forzó el fin del Imperio japonés, las tensiones geopolíticas alcanzaron un punto de ruptura ante el despliegue estratégico aliado de bombarderos nucleares en Turquía. Amparado en la colosal superioridad convencional y acorazada del Ejército Rojo en Europa Central, Moscú lanza una ofensiva general para desalojar a las potencias imperialistas del Rin antes de que el arsenal atómico estadounidense incline la balanza.

column2: No other nation suffered such domestic political turmoil as Russia during the Great War, which saw the ancient throne of the Romanov Tsars toppled and the vast empire of Peter the Great and Alexander II fall into the hands of a mass revolutionary movement , the Bolshevik Marxists of Vladimir Illych Lenin. Renamed the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics (USSR), the country was rededicated to the spread of revolutionary communist ideology across the world, making it a pariah amongst the decadent capitalist economies of Europe. After Lenin's death and a series of behind-the-scenes intrigues, his lieutenant Josef Stalin emerged as the heir to the Bolshevik legacy. By a ferocious policy of industrialization and an equally uncompromising attitude towards political foes, Stalin has by 1936 consolidated his position as supreme ruler of the USSR and returned the once-battered and ignored Russian state to the diplomatic table as a major power. But many strategic dilemmas haunt him. Should Russia seek to expand into the lost territories of Eastern Europe, or strike southwards to the blue waters of the Indian Ocean? Can a deal be brokered with the British and French - or even Hitler and Mussolini? What of the Japanese and their designs?
column5: Tras el colapso del Imperio zarista en la Gran Guerra y el triunfo bolchevique, Lenin fundó la Unión Soviética como baluarte de la revolución obrera internacional. Hacia 1936, Stalin ha afianzado su mando supremo indiscutible mediante una brutal política de colectivización forzosa, industrialización pesada y depuración de rivales políticos. Restaurada como una temida potencia en el tablero diplomático, el Kremlin encara dilemas estratégicos decisivos: reivindicar las tierras perdidas en Europa del Este, avanzar hacia el Índico, buscar entendimientos temporales con las potencias capitalistas o blindar el Extremo Oriente frente al expansionismo militar japonés.

column2: In 1898 Spain lost the Spanish-American War, and with it much of her colonial empire. Cuba, the main battleground, gained her independence, Puerto Rico, Guam and the Philippines were ceded to the USA (Treaty of Paris, 1898), the Spanish claim over the Marianas (except Guam) and Carolina Islands sold to Germany. Spain only held on to her African colonies. Spain, having century-old outposts in Morocco, played a role in the Moroccan crises: the country hosted the Algericas Conference and gained three stretches of Moroccan territory as well as the northern part of the Spanish Sahara. In the 1890s Spain found itself in a political crisis. The Canovite System with government-controlled elections insuring the regular alternation of liberal and conservative cabinets ('dynastic politicians') showed signs of breaking up. The political movements denied fair competition voiced their demands for participation in the political process on equal terms or for another change of the constitution. The PSOE (Socialist Party) had been founded in 1879. The Basque Nationalist Party was founded in 1894, the Catalan Lliga Regionalista in 1901, the Republicans formed an electoral alliance in 1903 which turned into the Reformist Party in 1912. King Alfonso XIII. (1902-1931) was not satisfied with the function of a figurehead and used the powers granted to the king by the constitution of 1876, by repeatedly forcing a government to resign etc. Spain saw a succession of short-lived cabinets. In 1906 an attempt to assassinate the king failed. In 1914 Spain no longer was a major political power. The country did not feature in the various alliance systems that preceded World War I, while countries such as Italy, Bulgaria and Rumania were wooed by Europe's military powers as potential partners. Spanish Public opinion was split between the 2 alliances: the more conservative elements were Germanophiles, the leftist organizations Francophiles. Prime Minister Dato hoped to keep the country neutral in any conflict, as Spain had grown politically unstable and militarily weak. But storm clouds over Europe were looming…
column5: El desastre de 1898 desmanteló el imperio colonial español con la pérdida de Cuba, Puerto Rico y Filipinas en el Tratado de París, vendiéndose las Carolinas y Marianas a Alemania. En el interior, el turnismo canovista de conservadores y liberales muestra signos de agotamiento frente al auge de fuerzas periféricas, republicanas y del movimiento obrero. El rey Alfonso XIII interviene activamente en la vida política forzando frecuentes crisis de gobierno. En el plano militar, la sangría del Protectorado de Marruecos polariza a la sociedad. En 1914, con un ejército mal pertrechado e inestabilidad social, el presidente Dato proclama la neutralidad estricta ante el estallido de la guerra europea.

column2: The Spanish confidence was badly shaken after the war against the U.S.A. in which the colonies of Cuba, Puerto Rico, the Philippines, and Guam were lost. Seperatist movements like those of the Basques or the Catalans gained support, the church interfered in politics, and a radical workers movement destabalized the balance between conservatives and liberals. After taking the governmentin 1902 Alfons XIII showed expansionist tendencies as demonstrated by the intervention in Morocco.. The Algeciras Act of 1906 did acknowledge Spanish interests in Morocco, institutionalized by a protectorate over the north and south of the African country in 1912, but it became a source of permanent unrest. During World War 1 Spain remained neutral. After 1918 the social tensions erupted in a number of revolts by the rural populace and right wing as well as anarchistic factions. Alfons XIII supported the military coup against the government by General Miguel Primo de Rivera who abolished the constitution of 1876 and installed a dictatorial rule between 1923 and 1930. He ended the uprising in Morocco with a victory over Abd el-Krim in 1926, but could not master the economic crisis and had to resign after repeated revolts by the military and students. In 1931 Alfons XIII also abdicated and allowed the Liberal Conservative Niceto Alcalá Zamora y Torres the proclamation of the Second Republic.The republic, however, could not overcome the deep rift between the factions of the Spanish society, reaching from fascist Falangists to monarchists, conservative liberals, left liberals, socialists, communists and Anarcho-Syndicalists. And so, in 1936 the shadow of civil war loom over the Iberian country The differences eventually led to the Spanish Civil War which erupted in 1936. The National Front went into armed conflict against the elected People's Front government. Francisco Franco y Bahamondeled the National Front and united the catholic traditionalists and the Falangists with his faction. In 1939 Franco achieved - supported militarily by both Germany and Italy - victory over the People's Front who had been favored by the USSR and Mexico and who had signed up the aid of the International Brigades of Republicans, Socialists, and Communists from all over the world..
column5: Tras el Desastre del 98 y el colapso del turnismo, la dictadura de Primo de Rivera y la posterior abdicación de Alfonso XIII desembocaron en 1931 en la Segunda República. La fractura social entre las clases tradicionales y el obrerismo radical frustró la estabilidad parlamentaria. En julio de 1936, una sublevación militar respaldada por tradicionalistas y falangistas inició la sangrienta Guerra Civil Española. Apoyado militarmente por la Legión Cóndor alemana y el Corpo Truppe Volontarie italiano, el general Francisco Franco se alzó con la victoria en abril de 1939 frente a las fuerzas republicanas respaldadas por la Unión Soviética y las Brigadas Internacionales.

column2: Franco joined the Anti-Comintern Pact on 7th April 1938 but declared the neutrality of Spain on the outbreak of the Second World War. Adolf Hitler had tried hard to get Franco to change his mind. In their negotiations Franco demanded that in any postwar settlement he wanted control of Gibraltar, French Morocco, a portion of Algeria including Oran, and parts of Africa. Franco's main demand was that Germany had to fully compensate Spain for the cost of any British blockade of the country. Hitler was in no position to take on this burden and the negotiations came to an end. However, Franco did agree to provide logistical and intelligence support and promised to send a volunteer force, the Spanish Blue Division, to help the fight against communism in Europe. After the defeat of France in May 1940, Adolf Hitler resumed negotiations with Franco. The two men met at Hendaye on 23rd October 1940. Hitler's main request was for his troops to travel through Spain to link up with an airborne assault on Gibraltar. Franco, who believed that Germany would not win a long war, refused. Now with the crusade against communism in the east, should Spain continue to remain neutral?
column5: Tras unirse al Pacto Antikomintern, España proclamó la no beligerancia al estallar el conflicto mundial. En la conferencia de Hendaya en octubre de 1940, Franco rechazó autorizar el paso de tropas de la Wehrmacht para el asalto a Gibraltar (Operación Félix), exigiendo desmesuradas compensaciones coloniales en el norte de África y masivos suministros que Alemania no podía costear. Aunque escéptico sobre la victoria nazi en una contienda prolongada, el régimen franquista prestó apoyo diplomático, facilitó minerales estratégicos al Eje y autorizó el despliegue del contingente voluntario de la División Azul en el frente oriental frente a la Unión Soviética.

column2: Generalissimo Franco walked a careful path through the war in Europe, but now the Soviet Union threatens to push aside the Allies. Will Spain take part in the fight against Communism?
column5: Habiendo mantenido un delicado equilibrio diplomático para eludir la conflagración europea, el general Franco observa con aprensión el colapso del Eje y la arrolladora penetración del Ejército Rojo en Europa Central. Ante la reactivación del choque armado entre la Unión Soviética y las potencias occidentales, España se debate entre romper su aislamiento internacional apoyando la lucha contra el comunismo o preservar una neutralidad férrea frente a una conflagración abierta.

La inestabilidad política, las revueltas obreras y la sangría colonial en el Rif precipitaron la dictadura militar de Primo de Rivera en 1923. Su colapso forzó en 1931 la proclamación pacífica de la Segunda República. Sin embargo, la virulenta polarización política entre fuerzas de izquierda y los sectores reaccionarios, monárquicos y tradicionalistas paralizó al parlamento. A comienzos de 1936, la victoria electoral del Frente Popular y la agitación social sitúan a España al borde de una inminente guerra fratricida.

column5: La crisis del Desastre de 1898 aceleró la descomposición del régimen de la Restauración. Tras el fracaso del directorio militar de Primo de Rivera y la renuncia de Alfonso XIII, en abril de 1931 se proclamó la Segunda República bajo la presidencia de Alcalá-Zamora. El nuevo régimen emprendió ambiciosas reformas militares, educativas y agrarias, chocando frontalmente con la oposición conservadora, la jerarquía eclesiástica y la polarización insurreccional sindicalista. En 1936, tras el triunfo electoral del Frente Popular y una creciente espiral de atentados y huelgas, la República encara la inminente amenaza de una sublevación militar generalizada.

column2: In the 18th Century Sweden dreamed of a Unified Scandinavia ruled from their capital, Stockholm. However, the last century shattered Sweden's dream - In 1809 they lost control of Finland to Russia, but a United Scandinavia was considered a reality again when five years later Denmark was compelled to cede Norway to Sweden. The Norwegians were not happy with this union however, and a rebellion began in 1878. Finally the Norwegians capped decades of sedition by breaking away in 1905. By 1914, the Swedish government has granted extensive suffrage for men, but women remain disenfranchised. While the Social Democrats are on the ascendancy, the bourgeoisie and middling classes attempt to stop their reforms, and as 1914 dawns, Sweden must choose between neutrality and relative obscurity or to take sides in an increasingly polarised Europe. The Germans have secretly promised Finland in the event of war, but questions remain as to whether the public will support Sweden's entry into what could be a devastating war.
column5: Tras la cesión forzosa de Finlandia a Rusia en 1809 y la posterior disolución pacífica de la unión personal con Noruega en 1905, el sueño escandinavista sueco se disolvió. Para 1914, el país goza de estabilidad parlamentaria con un sufragio masculino extendido y el auge progresivo de la socialdemocracia frente a las élites tradicionales. Ante la inminente conflagración europea, Estocolmo afronta una difícil elección: preservar una estricta política de neutralidad comercial o alinearse discretamente con el Imperio alemán a cambio de promesas territoriales sobre Finlandia, arriesgándose a un conflicto destructivo en el Báltico.

column2: In 1818 Karl XIV Johan was crowned the first king of the still ruling house of Bernadotte. Neutrality became the guideline of Swedish freign policy from then on. Even though Oskar I (1844 - 1859) supported Denmark in her first war against the German Leage (1848 - 1850) Sweden insisted on its neutrality during the Crimean War (1853 - 1856) and the 2nd German-Danish War of 1864 which allowed for the country's unhindered developmen into a parliamentary democracy. In 1865/66 a bicameral system was introduced and a Liberal cabinet was established in 1905. In 1909 Gustav V (1907 - 1950) acknowledged universal suffrage for the Second Chamber of parliament, eventually making Sweden a constitutional monarchy. The union with Norway broke in 1905, defeating the idea of a panscandinavian state which had especially been envisioned by Karl XV (1859 - 1872). During World War I (1914 - 1918) Sweden remained neutral and became the starting point of many peace efforts, particularly from the socialist side. The Social Democrats became the strongest party in 1920 and foraged the government numerous times till 1936. Under the impact of the Great Depression which reached in 1931/32 even the highly advanced Swedish agriculture and industry a welfare state was created which became a rolemodel for most of Western Europe.
column5: Con la entronización de la dinastía Bernadotte en 1818, la neutralidad armada se convirtió en el principio rector de la política exterior sueca, manteniéndose al margen de las guerras germano-danesas y de la Primera Guerra Mundial. Consolidada plenamente como una monarquía parlamentaria tras aprobar el sufragio universal en 1909 y disolver pacíficamente la unión con Noruega, Suecia vivió el predominio político del Partido Socialdemócrata. Ante la Gran Depresión de los años 30, el Estado forjó un avanzado modelo de bienestar y cohesión social, combinando una sólida industria siderúrgica con una firme política de coexistencia pacífica.

column2: Syria, geographically, stretched from Gaza to Alexandretta on the Mediterranean and was limited to its east by nomadic desert with rugged mountains dividing a costal strip from a wide inland plain. With a temperate climate on the coast, the population here were more affluent than those inland – a main component of the population here was the community of Ansariya, disciples of a cult of fertility, pagan-like, anti-foreign, distrustful of Islam, drawn at moments towards Christians by common persecution. Amongst these were colonies of Christians, with the territory between Beirut and Tripoli populated by Maronites and Greeks and further to the east, semi-nomadic people. The northern areas of the country, from Alexandretta to Aleppo were populated by a significant number of Armenians, Druses, Circassians and Kurds also residing in sizeable communities, with Aleppo itself a kaleidoscope of multiculturalism. Southwards, near Acre the inhabitants were a mix of Sunni Arabs, Druses and Metawala. On the banks of the Jordan valley inland live bitterly-suspicious colonies of Algerian refugees, facing villages of Jews, who came from a broad and varied background – many were more traditional in culture and Orthodox in religion, others being newcomers to the region, introducing European practices to the region. In settled Syria there was no indigenous political entity larger than the village, in patriarchal Syria nothing more complex than the clan. All higher constitution took the guise of the imported bureau-system of the Turkish Empire, which had been established and strengthened over centuries of rule. With the Ottomans now weakened, many in Syria see opportunity: Muslims mostly want an Arab kingdom, whilst Catholics largely yearn for European protection. Many simply want autonomy for Syria, yet sharp divisions ensure that while an ultimate objective was conceptualised, their only common trait is hatred of the Turks. While the people of Syria struggle for freedom, the Turks, French and British alike seek dominion over the region.
column5: La Gran Siria otomana se extendía desde la costa levantina hasta el Éufrates, albergando un mosaico complejo de confesiones suníes, drusas, alauíes, kurdas y cristianas maronitas y ortodoxas, organizadas en redes comunales y clanes locales bajo la rígida estructura administrativa de la Sublime Puerta. Con el declive progresivo del Imperio otomano en vísperas de 1914, las élites urbanas y los clanes árabes reclaman un reino independiente, mientras las comunidades cristianas buscan la protección de las potencias europeas. Entretanto, Gran Bretaña y Francia maniobran discretamente para imponer su tutela colonial sobre toda la cuenca del Levante.

column2: Following the collapse of the Ottoman Empire after World War I an independent Arab Kingdom of Syria was established under King Faysal. However, his rule over Syria ended in July 1920 when French forces entered Syria to impose their League of Nations mandate. After the Vichy government assumed power in France in 1940, the Vichy government controlled Syria. The Vichy government's control ended when its forces were unable to halt the advance of British and Free French troops into Lebanon and Syria. The entry of Allied troops brought a promise from the Free French leader, General Charles de Gaulle, of eventual independence. During 1944 the Syrian government took over some of the internal governmental functions. The United States and the Soviet Union and other governments recognized Syria's independence. The Allied nations pressured France to evacuate Syria to no avail. When will Syria truly be free?
column5: Tras el colapso del Imperio otomano en 1918, se formó el efímero Reino Árabe de Siria bajo Faysal I, aplastado en julio de 1920 por las tropas francesas para imponer el Mandato de la Sociedad de Naciones. En 1940 el control pasó al régimen de Vichy, hasta que fuerzas británicas y de la Francia Libre expulsaron a los leales al Eje en 1941, garantizando De Gaulle una futura soberanía. Pese al reconocimiento formal por parte de Washington y Moscú en 1944 y a la transferencia de competencias civiles a Damasco, las autoridades francesas se resisten a una evacuación militar definitiva, prolongando la lucha por una autodeterminación real.

column2: Tannu Tuva has long been involved in a complicated relationship between Russia and China.  First occupied by by Dzhungar Khan Galdan in 1688, the land came under Mongol rule.  In 1758 when Dzhungaria was defeated by the Chinese the territory was under the dominion of Manchuria. During the middle 19th century, because of mutual interest of Tannu Tuva and Russia, the Tuvans began to allow Russian merchants to trade duty free.  In the late 1800s tensions rose as the Tuvans began a series of rebellions against their rulers. After the fall of the Tsin Empire in China Tannu Tuva moved to liberate itself from Chinese rule.  Knowing that as a small and weak nation they could not expect to remain independent they sought the protection of Russia, becoming a Russian protectorate in 1914.  After the Russian Revolution the Attorney of the Siberian revolutionary committee of RSFSR I.G. Safianov declared that 'Now the Soviet government considers Uryankhai (Tuva) independent as before' and in August 1921 the Peoples Republic of Tannu Tuva was formed.  The small nation in the center of Asia was primarily an agrarian society with little industry (mostly coal and gold mining).  The nation also maintained close ties with the Soviet government.
column5: Situada en el corazón montañoso de Asia, Tuvá osciló históricamente entre la influencia china y rusa tras el colapso del janato de Zungaria. Tras la caída de la dinastía Qing en 1911, los líderes tuvanos buscaron la protección de San Petersburgo, formalizándose el Protectorado del Krai de Urianjái en 1914. Con el triunfo de los bolcheviques en la guerra civil rusa, en agosto de 1921 se proclamó la República Popular de Tannu Tuvá bajo auspicio soviético. Siendo una nación predominantemente ganadera y con una minería incipiente, su gobierno opera como un Estado satélite fuertemente alineado con las directrices políticas y de seguridad de Moscú.

column2: The Manchus who conquered China and established the Qing dynasty in the seventeenth century embraced Tibetan Buddhism as the Mongols had and developed close ties with the Tibetans. The Dalai Lama who had by then become the spiritual and temporal ruler of Tibet agreed to become the spiritual guide of the Manchu emperor. He accepted patronage and protection in exchange. This priest-patron relationship which the Dalai Lama also maintained with numerous Mongol Khans and Tibetan nobles was the only formal tie that existed between the Tibetans and Manchus during the Qing dynasty. It did not in itself affect Tibet`s independence. On the political level some powerful Manchu emperors succeeded in exerting a degree of influence over Tibet. Thus between I720 and I792 the Manchu emperors Kangxi Yong Zhen and Qianlong sent imperial troops into Tibet four times to protect the Dalai Lama and the Tibetan people from foreign invasion or internal unrest. It was these expeditions that provided them with influence in Tibet. The emperor sent representatives to the Tibetan capital Lhasa some of whom successfully exercised their influence in his name over the Tibetan government particularly with respect to the conduct of foreign relations. At the height of Manchu power that lasted a few decades the situation was not unlike that which can exist between a superpower and a neighbouring satellite or protectorate. The subjection of a state to foreign influence and even intervention in foreign or domestic affairs however significant this may be politically does not in itself entail the legal extinction of that state. Consequently although some Manchu emperors exerted considerable influence over Tibet they did not thereby incorporate Tibet into their empire much less China. Manchu influence did not last for very long. It was entirely ineffective by the time the British briefly invaded Tibet in 1904 and ceased entirely with the overthrow of the Qing dynasty in 1911 and its replacement in China by a native republican government. Whatever ties existed between the Dalai Lama and the Qing emperor were extinguished with the dissolution of the Manchu Empire. From 1911 on Tibet successfully avoided undue foreign influence and behaved in every respect as a fully independent state. The 13th Dalai Lama emphasized his country's independent status externally in formal communications to foreign rulers and internally by issuing a proclamation reaffirming Tibet's independence and by strengthening the country's defences. The attitude of most foreign governments with whom Tibet maintained relations implied their recognition of Tibet's independent status.
column5: Durante la dinastía Qing se forjó un vínculo de «sacerdote y protector» entre el Dalái Lama y los emperadores manchúes, quienes intervinieron militarmente en el siglo XVIII para repeler invasiones sin suprimir la soberanía tibetana. Con la decadencia imperial, confirmada tras la expedición británica de 1904 y el colapso Qing de 1911, todo nexo formal quedó extinguido. El decimotercer Dalái Lama expulsó a las tropas imperiales, proclamó la independencia y reforzó las fronteras de Lhasa, operando desde entonces como un Estado soberano de facto frente a la naciente e inestable República de China.

column5: El vínculo histórico entre el Tíbet y la dinastía manchú de los Qing se basó en el acuerdo de tutela y padrinazgo espiritual, sin anular la identidad jurídica del Estado teocrático. Tras el derrocamiento de los Qing en 1911, el 13.º Dalái Lama proclamó la total independencia nacional y expulsó a los representantes imperiales. Aunque la Convención de Simla de 1914 intentó fijar fronteras formales con la India británica, el gobierno republicano chino rechazó ratificarla, manteniendo vivas sus reclamaciones sobre el territorio tibetano mientras Lhasa ejerce un autogobierno indiscutible.

column2: Following World War One the territory of the defeated Ottoman Empire had been reduced to Anatolia in the peace treaty of SŠvres 1920. Mustafa Kemal organised the national resistance against foreign invaders bringing about a major victory over the Greek in 1922 after which the Peace of SŠvres was revised and Turkey was granted control of the (de-militarized) Bosporus. After the last Sultan had been deposed and the capital had been moved to Ankara the Republic of Turkey was proclaimed on October 29th 1923. Kemal who would begin calling himself Atatrk (Father of the Turks) from 1934 on began a cultural reform moving towards nationalist instead of religious ideals and abolishing the Caliphate in 1924. A year later a Kurdish uprising was brutally suppressed and Kemal disposed of all dangerous opposition during that time. Kemal's reforms were aimed at removing the old elite and patterns of power. Islam was no longer state religion by constitution the Latin alphabet was introduced as well as the international calendar and time system. A code of laws was patterned after the Swiss civil law and the traditional Fez was no longer allowed to be worn. Economically the young state focused on industrialisation and the building up of a decent infrastructure. When the Great Depression caused an agricultural crisis in Turkey in 1929 Kemal steered a course self-sufficiency. In 1934 the first Five Year Plan introduced the era of planned economy. At first the young republic found a good friend in the Soviet Union who had been the only country to support the Anatolian independence movement. However when Turkey was allowed by international law to fortify the Bosporus and the Dardanelles the Western powers became more important especially Great Britain. Nevertheless an independent foreign policy remained a main goal for Kemal Atatrk. After the death of Atatrk in 1938 Ismet In'n became president. During the politcal crisis that kept growing Ankara remained neutral keeping an equal distance to both London and Berlin.
column5: Tras la derrota otomana y la partición del Tratado de Sèvres, Mustafa Kemal lideró la Guerra de Independencia turca, logrando la revisión de los términos en Lausana. Proclamada la República en 1923 con capital en Ankara, Atatürk transformó radicalmente la nación: abolió el califato, secularizó las instituciones, adoptó el alfabeto latino y emprendió la industrialización mediante planes quinquenales de corte autárquico. Tras su fallecimiento en 1938, el nuevo presidente Ismet Inönü mantiene una política exterior pragmática, preservando una estricta neutralidad entre las potencias occidentales y el Eje.

column2: In October 1939 Turkey signed a mutual assistance pact with France and United Kingdom which would spoil the friendly relations to the Soviet Union forever. When France was occupied in 1940 and Italy joined the war Turkey decided to stay neutral. In 1941 Hitler had conquered the Balkans and the agreement of Ankara to remain neutral secured Hitler's attack on the Soviet Union on that front. In June 1941 the non-aggression pact between Turkey and Germany was signed. So far Turkey's goal has been to stay neutral. Is this possible with Europe aflame?
column5: En octubre de 1939 Turquía suscribió un tratado de asistencia mutua con Gran Bretaña y Francia, enfriando sus relaciones históricas con Moscú. No obstante, la caída de Francia y la entrada bélica de Italia en 1940 reafirmaron la decisión de Ankara de preservar su neutralidad. Tras la ocupación alemana de Grecia y los Balcanes en la primavera de 1941, el presidente Inönü firmó un pacto de no agresión germano-turco apenas unos días antes del inicio de la Operación Barbarroja, buscando resguardar la soberanía nacional ante el avance de las hostilidades.

column2: As tensions in Europe heightened, Turkey kept neutral. The Molotov-Ribbentrop Pact of August 1939 prompted Turkey to sign a treaty of mutual assistance with Britain and France in October. Hedging its bets, the government concluded a nonaggression treaty with Nazi Germany on June 18, 1941, just four days before the Axis invasion of the Soviet Union. The early military successes of the Axis forces contributed to increased pro-German sentiment, even in some official circles. Despite German pressure, Turkey at no time permitted the passage of Axis troops, ships, or aircraft through or over Turkey and its waters, and the Montreux Convention was scrupulously enforced in the straits. Turkey broke diplomatic relations with Germany in August 1944, and, on February 23, 1945, declared war on Germany. Now Turkey is truly at war. Will the Allies reinforce Turkey? Can the Red Army be stopped?
column5: Durante la mayor parte del conflicto mundial, Turquía mantuvo una cautelosa no beligerancia, aplicando con firmeza la Convención de Montreux en los Estrechos e impidiendo el tránsito de tropas del Eje. Sin embargo, con el repliegue definitivo de Alemania, Ankara rompió lazos en 1944 y declaró la guerra a Berlín en febrero de 1945. Al concluir la lucha contra el Tercer Reich, la presencia masiva del Ejército Rojo en los Balcanes y las exigencias de Stalin sobre los Dardanelos colocan a Turquía bajo una directa amenaza estratégica, dependiendo del respaldo angloestadounidense.

column5: Tras la desintegración del Imperio otomano en 1918 y la anulación en combate del Tratado de Sèvres, Mustafa Kemal lideró la creación de la República de Turquía en 1923. Mediante un ambicioso programa secularizador y modernizador, Atatürk abolió el califato, suprimió el fez tradicional e implantó códigos jurídicos laicos de inspiración europea junto al alfabeto latino. Frente a la crisis agraria de la Gran Depresión, el Estado impulsó la industrialización nacional a través de su primer plan quinquenal estatista, manteniendo una prudente equidistancia diplomática entre la URSS y las potencias europeas.

column2: Four years after their crushing defeat, the French have hope again. With the landings by Allied forces in Normandy, the expulsion of the German oppressor from French soil seems now only a matter of time. But after the years of hardships and fighting from colonies and foreign soil, Free French forces under De Gaulle are determined to carry the war into Germany with their allies, to restore the honour of the French nation, and to get rid of Hitler and Nazism once and for all.
column5: Cuatro años después del desastre de 1940, la esperanza renace en Francia. Tras los desembarcos angloestadounidenses en Normandía y el posterior avance en el continente, el repliegue de las fuerzas del Eje del suelo patrio es inminente. Las divisiones de las Fuerzas Francesas Libres y del Ejército de África, conducidas por el general Charles de Gaulle, se aprestan a participar activamente en la liberación de París y empujar el frente militar hasta el corazón territorial de Alemania junto a sus aliados.

column2: In May of 1940 German forces attacked the Low Countries and then France. Their Blitzkrieg tactics succeeded in defeating the French and British armies in France. The British Expeditionary Force evacuated from Dunkirk leaving their heavy equipment behind, and the French government made a peace, which left the Germans in control of the North and the Vichy government in charge of the South. General Charles de Gaulle, a member of the French Cabinet in 1940, escaped from the German occupation in France. On June 18, 1940 De Gaulle spoke to the French people from London, via BBC radio. The British Cabinet had attempted to block the speech, but was over-ruled by Winston Churchill. De Gaulle asked French men and women to join in the fight against the Nazis. By the end of July that year, only 7,000 people had volunteered to join the Free French forces. Now in June 1941, Japan controls Indochina and France is a weak junior member of the Allies. Can France wrestle its overseas province from Vichy? When will metropolitan France be free again and what role will Free France play?
column5: En mayo de 1940, la ofensiva relámpago de la Wehrmacht colapsó el frente aliado, forzando la evacuación en Dunkerque y la rendición francesa. El mariscal Pétain estableció el régimen colaboracionista de Vichy, mientras el general Charles de Gaulle escapaba a Londres para emitir su histórico llamamiento del 18 de junio, fundando las Fuerzas Francesas Libres. En 1941, con escasos efectivos y su imperio colonial fracturado entre leales a Vichy y dominios ocupados por Japón, Francia Libre lucha por reagrupar apoyos en ultramar y legitimar su presencia entre los Aliados.

column2: At the end of the Great War, India remained the 'jewel in the crown' of the British Empire, and the Raj the consummate expression of its imperial ideology.  But the setting for the jewel was wearing thin and the ideology was no longer able to dominate in the way that it once had. The Raj, a territory encompassing the modern nations of India, Pakistan, Bangladesh and Myanmar, was born not from militaristic colonialism but from economic opportunism – a concept much more palatable to British sensibilities of the late 19th Century.  It was 'compiled' by the British East India Company through a series of trade wars spanning just over a hundred years, and then appropriated by the British Crown in 1858.  At this point it consisted of an array of company 'owned' conquered states to which had been welded a series of allied (effectively 'client') states maintaining various degrees of autonomy under native rulers. British acquisition brought a regularisation of government, an extension of government services including public works, and a notion of unified purpose and allegiance.  What it did not bring was the elimination of the range of regional, ethnic, and religious interests inherent in the patchwork of territories acquired.  These continued to manifest themselves in periodic local revolutions and mutinies and, paradoxically, in the foundation of an all-India secular political party (the Indian National Congress) in 1885.  The former were suppressed with increasing rigour (especially through the war years) but the latter proved much more difficult to subdue. The Amritsar massacre of 1919, a particularly brutal intervention by British troops, added urgency to the actions of the Congress and ultimately produced two outcomes of continuing significance.  The first was the fragmentation of its already frail unity into two opposing groups – one favouring violent action against the imperial government, the other committed to non-violent resistance.  The second was the emergence of Mohandas Karamchand Ghandi as leader of the non-violent movement. Ghandi's immense popular appeal produced two mass movements for national independence before the advent of the Second World War – one active in 1920-22, the other from 1930-34.  In both cases these saw very large numbers of the population adopt practices of non-violent non-cooperation that the authorities sought to repress through increasingly draconian measures. Both also, however, produced significant 'leakage' away from the non-violent faction of the party toward the more extreme elements - increasingly identified with Subhas Chandra Bose and culminating in his Indian National Army.
column5: El Raj británico, núcleo colonial del Imperio, afronta un creciente desafío a su autoridad tras la Gran Guerra. El descontento popular y la violenta represión británica en la masacre de Amritsar de 1919 consolidaron al Congreso Nacional Indio en la vanguardia emancipadora. Bajo el liderazgo de Mahatma Gandhi, sucesivas campañas masivas de desobediencia civil y no cooperación han paralizado la administración colonial, provocando severas medidas penales británicas. Al mismo tiempo, las corrientes más combativas afines a Subhas Chandra Bose abogan por la vía armada para lograr la independencia plena.

column2: With the outbreak of World War II in 1939, the viceroy, Lord Linlithgow, declared war on India's behalf without consulting Indian leaders, leading the Congress provincial ministries to resign in protest. The Muslim League, in contrast, supported Britain in the war effort
column5: Al estallar la guerra en septiembre de 1939, el virrey Linlithgow declaró a la India en estado de guerra contra Alemania de forma unilateral y sin consultar a los dirigentes locales. En señal de protesta contra la imposición colonial, los ministros provinciales del Congreso Nacional Indio renunciaron a sus cargos en bloque. Por el contrario, la Liga Musulmana de Muhammad Ali Jinnah decidió cooperar activamente con las autoridades imperiales británicas para consolidar su futura representación política.

column2: In 1936, India, known at the time as the British Raj, is a huge country of contradictions at the crossroad road between colonial subjugation and national independence. Nearly a million and a half Indian nationals served in the British army of the First World War, and the fate of the people of India and the waning fortunes of empire are bound together. The 'Jewel of the British Empire' continues to stagger along on the legacy of an aging colonial administration binding together a country of diverse and often fractious peoples. After many years of on and off rebellion, agitation for national independence and civil rights the Government of India Act of 1935 establishes local governing authority through elected provincial parliments. In 1937 the Congress party of Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi, Jawaharlal Nehru and Subhas Chandra Bose win sweeping governing powers in seven of eleven provinicial legislatures.
column5: Conocida formalmente como el Raj británico, la India encara un período de tensión política entre la tutela colonial de Londres y los reclamos soberanistas. Tras décadas de resistencia civil y agitación nacionalista, la Ley de Gobierno de la India de 1935 introdujo una autonomía limitada mediante asambleas provinciales electas. En los comicios de 1937, el Partido del Congreso liderado por Nehru y Gandhi obtuvo una contundente victoria en la mayoría de las legislaturas, consolidando una plataforma institucional frente a la autoridad del virrey.

column2: French Indochina is part of the French colonial Empire in South-East Asia. A federation of 3 Vietnamese regions, Tonkin, Annam and Cochinchina, together with Cambodia was created in 1887. Laos was added in 1893 and Kouang-Tchéou-Wan in 1900. The capital was moved from Saigon (in Cochinchina) to Hanoi (Tonkin) in 1902. On February 10th 1930 there was a rebellion of Vietnamese soldiers in the garrison of the French Colonial Army in Yen Bay. The mutiny was sponsored from the Nationalist Vietnamese Party. The attack was the biggest problem fueled by the monarchist movement Can Vuong since the end of the 19th century. The aim of the rebellion was to prompt a greater rebellion among the population in an effort to remove the colonial authority. An increase of French control over their activities pushed the main group to take the risk of facing a grand scale attack on the North of Vietnam. Although the rebellion was crushed, the tensions remain and the peace is precarious.
column5: La Indochina francesa, establecida a finales del siglo XIX, integró en una federación administrativa a las regiones de Tonkín, Annam, Cochinchina, Camboya y Laos. Pese al férreo dispositivo militar galo, el descontento anticolonial desembocó en el motín militar de Yên Bái en febrero de 1930, impulsado por el Partido Nacionalista de Vietnam (VNQDD) junto a reductos monárquicos. Aunque las autoridades coloniales aplastaron la sublevación mediante una dura represión y ejecuciones públicas, la agitación revolucionaria y el sentimiento patriótico permanecen latentes en todo el sudeste asiático.

column2: The French Mandate for Syria and the Lebanon (also known as the French Mandate for Syria) was a League of Nations mandate created after the First World War and the partitioning of the Ottoman Empire. During the two years that followed the end of the war in 1918, and according to the Sykes-Picot Agreement which was signed between Britain and France during the war, the British held control of the Ottoman province of Mesopotamia (Iraq) and the southern part of the Ottoman province of Syria (Palestine and Jordan), while the French controlled the rest of Ottoman Syria (modern Syria, Lebanon, and Hatay province of Turkey). During the first years of the 1920s, the British and French control of these territories became formalized by the League of Nations' mandate system, and France was assigned the mandate of Syria in September 29, 1923, which included modern Lebanon and Hatay (Alexandretta) in addition to modern Syria. The French mandate of Syria lasted until 1943, when two independent countries emerged from the mandate period, Syria and Lebanon, in addition to Hatay which had joined Turkey in 1939 following a referendum. French troops left Syria and Lebanon finally in 1946.
column5: El Mandato francés sobre Siria y el Líbano fue establecido formalmente por la Sociedad de Naciones en 1923 tras la partición de las provincias otomanas en el acuerdo secreto Sykes-Picot. Francia dividió administrativamente el territorio para contrarrestar el nacionalismo panárabe y sofocó con dureza la Gran Revuelta Siria de los años veinte. Pese a la cesión diplomática del sanjacado de Alejandreta a Turquía en 1939 y a las presiones de París por retener bases operativas, las repúblicas de Siria y Líbano lograron la independencia formal, concretándose la evacuación militar en 1946.

column2: The Dutch East Indies, or Netherlands East Indies, was the Dutch colony that became modern Indonesia following World War II. It was formed from the nationalised colonies of the former Dutch East India Company that came under the administration of the Netherlands in 1800. During the 19th century, Dutch possessions and its hegemony were expanded, reaching their greatest extent in the early 20th century, defining the borders of modern-day Indonesia. The colony was based on rigid racial and social categorisations with a Dutch elite living separate but linked to their native subjects. Following the Japanese occupation during World War II, Indonesian nationalists declared independence in 1945. This resulted in the Indonesian National Revolution which ended when, under the auspices of the UN, the Dutch–Indonesian Round Table Conference formally recognised Indonesian sovereignty on December 27, 1949.
column5: Las Indias Orientales Neerlandesas constituyeron la posesión más valiosa del imperio colonial de La Haya, conformada a partir de los territorios de la Compañía de las Indias Orientales. Consolidado su dominio insular en el siglo XIX, el archipiélago suministró valiosos recursos petrolíferos, de caucho y estaño bajo una estricta jerarquía administrativa colonial. La fulgurante invasión japonesa en 1942 desmanteló el control holandés y facilitó el rearme nacionalista de Sukarno, quien proclamó la República de Indonesia en 1945 abriendo una cruenta guerra de independencia.

column2: The Free City of Danzig is a semi-autonomous city-state created on 15 November 1920 in accordance with the terms of Part III, Section XI of the 1919 Treaty of Versailles. The Free City included the Baltic Sea port of Danzig and over two hundred nearby towns, villages, and settlements. It was under League of Nations protection and put into a binding customs union with Poland. Poland was also given full rights to develop and maintain transportation, communication, and port facilities in the city. The Free City was created in order to give Poland access to a well-sized seaport while respecting the fact that the city's population was roughly ninety-five percent German.
column5: La Ciudad Libre de Dánzig fue una entidad semiindependiente instituida en noviembre de 1920 por el Tratado de Versalles bajo la tutela de la Sociedad de Naciones. Diseñada para dotar a la Segunda República Polaca de salida portuaria al mar Báltico y enlace ferroviario mediante una unión aduanera, la ciudad conservó una aplastante mayoría demográfica germana (un 95 por ciento del censo). Esta contradicción nacional convirtió al enclave en un constante foco de fricción geopolítica que el Tercer Reich utilizó como pretexto directo para la invasión militar de Polonia.

column2: The German Empire was created at Versailles in 1871 under the aegis of Prussian military might after the defeat of France a year previously. Yet Chancellor Bismarck desired no further expansion - rather, favoured the maintenance of the status quo. Bismarck's foreign policy aimed at maintaining Germany's position as Europe's pre-eminent military power by keeping France diplomatically isolated. In 1879, a rapprochement with Austria was completed, with the signing of an alliance. 1882 saw Italy included into the combination, and a Reinsurance Treaty was signed with Russia, thereby separating France from potential allies and curtailing its desires for 'revanche'. Domestically, Bismarck appeased the socialists' desires for democratisation by pursuing a popular policy of colonialism and modest reforms. 1888 saw the ascent to the throne of Germany's new emperor, Wilhelm II - a year later he sacked Chancellor Bismarck, refused to renew the Russian Reinsurance Treaty and began his pursuit of 'a place in the sun'. Russia, insecure with the recent repeal of the Reinsurance Treaty, aligned themselves with France. Germany suddenly found itself with potential enemies on two fronts, not to mention the enemy within: the socialists. Wilhelm II's policy of 'Weltmacht' aimed at turning Germany from a continental power, into a global power. Wilhelm II believed that this could be achieved by the construction of an ocean-going fleet, and in 1897, his Navy minister, Alfred Tirpitz passed the first of two important navy bills, backed by rich industrialists and junkers alike - an attempt to unite all German peoples and integrate the socialist leaning working classes into the volksgemeinschaft. This move of naval expansion alarmed the British, causing the latter to align itself closer to France by signing the Entente Cordiale in 1904. By 1906, the British had responded comprehensively to the German naval challenge, by beginning the Dreadnought race, causing considerable antipathy between Great Britain and Germany. 'Der Fischer kommt' (Fisher is coming) was one of the frightened mottos of some of the residents of Kiel. With such a growing sense of encirclement, plans were drawn up for the eventuality of war with France and Russia - Chief of General Staff, Field Marshal Alfred von Schlieffen devised a timetable-tight plan involving an invasion of Belgium and a right-wheel flanking movement to circle Paris and crush the French army in its rear, before moving eastward to defeat the Russians before they had mobilised properly. This was not the only war that was planned: unease about the growing power of the socialists forced the German General Staff to devise the 'Staatsstreich', a contingency plan to crush uprising revolutionary workers that could imperil the stability of the German state and security of the landed elites. Crises over Morocco had worsened relations with France, and the continued Dreadnought race strained relations with Britain yet further. By 1914, the socialists had become the most powerful party in Germany, France was planning to increase conscription from two years service to three, and the infrastructure in western Russia had improved vastly. The German military had estimated that given current developments, Franco-Russian military power would become unassailable by 1916, and that the Schlieffen Plan would have to be implemented by 1915 at the very latest to work successfully. These facts could not have been far from the German military's mind as 1914 came: as Chief of Staff von Moltke put it - 'war is inevitable, and the sooner the better'. Time is running out. Can the 'place in the sun' still be found?
column5: Forjado tras la Guerra Franco-Prusiana de 1871, el Imperio alemán afianzó inicialmente su hegemonía aislando a París mediante el sistema bismarckiano. La entronización de Guillermo II y la renuncia al Tratado de Reaseguro aproximaron a Rusia y Francia, confrontando al Reich a una guerra en dos frentes. La agresiva política de la Weltpolitik y la carrera naval de acorazados impulsada por Tirpitz quebraron los lazos con Londres, originando la Triple Entente. Con el Schlieffen Plan diseñado para invadir Bélgica y neutralizar velozmente a los franceses, el Estado Mayor teme que el rearme zarista en 1916 frustre su campaña militar.

column2: The Dual Monarchy had been created in 1867 from a compromise between Emperor Franz Josef and the nobility of Hungary. A patchwork empire, it was composed of eleven major ethnic groups: Germans, Magyars, Czechs, Poles, Ruthenes, Slovaks, Serbs, Rumanians, Croats, Slovenes, and Italians, the empire centred around the capital, Vienna, and held together to a great degree by the strength of Emperor Franz Josef's character. To limit Russian influence in the Balkans, Austria-Hungary aligned itself with Germany in 1879, and then with Italy in 1882 to form the Triple Alliance. However, with Germany the dominant party in the alliance, Austria-Hungary would find its foreign policy wishes subordinated to the desires of its senior partner. The rulers of Austria-Hungary looked at their surroundings with great unease. Although Austria-Hungary was an ally of Italy, it was an unreliable power, and desired to complete its unification process with the addition of Austrian-owned Trieste and Trentino. Furthermore, the two nations had engaged in an intense naval race after the commissioning of the Dreadnought. Russia had traditionally been Austria's rival in the Balkans: the two powers vying for influence in a region free from the hegemony of the declining Ottoman Empire. Russia was seen as the prime agent behind the phenomenon of Pan-Slavism, the motivating force behind Serbia's growing power. The years leading up to 1914 would see Austria-Hungary grow ever more anxious about Serbia's mounting strength: the two states engaged in a trade quarrel in 1906, followed by a diplomatic breakdown after Austria-Hungary's annexation of the largely Serbian populated Bosnia-Herzegovina. 1913 saw further disagreement over the Balkan Wars, which pitted Serbia against Austrian-backed Bulgaria. By 1914, Austria-Hungary was faced with what was seen as an increasingly unfavourable situation in the Balkans. Russia appeared to be stronger after its defeat against Japan in 1905, and continued to be Vienna's main rival in the Balkans. Furthermore, its Pan-Slav policy made it Serbia's greatest supporter. Serbia itself was greatly strengthened after victory over Bulgaria, and its desire for a 'Greater Serbia' had obvious implications for Austria-Hungary: any moves towards greater Serbian unity would result in a great proportion of Austro-Hungarian Serbs having greater affinity to the Serbian motherland, leading to their inevitable breakaway from the Dual Monarchy. Austria-Hungary's rulers realised that if the Serbs broke away, other ethnic groups would demand greater autonomy, leading to the empire's ultimate demise. It appeared that time was against Austria-Hungary: the longer the situation manifested, the stronger Russian-backed Serbia would grow. With the empire's existence at stake, the Austro-Hungarian government knew that a remedy to the Serbian problem had to be found and administered soon. They would have to play their cards right though: war with Serbia may be desirable, but not so much with Russia. Any escalation of a European war must soon involve Italy and Rumania. Could it really be expected of the Austro-Hungarian Empire to survive a four-front war?
column5: La Monarquía Dual, consolidada en el Compromiso de 1867 bajo Francisco José I, integraba once etnias principales en un complejo mosaico institucional. Para frenar el paneslavismo zarista, Viena selló la Triple Alianza con Alemania e Italia, aunque la rivalidad adriática con Roma generaba desconfianza. Tras la anexión de Bosnia en 1908 y las Guerras Balcánicas, el vertiginoso fortalecimiento serbio con respaldo de San Petersburgo amenaza con descomponer el imperio por secesión étnica. En 1914, el mando imperial teme que el retraso en sofocar a Belgrado desemboque en una guerra en múltiples frentes sin salida.

column2: Following the fall of Nazi Germany, Soviet troops occupied all of the country, and Hungary gradually became a communist satellite state of the Soviet Union. Some 600,000 Hungarians were deported to Soviet labour camps after the Second World War and at least 200,000 died in captivity.\n\nMatyas Rakosi adhered to a militarist, industrialising, and war compensation economic policy, and the standard of living fell.

column5: El Protectorado del Sarre fue una entidad territorial transitoria instituida por los Aliados tras la capitulación de Alemania.
