column2: The first Yugoslav post-war elections were set for 11 November 1945. By this time the coalition of parties backing the Partisans, the People's Liberation Front, had been renamed into the People's Front. The People's Front was primarily led by the Communist Party of Yugoslavia, and represented by Josip Broz Tito. The reputation of both benefited greatly from their wartime exploits and decisive success, and they enjoyed genuine support among the populace. However, the old pre-war political parties were reestablished as well. However, while the elections themselves were fairly conducted by a secret ballot, the campaign that preceded them was highly irregular. The opposition withdrew from the election in protest to the hostile atmosphere. Indeed, voting was on a single list of People's Front candidates with provision for opposition votes to be cast in separate voting boxes, but this procedure made electors identifiable by OZNA agents. The election results of 11 November 1945 were decisively in favor of the latter, with an average of 85 percent of voters of each federal state casting their ballot for the People's Front.\n\nOn 29 November 1945, the Constituent Assembly of Yugoslavia formally abolished the monarchy and declared the state a republic. The country's official name became the Federal People's Republic of Yugoslavia, and the six 'Federal States' became 'People's Republics'. Yugoslavia became a single-party state and was considered in its earliest years a model of communist orthodoxy.
column5: En noviembre de 1945, el Frente Popular liderado por Josip Broz Tito y el Partido Comunista de Yugoslavia se alzó con la victoria electoral tras el boicot de las formaciones monárquicas ante el hostigamiento del servicio de seguridad OZNA. La Asamblea Constituyente abolió formalmente la monarquía de los Karadordevic y proclamó la República Popular Federal de Yugoslavia. El nuevo régimen estructuró el Estado en seis repúblicas populares bajo un férreo sistema de partido único, consolidándose como una potencia socialista hegemónica en los Balcanes.

column2: Until Yugoslavia's expulsion from the Cominform in 1948, Albania acted like a Yugoslav satellite and Tito aimed to use his choke hold on the Albanian party to incorporate the entire country into Yugoslavia. Albania became dependent on Soviet aid and know-how after the break with Yugoslavia in 1948. In February 1949, Albania gained membership in the communist bloc's organization for coordinating economic planning, the Council for Mutual Economic Assistance (Comecon). Tirana soon entered into trade agreements with Poland, Czechoslovakia, Hungary, Romania, and the Soviet Union. Soviet and East European technical advisers took up residence in Albania, and the Soviet Union also sent Albania military advisers and built a submarine installation on Sazan Island.\n\nAnxious to pay homage to Stalin, Albania's rulers implemented new elements of the Stalinist economic system. In 1949 Albania adopted the basic elements of the Soviet fiscal system, under which state enterprises paid direct contributions to the treasury from their profits and kept only a share authorized for self-financed investments and other purposes. In 1951, the Albanian government launched its first five-year plan, which emphasized exploiting the country's oil, chromite, copper, nickel, asphalt, and coal resources; expanding electricity production and the power grid; increasing agricultural output; and improving transportation. The government began a program of rapid industrialization after the APL's Second Party Congress and a campaign of forced collectivization of farmland in 1955.
column5: Hasta la ruptura entre Tito y Stalin en 1948, Albania actuó bajo una estrecha tutela yugoslava. Tras el cisma con Belgrado, el régimen de Enver Hoxha estrechó lazos con Moscú e ingresó en el COMECON, acogiendo asesores militares soviéticos y facilitando la base naval de la isla de Sazan. Inspirado en el modelo estalinista más ortodoxo, el Partido del Trabajo albanés implementó planes quinquenales centralizados centrados en la minería pesada, la electrificación estatal y la colectivización agraria forzosa, blindando al país en un rígido aislamiento exterior.

column2:
During the postwar period the country was known as the 'People's Republic of Bulgaria' and was ruled by the Bulgarian Communist Party. Its leader Dimitrov was close to the Yugoslav Communist leader Tito and believed that Yugoslavia and Bulgaria, as closely related South Slav peoples, should form a federation. This idea was not favoured by Stalin and there have long been suspicions that Dimitrov's sudden death in July 1949 was not accidental, although this has never been proven. It coincided with Stalin's expulsion of Tito from the Cominform and was followed by a 'Titoist' witch hunt in Bulgaria. This culminated in the show trial and execution of Deputy Prime Minister Traicho Kostov. The elderly Prime Minister Kolarov died in 1950 and power then passed to a Stalinist, Vulko Chervenkov.

Bulgaria's Stalinist phase lasted less than five years. Under his leadership, agriculture was collectivised, peasant rebellions were crushed, and a massive industrialisation campaign was launched. Labor camps were set up and at the height of the repression housed about 100,000 people. The Orthodox Patriarch was confined to a monastery and the Church placed under state control.

In 1950 diplomatic relations with the U.S. were broken off. But Chervenkov's support base in the Communist Party was too narrow for him to survive long once his patron Stalin was gone. Stalin died in March 1953 and in March 1954 Chervenkov was deposed as Party Secretary with the approval of the new leadership in Moscow and replaced by Todor Zhivkov. Chervenkov stayed on as Prime Minister until April 1956, when he was dismissed and replaced by Anton Yugov.

During the 1960s, Zhivkov initiated reforms and passed some market-oriented policies on an experimental level. By the mid-1950s standards of living rose significantly, and in 1957 collective farm workers benefited from the first agricultural pension and welfare system in Eastern Europe.
column5: Tras la guerra, la República Popular de Bulgaria quedó bajo la égida del Partido Comunista. Los planes de Gueorgui Dimitrov de crear una federación balcánica junto a la Yugoslavia de Tito chocaron con la férrea oposición de Stalin. Tras su sospechosa muerte en 1949 y la ruptura yugoslavo-soviética, el régimen desató una severa purga interna contra presuntos titoístas, ejecutando a figuras clave como Traicho Kostov. El líder estalinista Valko Chervenkov impulsó la colectivización forzada, la apertura de campos de trabajo y la subordinación de la Iglesia Ortodoxa, hasta que la desestalinización en Moscú facilitó el ascenso de Todor Zhivkov al frente del Estado.

column2: In 1947, King Michael I was forced by the Communists to abdicate and leave the country, Romania was proclaimed a republic, and remained under direct military and economic control of the USSR until the late 1950s. During this period, Romania's resources were drained by the 'SovRom' agreements: mixed Soviet-Romanian companies established to mask the looting of Romania by the Soviet Union.\n\nThe leader of Romania from 1948 to his death in 1965 was Gheorghe Gheorghiu-Dej, the First Secretary of the Romanian Workers' Party, who first sowed the seeds of greater independence from the Soviet Union by persuading Soviet First Secretary Nikita Khrushchev to withdraw troops from Romania in April 1958.During the 1947 1962 period, many people though were arbitrarily killed or imprisoned for political, economic or unknown reasons: detainees in prisons or camps, deported persons, persons under house arrest, and administrative detainees.
column5: En 1947 el rey Miguel I fue obligado a abdicar y se proclamó la república popular, consolidando el control soviético sobre Rumanía. Durante la posguerra, la economía nacional fue sistemáticamente drenada mediante las empresas mixtas SovRom para satisfacer las reparaciones exigidas por Moscú. Bajo el liderazgo de Gheorghe Gheorghiu-Dej al frente del Partido de los Trabajadores, el aparato estatal reprimió con dureza a disidentes y ejecutó purgas masivas en prisiones y campos. Pese al férreo alineamiento inicial, Bucarest maniobró diplomáticamente hasta lograr que Nikita Jrushchov retirase las tropas del Ejército Rojo en 1958.

column2: The Third Republic came into being in April 1945. Its government, installed at Kosice on April 4 and moved to Prague in May, was a National Front coalition. The popular enthusiasm evoked by the Soviet armies of liberation (which was decided by compromise of Allies and Joseph Stalin at the Yalta conference in 1944) benefited the communist party. Czechoslovaks, bitterly disappointed by the West at the Munich Agreement, responded favorably to both the party and the Soviet alliance. Reunited into one state after the war, the Czechs and Slovaks set national elections for the spring of 1946, when democratic parties won plurality of the vote. In 1947, Stalin summoned Gottwald to Moscow; upon his return to Prague, the communists demonstrated a significant radicalization of its tactics. On February 20, 1948, the twelve non-communist ministers resigned, in part, to induce Benes to call for early elections. On February 25, Benes, perhaps fearing Soviet intervention, capitulated. He accepted the resignations of the dissident ministers and received a new cabinet list from Gottwald, thus completing, under the cover of superficial legality, the communist takeover.\n\nCzechoslovakia was declared a 'people's democracy' (until 1960)   a preliminary step toward socialism and, ultimately, communism. Bureaucratic centralism under the direction of Communist Party of Czechoslovakia leadership was introduced. The ideological principles of Marxism-Leninism and socialist realism pervaded cultural and intellectual life.The economy was committed to comprehensive central planning and abolition of private ownership of capital. Czechoslovakia became a satellite state of the Soviet Union; it was a founding member of the Council for Mutual Economic Assistance (Comecon) in 1949 and of the Warsaw Pact in 1955.
column3: La Tercera República nació en abril de 1945. Su gobierno, instalado en Kosice el 4 de abril y trasladado a Praga en mayo, era una coalición del Frente Nacional. El entusiasmo popular despertado por los ejércitos soviéticos de liberación (decidido mediante el compromiso entre los Aliados y Iósif Stalin en la Conferencia de Yalta de 1944) benefició al Partido Comunista. Los checoslovacos, amargamente decepcionados con Occidente tras los Acuerdos de Múnich, respondieron favorablemente tanto al partido como a la alianza soviética. Reunificados en un solo Estado después de la guerra, checos y eslovacos convocaron elecciones nacionales para la primavera de 1946, en las que los partidos democráticos obtuvieron la mayoría relativa de los votos. En 1947, Stalin convocó a Gottwald a Moscú;;Restablecida en 1945 tras la expulsión del Eje, la Tercera República Checoslovaca formó un gobierno de coalición del Frente Nacional. El desencanto popular con Occidente tras los Acuerdos de Múnich facilitó el auge electoral comunista. En febrero de 1948, ante la dimisión de ministros moderados y el temor a una invasión soviética, el presidente Edvard Beneš capituló ante Klement Gottwald en el «Golpe de Praga». El Partido Comunista monopolizó el poder político, instaurando una democracia popular de rígida planificación económica estatal y convirtiendo al país en un Estado satélite soviético fundador del COMECON y del Pacto de Varsovia."

column2:
In June 1945, as an implementation of the February Yalta Conference directives, according to the Soviet interpretation, a Polish Provisional Government of National Unity was formed; it was soon recognized by the United States and many other countries. A communist rule and Soviet domination were apparent from the beginning: sixteen prominent leaders of the Polish anti-Nazi underground were brought to trial in Moscow in June 1945. In the immediate post-war years, the emerging communist rule was challenged by people and groups not reconciled with it and many thousands perished in the fight or were pursued by the security forces and executed.

Although the Yalta agreement called for free elections, those held in January 1947 were controlled by the communists. From that time the communist-dominated ruling bloc was officially the only source of governmental authority.

Larger rural estates and agricultural holdings as well as post-German property were redistributed through land reform and industry was nationalized beginning in 1944. The Three-Year Plan (1947 1949) continued with the rebuilding, socialization and restructuring of the economy. The rejection of the Marshall Plan (1947), however, made the aspirations of catching-up with the West European standard of living unrealistic.

The government's economic high priority was the development of militarily useful heavy industry. State-run institutions, collectivization and cooperative entities were imposed, while even small-scale private enterprises were being eradicated. Stalinism introduced heavy political and ideological indoctrination in social life, culture and education. Great strides, however, were made in the areas of universal public education (including elimination of adult illiteracy), health care and recreational amenities for working people. Many historic sites, including central districts of war-destroyed Warsaw and Gda sk (Danzig), were rebuilt at a great cost.
column4: En junio de 1945, en aplicación de las directrices de la Conferencia de Yalta de febrero, según la interpretación soviética, se formó un Gobierno Provisional Polaco de Unidad Nacional;En junio de 1945, según las directrices de Yalta, se constituyó el Gobierno Provisional de Unidad Nacional, bajo un férreo control soviético evidenciado en el «Juicio de los Dieciséis» contra la resistencia clandestina polaca. Tras los comicios manipulados de 1947, el bloque comunista consolidó su hegemonía absoluta y aplastó a los grupos insurgentes opositores. El Estado impuso la nacionalización industrial, la colectivización agraria y el rechazo al Plan Marshall en favor de la industria pesada militar, priorizando paralelamente la alfabetización pública y la reconstrucción integral de Varsovia y Gdansk."

column2: The Zhili Clique was one of several factions that split during the warlord era named for the Zhili region. Unlike other cliques, this one was formed by officers who felt discriminated against by Premier Duan Qirui in matters of appointment and promotions. They rallied around President Feng Guozhang who had to share power with Duan's dominant Anhui clique in the Beiyang government. After Feng's natural death, leadership passed to Cao Kun. Cao was victorious in the Zhili-Anhui War (1920) though the credit belongs to his chief lieutenant, Wu Peifu. Relations with the Fengtian clique, which gave nominal assistance against Anhui, deteriorated and Wu again brought victory during the First Zhili-Fengtian War. In the next two years, the Zhili clique scored successive victories which led to Cao Kun's ascendency to the presidency via bribery. Cao's ambition brought all of his enemies against him and created dissension within the clique. Zhili would have won the Second Zhili-Fengtian War (1924) and eventually reunite all of China had it not been for Feng Yuxiang's betrayal with the Beijing coup. Cao was imprisoned and leadership passed to Wu who along with Sun Chuanfang managed to hold central China for the next two years. The Zhili clique was the only warlord faction to be destroyed as a result of the Northern Expedition.
column5: La camarilla de Zhili fue una de las facciones militares más influyentes durante la era de los señores de la guerra en China. Formada en torno al presidente Feng Guozhang en oposición a Duan Qirui, alcanzó la hegemonía del gobierno de Beiyang tras vencer en la Guerra Zhili-Anhui de 1920 y en el primer choque contra Fengtian, gracias al liderazgo militar del general Wu Peifu. No obstante, la polémica elección presidencial de Cao Kun desató la discordia interna. Durante la Segunda Guerra Zhili-Fengtian en 1924, la traición de Feng Yuxiang en el golpe de Pekín precipitó la derrota de la facción, siendo definitivamente desmantelada por la Expedición del Norte del Kuomintang.

column2: Created after successful conquest of Poland from territories not directly assigned to existing Reichsgau districts in the Reich, the Generalgouvernement was a tool of ultimate oppression and exploitation of conquered Polish territories, aimed on disestablishment of the Polish nation and culture in every possible aspect.
column5: Establecido tras la invasión y ocupación militar de Polonia en 1939 con las regiones no anexionadas directamente a los Reichsgau alemanes, el Gobierno General funcionó como una estructura de estricta ocupación colonial. Administrado con mano de hierro por las autoridades nacionalsocialistas, el territorio fue destinado a la desarticulación institucional, la explotación forzada de recursos y el desmantelamiento sistemático de la cultura y sociedad polacas.

column2: Africa Orientale Italiana, or AOI, is an Italian colonial state established after the Italian victory in the Second Italo-Abyssinian War. It has been created by the merger of the newly conquered Abyssinia with the old colonies of Italian Somaliland and Italian Eritrea. AOI is divided into six governorates of Italian East Africa (Amhara, Galla-Sidamo, Scioa, Harar, Eritrea and Somalia), each run by an Italian governor. Each governor is answerable to the Italian viceroy, who represents the King of Italy. Rule in Italian East Africa is harsh for the native peoples, especially towards Ethiopians as Fascist policy seeks to integrate their culture into the Italian Empire. Italy is making huge and expensive infrastructure investments and encouraging Italian peasants to colonize the AOI by creating agriculture and small industries there. However few Italians are moving to the colony and AOI is proving to be highly expensive to maintain, slowly draining the Italian economy.
column5: El África Oriental Italiana (AOI) fue constituida formalmente tras el triunfo en la Segunda Guerra Ítalo-Etíope de 1936, fusionando la recién ocupada Abisinia con las antiguas colonias de Eritrea y Somalia. Estructurado en seis gobernaciones bajo el mando superior de un virrey en Adís Abeba, el territorio afronta una rígida administración militar orientada a supeditar las poblaciones locales a la soberanía imperial de Roma. Pese a las ingentes partidas presupuestarias destinadas a obras viales y colonización agraria, la escasa afluencia de colonos y los costes defensivos drenan sensiblemente las reservas del Reino de Italia.

column2: Arab nationalism was a rising force in the political world at the turn on the twentieth century. Nowhere was this feeling greater than in the Hejaz - a desolate strip of territory running from the Gulf of Aqaba in the north to the Asir in the south, centred around the Holy city of Mecca. From here, the Sharif of Mecca, Hussein ibn Ali ruled under the auspices of the Ottoman Empire, with a considerable amount of independence. Although loyal to the Sultan of Turkey, Hussein found himself at odds with the Young Turks' policy of centralisation - chief amongst them, the Hejaz railway link to Anatolia, that would allow the Ottoman authorities to strengthen their garrisons in the Hejaz and thus deprive the territory of its autonomy. Hussein knew that the completion of the railway would result in his relegation to the status of a local figurehead, and that any Arab revolt against Constantinople would have to come soon. However, the Arab world was not the united force that it appeared, and Mecca was not the only centre for Arab nationalists' loyalties. Ibn Saud of Nejd, and Ibn Mohammed of Yemen were but two rivals of Hussein, and the Sharif of Mecca knew only too well that the attitudes of these leaders would have to be considered when launching any revolt. In fleeting times of unity, the Arab chiefs had asked Hussein to throw off the Turkish yoke, yet he had refused, causing many senior Arab leaders to accuse Hussein of being a 'tool of the Turks'. Indeed, Hussein had considered the possibility of cooperating with the Turks in hope of being granted more sovereignty, but fears of losing credibility had discouraged any such course of action. By 1914, Hussein found himself surrounded by external enemies: many Arab nationalists saw himself as a Turkish official, the Ottoman authorities were extending their power over his domain via the Hejaz railway and Hussein was always wary of the intentions of his regional Arab rivals. As trouble brewed in Europe, Hussein chose to acquiesce, and allow developments on the continent determine his course of action.
column5: En vísperas de 1914, el valiato del Hiyaz y la ciudad santa de La Meca permanecían bajo el gobierno autónomo del jerife Hussein bin Ali, supeditado a la tutela otomana. No obstante, las reformas centralizadoras de los Jóvenes Turcos y la culminación del ferrocarril de Hiyaz amenazan con anular la autonomía tradicional árabe mediante el despliegue de guarniciones de la Sublime Puerta. Presionado entre la suspicacia de clanes rivales como los Saud de Néyed y las crecientes corrientes nacionalistas árabes, el jerife aguarda con cautela los acontecimientos bélicos en Europa antes de encabezar un alzamiento general contra Constantinopla.

column2: The Rashid dynasty begun their rule of Jebel Shammar in 1835, when Abdallah Ibn Rashid occupied the town of Hail, situated in the Shammar mountain range, located on an important pilgrimage route between Mesopotamia and Mecca. Throughout the nineteenth century the Rashidis consolidated their hold on Jebel Shammar, whilst rivalry for control of the Arabian peninsula continued with the Saud family. In 1887, the Rashidis extended their domain to the Saudi ruled city of Riyadh, driving the Saud family into exile in Kuwait. With the power of Jebel Shammar at its zenith, the Saudis plotted to retake Riyadh, and in 1902 a force of just eighty camel riders surprised the Rashidi garrison and retook the city. Now somewhat in recession, Jebel Shammar's ruler, Abdul Aziz Al Rashid now looks for closer relations with the Turks to counterbalance the rising power of Ibn Saud.
column5: El Emirato de Jabal Shammar, gobernado por la dinastía rashidí desde su capital en Hail, dominó estratégicamente las rutas caravaneras y de peregrinación entre Mesopotamia y el Hiyaz durante el siglo XIX. Tras alcanzar su apogeo forzando al exilio a la dinastía rival de los Saud en 1887, la posición rashidí decayó abruptamente en 1902, cuando Ibn Saud recuperó Riad mediante un audaz golpe de mano. Enfrentado al creciente avance territorial del Emirato de Néyed y Hasa, el emir Abdul Aziz bin Rashid busca una estrecha alianza política y militar con el Imperio otomano para contener el ascenso de sus rivales dinásticos.

column2: Nestor Makhno was an experienced revolutionary and anarchist, who led the people of eastern Ukraine in a guerrilla war against the reactionary German-backed government of that state. Following the departure of the Germans, he supported the establishment of a Regional Congress of Peasants', Workers' and Insurgents' Soviets as a democratically elected government, based in the city of Huliaipole. To defend its territory, the Congress then organised the Revolutionary Insurgent Army, led by Makhno. Although the government was nominally run on anarchist principles of consensus, there is no doubt that Makhno was in charge. He supported many of the principles espoused by Lenin and the Bolsheviks, but opposed them over confiscation of land from peasant families and the independence of elected Soviets. For this reason, many Bolsheviks regarded him as an enemy. On the other hand, Makhno hated the Whites and everything they stood for, and was willing to fight alongside anybody who opposed the forces of reaction. Indeed, when the prominent Cossack leader Grigoriev offered to join forces with Makhno against the Reds and together seek an alliance with the White general Denikin, Makhno pulled out his revolver and shot Grigoriev dead on the spot. Makhno's followers are as fanatical and devoted to the cause and he may be the first able to realise a dream of an anarchist society.
column5: Veterano militante libertario, Néstor Majnó encabezó una vasta guerra de guerrillas en el sureste de Ucrania tras la retirada alemana y el colapso del Hetmanato. Al mando del Ejército Revolucionario Insurreccional y con centro en Guliaipole, organizó asambleas de sóviets libres de campesinos y obreros en confrontación directa tanto con el Ejército Blanco zarista como con el centralismo bolchevique. Reacio a las requisas forzosas de grano de Moscú y defensor a ultranza de la autogestión comunal agraria, el movimiento majnovista lucha por preservar un territorio libre frente a las acometidas del Ejército Rojo.

column2: Venustiano Carranza de la Garza was one of the leaders of the Mexican Revolution. In August 1911 Carranza was elected governor of Coahuila. As governor, Carranza began to reform the judiciary, the legal codes, and tax laws. He introduced regulations to prevent mining accidents, to rein in abusive practices at company stores, to break up commercial monopolies, to combat alcoholism, and to rein in gambling and prostitution. He also made large investments in education, which he saw as the key to societal development. When Victoriano Huerta declared himself President of Mexico on February 19th 1913, Carranza allied with other politicians and generals (Pablo González, Álvaro Obregón, Emiliano Zapata and Francisco Villa) to fight against the harsh military dictatorship of Huerta and his Federal Army. Carranza became Primer Jefe (First Chief) of the Constitutional Army which promised to restore the 1857 Constitution of Mexico.
column5: Elegido gobernador de Coahuila en 1911, Venustiano Carranza impulsó importantes reformas laborales y fiscales antes del estallido del golpe de Estado de Victoriano Huerta en 1913. En respuesta a la usurpación del régimen de la Ciudadela, Carranza proclamó el Plan de Guadalupe y asumió el mando supremo como Primer Jefe del Ejército Constitucionalista. Aglutinando temporalmente bajo su causa a comandantes y caudillos como Álvaro Obregón, Francisco Villa y Emiliano Zapata, su objetivo central es la completa derrota del Ejército Federal y la restauración del orden constitucional republicano en México.

column2: Francisco 'Pancho' Villa was one of the most prominent Mexican Revolutionary generals. Villa's men and supporters became known as Villistas during the Mexican Revolution, a a major armed struggle that started in 1910 and lasted roughly until 1920. As commander of the División del Norte (Division of the North), he was the real governor of the Northern Mexican state of Chihuahua. Villa and his supporters seized hacienda land for distribution to peasants and soldiers. He robbed and commandeered trains, and, like the other revolutionary generals, printed fiat money to pay for his cause. When Victoriano Huerta declared himself President of Mexico on February 19th 1913, Villa allied with other politicians and generals (Venustiano Carranza, Pablo González, Álvaro Obregón and Emiliano Zapata) to fight against the harsh military dictatorship of Huerta and his Federal Army.
column5: Comandante en jefe de la célebre División del Norte, Francisco «Pancho» Villa se convirtió en una de las figuras militares más determinantes de la Revolución mexicana. Como autoridad militar indiscutible en el estado de Chihuahua, expropió grandes haciendas para repartirlas entre sus tropas y campesinos, asegurando el abastecimiento logístico mediante el control de la red ferroviaria. Alineado inicialmente con el movimiento constitucionalista contra la dictadura militar de Victoriano Huerta, sus fuerzas de choque de caballería representan el ala social y agrarista más combativa del norte del país.

column2: Emiliano Zapata Salazar was a leading figure in the Mexican Revolution, which broke out in 1910 and lasted roughly until 1920. Zapata formed and commanded an important revolutionary force, the Liberation Army of the South, during the Mexican Revolution and his soldiers and followers became known as Zapatistas. His main demands and slogan was 'Reform, Freedom, Justice and Law!' which refered to the need for an agrarian reform in favor of the farmers and the need for free elections. When Victoriano Huerta declared himself President of Mexico on February 19th 1913, Zapata allied with other politicians and generals (Venustiano Carranza, Pablo González, Álvaro Obregón and Francisco Villa) to fight against the harsh military dictatorship of Huerta and his Federal Army. Zapata organized a succesfull guerilla war against the federal forces, mainly thanks to the support from the lower classes of the society.
column5: Originario de Morelos y adalid de las reivindicaciones campesinas, Emiliano Zapata encabezó la insurrección en el sur de México al frente del Ejército Libertador del Sur. Bajo el lema del Plan de Ayala («Reforma, Libertad, Justicia y Ley»), exigió la restitución inmediata de tierras y recursos comunales arrebatados por los grandes terratenientes. Tras repudiar la usurpación militar de Victoriano Huerta en 1913, el movimiento zapatista desató una exitosa guerra de guerrillas, articulando la resistencia armada popular y campesina en favor de una profunda reforma agraria nacional.

column2: The first European contact with Newfoundland was that of the medieval Norse sailing from Greenland. For several years after 1000 AD they operated a small village on the tip the Great Northern Peninsula, known today as L'Anse aux Meadows. Around 1500 AD European explorers, fishermen from England, Portugal, France and Spain and Basques began exploration. Sir Humphrey Gilbert, provided with letters patent from Queen Elizabeth I, landed in St John's in August 1583, and formally took possession of the island. Newfoundland became England's first permanent colony in the New World. During the Seven Years War, the control of Newfoundland became a major source of conflict between Britain, France and Spain who all pressed for a share in the valuable fishery there. The Battle of Signal Hill was fought in Newfoundland in 1762, when a French force landed and tried to occupy the island, only to be repulsed by the British. In 1854 the British government established Newfoundland's Responsible government, which rejected confederation with Canada in the 1869 general election. Poor fishing and economic stagnation characterized the country during the closing decades of the 19th century. The title of Dominion was formally adopted by the Government of Newfoundland in 1907.
column5: Terranova, enclave pesquero estratégico en el Atlántico Norte desde los primeros asentamientos nórdicos y exploraciones británicas del siglo XVI, constituyó la colonia ultramarina más antigua de Inglaterra. Tras disputarse el control marítimo frente a Francia en la Guerra de los Siete Años, la isla consolidó un gobierno parlamentario propio en 1854, rechazando su incorporación a la Confederación de Canadá en 1869. Pese a las periódicas crisis del sector pesquero y a su estancamiento financiero a finales del siglo XIX, Terranova adoptó formalmente el estatus soberano de Dominio británico en 1907.

column2: After the October Revolution, Cossack chieftain Grigory Semenov formed a Transbaikal Cossack armed force in Chita opposed to Bolshevik rule. However, he suffered an initial defeat and had to flee to Manchuria. After the revolt of the Czechoslovak Legion, he was able to return and consolidate his rule over the Transbaikal region. On September 10th 1918, Semenov was appointed commander of the 5th Army Corps of the Amur, with headquarters in Chita, by the Provisional Government of Autonomous Siberia (based in Vladivostok). Initially, the Provisional All-Russian Government refused to recognize Semenov's authority, but later it had to accept Semenov as de facto leader and confirm him as Commander-in-Chief of the Chita military district.
column5: Tras el triunfo bolchevique en 1917, el atamán Grigori Semiónov formó un destacamento de cosacos del Baikal en Chitá para combatir el naciente régimen soviético. Tras refugiarse temporalmente en Manchuria, la sublevación de la Legión Checoslovaca en el ferrocarril transiberiano le permitió retornar y afianzar su control en Transbaikalia. Respaldado por el gobierno blanco regional de Vladivostok y con asistencia militar japonesa, Semiónov se impuso como comandante supremo del distrito de Chitá, administrando el territorio oriental como señor de la guerra frente al avance comunista.

column2: Warlord Zhang Zuolin ruled over Manchuria with an iron hand, turning to Japan for political and military support. The Manchu State was formally declared independent in 1922 but collapsed in 1928 due to both internal and external pressures. When Zhang Zuolin's armies failed to stop Chiang Kai Shek's Northern Expedition in 1928, Kwantung Army saboteurs blew up the train on which both he and his foreign minister were riding. Zuolin's son, Zhang Xueliang, quickly asserted control and pledged his loyalty to the Guomindang. Zhang Xueliang got involved in a losing war with the Soviet Union in 1929 over control of the China Eastern Railway built by the Russians. In 1931, he faced an even bigger threat, as Japan invaded his domain after staging the Mukden Incident. Zhang consulted Chiang Kai Shek and the pair agreed not to oppose Japan's moves except in the League of Nations. But many Chinese were unhappy and volunteered to form citizen armies to oppose Japan's takeover. The Kwantung Army defeated these attempts, and installed its own puppet state of Manchukuo. At the time, Chiang was involved in attempts to suppress the communists, giving that task priority over opposing Japan's intrusions into northeast China. Chiang signed the Tanggu Truce in 1933, tactility acknowledging the state of Manchukuo, acknowledging Japanese control of Rehe and Chahar provinces, and creating a demilitarized zone in East Hebei province. In 1935 the He-Umezo agreement required China to remove its divisions from the rest of Hebei Province, meaning only militia was available for defense against Japan. Zhang grew increasingly distant from Chiang, and began exploring secret contacts with the communists in order to form a united front to oppose further Japanese intrusions and if possible recover the northeastern provinces. Will the Fengtian Clique quietly disappear? Or is Zhang Xueliang about to enter center stage in world history?
column5: Durante la década de 1920, el señor de la guerra Zhang Zuolin dominó Manchuria apoyado por la camarilla de Fengtian y Tokio. Su asesinato en el atentado ferroviario de Huanggutun en 1928 llevó a su hijo, Zhang Xueliang, a reconocer al gobierno del Kuomintang. Tras la invasión japonesa de Manchuria en 1931 y el establecimiento del Estado títere de Manchukuo, Chiang Kai-shek priorizó reprimir a los comunistas frente a la agresión foránea, firmando la tregua de Tanggu. Descontento con la pasividad de Nankín, Zhang Xueliang inició contactos secretos con el PCCh para forjar un frente unido nacional contra Japón.

column2: The Empire of China was a short-lived attempt by statesman and general Yuan Shikai from late 1915 to early 1916 to reinstate monarchy in China. The attempt was ultimately a failure, but it set back the Chinese republican cause by many years and fractured China into a period of conflict between various local warlords.
column5: El efímero Imperio de China (1915-1916) constituyó la fallida tentativa del general Yuan Shikai por restaurar la monarquía imperial bajo su mando como emperador Hongxian. El abierto rechazo de los gobernadores militares del sur, el estallido de la Guerra de Protección Nacional y el ultimátum de las potencias forzaron a Shikai a abdicar a los pocos meses. Su muerte prematura en junio de 1916 frustró la frágil institucionalidad republicana de Pekín, fragmentando el país en facciones militares rivales y marcando el inicio formal de la era de los señores de la guerra.

column2: Unsuccessful revolutions in both the Bourbon Kingdom and the United Kingdom left the African colonies of these nations independent with white minority governments. They quickly united together to avoid being picked off by their former mother countries and together intended to exploit the Dark Continent. As the 19th century drew to a close, the government realised that they would need a strong industrial base to maintain their independence in an increasingly expansionist world. However this would also sow the seeds of the end of the white minority rule as the only way to develop was to create a black working class. The early years of the 20th century saw the creation of the African National Congress lead by the former Emperors of Ethiopia who were seen as many in the black community as symbols of resistance for their long efforts to prevent Ottoman conquest of Ethiopia. Finally, the dam burst and an ANC government took  power. Quickly and wisely making concessions to the white minority who still staffed key positions in both industry and the military, the new state began to consolidate. Faced with hostile states to the north, conflict now seems inevitable.
column5: Tras revoluciones fallidas en Europa, las posesiones coloniales africanas formaron una unión independiente dominada por minorías blancas para evitar el sometimiento metropolitano y explotar sus recursos continentales. No obstante, la urgente industrialización demandó mano de obra nativa masiva, facilitando la creación del Congreso Nacional Africano (CNA) encabezado por linajes históricos etíopes. La agitación social forzó la transición a un gobierno soberano del CNA que garantizó la operatividad técnica de las élites industriales para consolidar sus fronteras frente a potencias hostiles.

column2: On 30 March 1940 a puppet government led by Wang Jingwei was established in the Republic of China under the protection of the Empire of Japan. The regime officially called itself the Republic of China and its government the Reorganized National Government of China. Informally it was known as the Republic of China-Nanjing. The Reorganized National Government claimed to be the rightful government of China, but it was widely regarded as a puppet state and enjoyed no diplomatic recognition, except from the states of the Anti-Comintern Pact.\nThe Japanese Army proceed to create a local army, supposedly to defend the areas controlled by the Reorganized National Government. In reality, it served as a second line of offense and internal security as part of the Second Sino-Japanese war. The regime also had a regular police force under Japanese control. The local politicians and media consistently provided pro-Japanese propaganda, praising the 'heroic efforts of the Imperial troops' and argued for a 'national defence against Communism and Western interests'.\nHowever, despite rapid growth in manpower and increased responsibility to support the Japanese, the collaborationist Chinese army suffered from very low morale because the general public in the occupied areas viewed them as Hanjian, or traitors to China, and many surrendered quickly to Generalissimo Jiang Jieshi's forces during military engagements. Many commanders of collaborationist army secretly cooperated with the Chinese Secret Service, providing intelligence about Japanese troop movements.
column5: En marzo de 1940 el mando militar japonés instauró en Nankín un gobierno títere presidido por Wang Jingwei, autodenominado Gobierno Nacional Reorganizado de la República de China. Reconocido únicamente por las potencias del Eje, el régimen actuó como instrumento administrativo y represivo bajo supervisión del Ejército Imperial japonés. Pese a levantar nutridas fuerzas militares colaboracionistas para tareas de seguridad en retaguardia, el ejército de Nankín adolece de una moral precaria: tildados de traidores (hanjian) por la población, numerosos oficiales desertan o colaboran con la resistencia del Kuomintang.

column2: During the bloody suppression of the Chartist movement in the United Kingdom, the more individualistic colonists 'down under' became increasingly concerned about the direction of the mother country. As the chaos grew to a climax, they saw no alternative but to part company and go their own way, forming the Federation of Australasia. Much of the 19th century saw peace and development and a great deal of immigrants from the mother country seeking freedom. However, this all changed when Japan started to expand into the power vacuum in the Pacific. The wave of xenophobia that followed convinced the Australasian government that they had no choice but to set up their own buffer zone in the Pacific. This might have sparked a war, but the sides quickly agreed to zones of influence and an uneasy truce formed between Japan, Indo-China and Australasia. In the wake of the Japanese Revolution and the appearance of a revolutionary communist government on its northern border, tensions started to grow.
column5: Tras la sangrienta represión cartista en Gran Bretaña, los asentamientos coloniales del Pacífico rompieron lazos metropolitanos para constituir la Federación de Australasia. El siglo XIX trajo una rápida expansión económica y flujos migratorios, hasta que el expansionismo naval japonés en el Pacífico forzó a Canberra a negociar áreas de influencia y guarnecer sus límites insulares. Tras la agitación revolucionaria que llevó a la instauración de un régimen comunista en el mar del Japón, Australasia vigila con extrema cautela sus puestos de avanzada naval en Oceanía ante una confrontación abierta.

column2: France narrowly avoided revolution at the end of the 18th century, and the death of last Bourbon King led to the crown passing to the Spanish branch of the family. The new kingdom quickly added Portugal to its domains. As the European powers started to form alliances to check the new super power, the Carlist war erupted. It became a bloody civil war between local nationalist forces and those that favoured a unified state. For the rest of Europe, the war came as a relief and they did much to support resistance against the Bourbon crown. The Crown's forces would be triumphant in Europe, but at the price of losing their colonial empire. The Bourbon Kingdom would spend the rest of nineteenth century trying to re-establish control over its old colonies but without success.  Reform at home resulted in the establishment of a constitutional monarchy. The Bourbon Kingdom was then looking for an outlet for expansion and the decaying Ottoman Empire looked vulnerable. Together with Italy and the Cossack state, a victorious war was waged against the Ottoman Empire leading to massive gains in North Africa. However, along its long European and African frontier, the Bourbon Kingdom faces ideologically hostile neighbours.
column5: Tras frustrar la revolución a fines del siglo XVIII, la unificación dinástica bajo la rama española de los Borbones integró a Francia, España y Portugal en una gran hegemonía continental. Pese a sofocar las cruentas guerras carlistas y establecer una monarquía constitucional, la contienda civil provocó la secesión definitiva de sus posesiones coloniales americanas. Reorientando su proyección estratégica hacia el Mediterráneo, el reino conquistó amplias zonas del norte de África a costa del Imperio otomano, enfrentando extensas fronteras rodeadas de regímenes ideológicamente rivales.

column2: The Republic is less than three years old. The corruption, weakness and incompetence that became synomynous with the Qing Dynasty is no more - or is it? China remains wracked by warlordism, central authority remains nothing but a facade, and remains the 'dead lion' of the East. Sun Yat-Sen's dream is just that - a distant mirage. Meanwhile, President Yuan Shi Kai rules China with an iron hand, crushing all opposition with his Beiyang army. Rumours are abound that he wishes to revive the monarchial system. The country is pressured from all sides by foreign powers. Much of Siberia has been lost to the Czar in the Bear's quest for access to warm waters and greater land. Outer Mongolia, once under the jurisdication of the Qing, has declared its independence. The far west of Xinjiang faces popular Islamic movements and Russian influences. Tibet is virtually under autonomous rule. The British Empire controls Hong Kong and the New terroritories as well as wielding considerable influence in Southern China and Tibet. Vietnam and Korea, long vassals of the Middle Kingdom, have fallen into the spheres of France and Japan respectively. To the latter China lost a humiliating war in 1894 that concluded with the loss of Taiwan and the Ryukyu islands. In the interior of China warlordism runs rampant as no figurehead has been able to control the masses. Countless warlords carve out their own areas of control, backed by private armies and funded by illicit trade sometimes in Opium. Warfare and dissent is common place and the country is in nothing short of anarchy. Other areas like Shandong and Hong Kong are carved up by foreign powers. China itself is technologically backwards, with a massive population of poor and illiterate peasants. Whoever controls Beijing lays claim to sovereignty over China. One could even make the case that the government changes hands monthly as rival warlords dispose of one another. For China there must arise a strong, ruthless and cunning leader. Capable of bring the overwhelming throng of the lower class into the technology and innovation of the western world, at the same time he must consolidate his rule, defeat the internal threat of the warlords and defend China's integrity from the schemes and designs of a wide array of powers who seek to carve China up. The road to victory for China will be long and arduous but the country has enormous potential due to its resources, size and population. It will be the mark of a true leader who is able to build upon such strengths.
column5: A tres años de la caída del Imperio Qing, la joven República de China permanece paralizada por la fragmentación armada y el caudillismo provincial. Mientras el presidente Yuan Shikai gobierna autoritariamente con el Ejército de Beiyang acariciando ambiciones monárquicas, la soberanía nacional se resquebraja ante las potencias: el Tíbet y Mongolia Exterior actúan al margen de Pekín, los imperios coloniales controlan los enclaves costeros y los señores de la guerra financian ejércitos privados mediante el tráfico de opio, requiriendo de un mando férreo para evitar la desintegración total del país.

column2: The end of the 19th century saw the gradual disintegration of the Ming Empire. China became a battleground between the powers with Russia and Japan fighting for control of Manchuria. For many Chinese nationalists the situation was intolerable and the revolution that overthrew the Ming Emperor was, with hindsight, inevitable. The result of the revolution nearly saw the destruction of China, as rival warlords carved out their power bases while, in the south, the Nationalists and Communists vied for power. However, just when it looked like China was doomed, the surprise death of Mao  led to the more pragmatic Deng Xiaoping becoming leader of the CCP. Putting the needs of China ahead of the revolution, a deal was struck with the KMT and the united forces quickly brought the warlords to heel. The Chinese state was at its strongest for centuries and would need to be, as none of its neighbours looked friendly.
column5: Tras el derrumbe de la monarquía tradicional a finales del siglo XIX y la devastación por las injerencias foráneas en Manchuria, el territorio chino se precipitó hacia el colapso territorial. Sin embargo, tras el inesperado fallecimiento de Mao Zedong, la asunción del mando comunista por el pragmático Deng Xiaoping facilitó un pacto estratégico histórico con el Kuomintang. Formando un frente unido nacional, las fuerzas aliadas sometieron con rapidez a los señores de la guerra provinciales, consolidando una China unificada, armada y decidida a disuadir cualquier amenaza en sus fronteras.

column2: When the Carlist Wars erupted in the great Franco-Spanish Bourbon Kingdom, for many in the old Spanish colonies it was time for independence. The war in the colonies took on the form of a national rising. Mexico formed out of the old Viceroyalty of New Spain. Quickly overrunning New Granada and the Bourbon Kingdom's Caribbean possessions, the new state of Mexico was born. After losing territory to its American neighbour, it became increasing hostile. It was prevented from intervening in the Confederate War of Independence by the Bourbon's short-lived installation of the Emperor Maximilian. Maximilian was soon deposed and executed and his only legacy was the name, The Empire of Mexico. For the Confederate States, the exhausting victory in their war of independence left a bankrupt country facing a still hostile neighbour. The United States continued to subvert the bankrupt south and when several of the border states left to rejoin the old union the Confederate States drew closer to Mexico. Eventually the two countries saw the logic of a Union and the Empire of the Confederates was formed. Although facing some hostility from their populace, a single authoritarian state was formed, ready for revenge.
column5: A raíz de las guerras carlistas en la metrópoli, el Virreinato de Nueva España proclamó su emancipación, anexionando Nueva Granada y plazas caribeñas para erigir el Imperio de México. Tras sufrir pérdidas territoriales ante Washington y superar la fallida intervención de Maximiliano, la geopolítica norteamericana dio un vuelco con la secesión de los Estados Confederados. Agotados económicamente y acosados por la Unión, Richmond y Ciudad de México pactaron una unión institucional permanente, conformando el Imperio Confederado: un Estado autoritario y militarizado decidido a cobrarse la revancha.

column2: In November 1917, Russia held her first (and last, for 80 years) free national elections. However, when the Constituent Assembly chosen by the voters turned out to be dominated by moderate socialists rather than communists, Lenin ordered it dispersed. Its leaders fled to the eastern city of Samara, where they formed Komuch, the Committee of the Constituent Assembly. This claimed to be the legitimate, democratically-elected government of Russia. Meanwhile, liberals and socialists in Omsk were setting up an autonomous Siberian state pending restoration of a free all-Russian government. After much tense negotiation, Komuch and the Omsk assembly agreed to join forces. The areas under their control would be organised into a loose federal system, with regional capitals at Omsk, Samara and Ekaterinburg. The hope is now to extend this system to the whole of Russia. However, the Directory will first have to defeat the twin threats of Red and White dictatorship before reuniting the country under the banner of democracy. One advantage it possesses is the Czech Legion: a large group of former prisoners of war who have armed themselves and now form an elite fighting force which has agreed to help the Omsk government. However, the Czechs' primary loyalty is only to themselves and the Directory faces threats from within as well as without. Prominent military leaders such as Admiral Kolchak are open in expressing their dislike for the democratic system, calling it weak and unable to face the real challenge of defeating the Bolsheviks. Will the Directory succeed in bringing its vision of a free, federal constitution to the rest of Russia? Or will White reaction or Red terror triumph in Omsk and Samara?
column5: Tras la disolución bolchevique de la Asamblea Constituyente en 1917, diputados socialistas moderados fundaron en Samara el Komuch, declarándose el gobierno legítimo de Rusia frente a Lenin. Coordinados con el Directorio de Omsk en una administración federal transitoria, los demócratas cuentan con la valiosa capacidad de choque de la Legión Checoslovaca en el Transiberiano. No obstante, el Directorio se halla atrapado en dos frentes ideológicos: debe contener la ofensiva militar del Ejército Rojo soviético y evitar ser depuesto por las corrientes autoritarias del almirante Kolchak y los militares Blancos.

column2: The 19th and early 20th centuries were a period of disaster for the Russian Empire and many wondered if the state would even survive. First there was defeat at the hands of Prussia, Sweden, Persia and the Ottoman Empire, which pushed back the Russian frontiers in both Europe and Central Asia leaving the reactionary government unable to counter the forces of revolution in Austria. However the Russia Empire appeared to recover and began a forward policy in Asia. Initial Russian sabre rattling convinced the Japanese to back off, and Russian influence steadily grew in Manchuria. But the Japanese did not stay passive for long and, as Russian influence grew, so too did Japanese determination to check it. The Russo-Japanese war ended in defeat and revolution for Russia. Forced to cede all of its gains in Asia, it seemed Russian collapse was imminent. The Ukraine broke away, forming a new Cossack state, but government repression was successful in Russia proper.  The Russian state licked its wounds and waited for the opportunity for revenge.
column5: El siglo XIX asestó graves reveses al Imperio ruso, retrocediendo sus fronteras ante Prusia, Suecia y el Imperio otomano. Aunque el régimen zarista reorientó sus ambiciones geopolíticas hacia Asia Central y Manchuria, la contundente derrota en la Guerra Ruso-Japonesa de 1905 desencadenó una oleada revolucionaria interna. El colapso secesionista de Ucrania como Estado cosaco independiente debilitó todavía más al poder imperial en San Petersburgo. Tras sofocar la agitación doméstica mediante una severa represión policial, el Estado Mayor ruso reconstituye sus ejércitos aguardando la revancha territorial.

column2: The history of the 19th century United Kingdom was one of tactical gain followed by strategic failure. The loss of the American colonies was initially not much of a loss as the level of trade continued to underpin the rising prosperity of the United Kingdom and the strong royal ties led to the Danish Monarchy also coming into personal Union with the British crown. This enhanced British security for its other royal domain, Hanover, and led to the passing of the Salic Law to keep the dynastic block together. Edward's daughter Victoria was thus disinherited and Ernest August, Duke of Cumberland, became heir to the throne. Ernest was highly unpopular with the British public and politically extreme conservative, leaving him distinctly out of touch with the popular political mood. Fortune still favoured Britain with the Dutch monarchy also falling into its lap, giving it a compact mass of territory in Northern Europe.  When the Chartist agitation began, Ernest was the strongest advocate of firm action and led troops in person to suppress the revolt. This brutal policy caused the settler colonies in Australia, New Zealand and the Cape to leave the Kingdom. The seizing of Austrian Belgium to block revolution did not compensate for the loss of India after its mutiny. The Kingdom was now ruled by an unpopular government and short on international prestige. The government faced rising nationalistic revolts but a policy of divide and rule enabled the government to keep a lid on discontent. However the rise of socialism enabled the various nationalistic movements to align behind a single leader and a massed revolution followed. The new state, the Union of European Soviets, named after the soviets of the failed Russian Revolution, arose and was ready to export its revolution to its neighbours.
column5: A lo largo del siglo XIX, la corona británica integró posesiones dinásticas en Hannover, Dinamarca y los Países Bajos. No obstante, el autoritarismo del monarca Ernesto Augusto y la brutal represión del cartismo provocaron la secesión colonial de Australia y El Cabo, a lo que siguió la pérdida de la India tras un devastador motín militar. La crisis institucional y el auge del sindicalismo revolucionario precipitaron una insurrección obrera que derrocó la monarquía. Surgida sobre las cenizas del antiguo imperio, la Unión de Sóviets Europeos se alza dispuesta a exportar la revolución al continente.

column2: For many, the beginning of modern Sweden began during the Great Northern War. Although forced to give up their territory in Germany, the Swedish state was able to hold the Russians off and remained a Baltic power. The Swedish Kingdom was quick to take advantage of the dissolution of the Danish monarchy and added Norway to their northern empire. Another victorious war against Russia left Sweden owning the entire Russian Baltic coast and the Kola Peninsula. With Russia halting its attempt to gain control the Baltic, Sweden's only issue was a dispute with the United Kingdom over ownership of Norway, although this never led to warfare. The second half of the nineteenth century saw Sweden retreat into isolationism abroad and reform at home. A more prosperous and democratic state grew up and, for the majority of the Kingdom's citizens, there was hope for perpetual peace and prosperity. However, it became clear that this was not going to be the case as their neighbours started to rattle their sabres. The Kingdom of Sweden knew it would have to fight.
column5: Forjada militarmente en la Gran Guerra del Norte, Suecia aseguró su dominio en el mar Báltico conteniendo el avance zarista y sumando a Noruega tras el ocaso de la corona danesa. Una subsiguiente campaña victoriosa permitió a Estocolmo ocupar las costas orientales del golfo de Finlandia y la península de Kola, consolidando su hegemonía septentrional. Aunque la segunda mitad del siglo XIX propició un aislamiento voluntario, un pujante bienestar social y la democratización del Parlamento, las crecientes ambiciones militares de las potencias vecinas obligan a la corona sueca a rearmarse para la guerra.

column2: The end of the 18th century and the beginning of the nineteenth saw a steady growth of European influence in Asia. For many of the Kingdoms there, it was a fearful time and each was looking for a solution to this problem. It was Thailand that rose triumphant with a solution. It first took advantage of the Carlist wars to displace French influence in Indo-China and then used the Indian Mutiny to replace the British in Malay and Burma. Forming a block powerful enough to maintain its independence, the multinational state originally based its authority on its successful defence against the Europeans but gradually it began to need a broader base. A poltical name change to Indo China and the gradual opening up of government jobs to non-Thais gave the state the stability it needed. Expansion into Indonesia earned the Kingdom the hostility of both Japan and Australasia, while the choice of the name Indo China did not make it popular with its Chinese neighbour. Only neighbouring India is friendly to the Kingdom.
column5: Frente a la penetración colonial europea a comienzos del siglo XIX, Siam consolidó su posición expulsando la influencia francesa en Indochina durante las guerras carlistas y relevando a los británicos en Birmania y Malasia tras el motín de la India. Reorganizado como la Federación de Indochina, el Estado integró a minorías no tailandesas en la administración civil para asegurar la cohesión interna. Su expansión hacia Insulindia desató la rivalidad abierta con Tokio y Australasia, mientras que la adopción de su denominación oficial generó tensiones con China, manteniendo sólo vínculos estrechos con la India.

column2: The United Kingdom was already facing serious unrest at home when its Indian Army mutinied. Unable to send reinforcements to suppress the soldiers of the Bengal presidency, the British power started to look shaky. When the revolt spread to the armies of Madras and Bombay, 100 years of British rule in India was at an end. The reborn Mogul Empire brought to heel the princely states that had broken away during its long decline and advanced into Afghanistan.  Large-scale industrialisation then shaped a new politics. The newly empowered working and middle classes became increasingly disillusioned with the old imperial order and the failure of liberal politics. They turned towards a more extreme nationalistic politics. The old order could not cope with the new society and was swept away in a revolution that brought the nationalists to power. The new government's first act was to rename the state as the Indian Republic and now to make India a power on the world stage.
column5: El colapso de la autoridad metropolitana durante el levantamiento del ejército colonial en Bengala, Madrás y Bombay puso fin a un siglo de dominio británico en el subcontinente. La dinastía mogol restablecida sometió a los principados rebeldes y expandió sus fronteras hacia Afganistán. No obstante, una rápida industrialización forjó una pujante clase obrera que, desencantada del orden aristocrático, impulsó un levantamiento nacionalista que derrocó la monarquía imperial. Proclamada la República de la India, el nuevo régimen busca consolidar su peso militar y geopolítico a escala mundial.

column2: After the Russian revolution, Ukrainian nationalists assumed control of many institutions, forming the National Council or 'Rada'. The Rada entered into negotiations with the Russian central government over autonomy for the Ukraine. However, no agreement had been reached before the Bolsheviks took power. The Ukrainians took this opportunity to declare full independence from Russia, on 20 November 1917. Lenin was willing to recognise the new National Republic of Ukraine, but this did not mean its early days would be trouble-free. In February Ukrainian Bolsheviks based in Kharkov seized control of Kiev and declared that Ukraine was now a Soviet Republic. The Rada, under the leadership of Golubovich, moved its seat of government to Zhitomir and attempted to negotiate a truce with Germany while they fought their civil war against the Reds. In March German troops entered Ukraine and rapidly occupied it, suppressing the Communists and restoring Golubovich to power - but as a German puppet. When the Rada failed to cooperate with the Germans, it was suppressed (29 April 1918) and the cossack leader Skoropadsky installed as the new ruler. He remained in power until the German defeat removed his main source of support, and the Nationalists were able to recover control. However, their attempt to establish control over West Ukraine in January 1919 led to conflict with Poland, which claimed the same territory. Polish victory led to them annexing West Ukraine in June 1919, and left the Nationalist government weakened. In summer 1920 it was unable to put up much resistance to the invading Soviet Russian armies, and Ukraine's brief period of independence came to an end.
column5: Tras la Revolución rusa de 1917, la Rada Central de Kiev proclamó la República Popular Ucraniana. Acosado por los bolcheviques de Járkov, el gobierno pactó el Tratado de Brest-Litovsk facilitando la ocupación de la Wehrmacht imperial, que depuso a la Rada e impuso el Hetmanato de Pavló Skoropadski. Con la capitulación alemana en 1918, los nacionalistas recuperaron el poder, pero chocaron en el oeste contra Polonia perdiendo Galitzia. Debilitado por la guerra civil y sin aliados, el ejército ucraniano sucumbió ante la ofensiva de la Rusia soviética en 1920, disolviendo su precaria soberanía.

column2: The First Eastern Turkestan Republic was a short-lived breakaway would-be Islamic republic founded in 1933. It was centered on the city of Kashgar in what is today the People's Republic of China-administered Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region. Although primarily the product of independence movement of the Uyghur population living there, the ETR was Turkish-ethnic in character, including Kyrgyz and other Turkic Turkish in its government and its population. With the sacking of Kashgar in 1934 by Hui warlords nominally allied with the Kuomintang government in Nanjing, the first ETR was effectively eliminated. Its example, however, served to some extent as inspiration for the founding of a Second East Turkestan Republic a decade later.
column5: Proclamada en Kashgar en noviembre de 1933, la Primera República del Turquestán Oriental surgió de la sublevación de las poblaciones uigures y túrquicas contra la tutela del señor de la guerra Sheng Shicai. De marcada orientación panislámica y respaldada por kirguises locales, la república proclamó la soberanía plena frente al poder central chino. Sin embargo, en 1934 las fuerzas leales a Nankín integradas por la 36.ª División de infantería hui de Ma Zhongying saquearon Kashgar y desmantelaron el régimen, sentando el precedente insurgente para la región.

column2: The Kingdom of Prussia was first just a contender to be the dominant power in Germany. But the first victory over the Russians gave Prussia large tracts of Poland. Then Prussia was quick to take advantage of the 1848 revolution. By making a few concessions at home, the Prussians were able to intervene in the collapse of Austria and divide the country with the powerful Italian state of Piedmont. The end of the Austria left Prussia dominant in Germany and gradually the various states were brought into the Prussian orbit. The one exception was Hanover which remained under the British crown,  The new state remained authoritarian and, as the forces of socialism grew, so too did the fear of socialism amongst the ruling circles in Prussia. The communist revolutions in both Italy and Britain left two powerful communist neighbours on the border and Prussia's central position was looking increasingly weak.  The choice was clear, rapprochement with the Russian Empire.
column5: Tras derrotar al Imperio ruso y anexionar tierras polacas, Prusia aprovechó la ola revolucionaria de 1848 para desmantelar al Imperio austríaco en connivencia con el Piamonte. Establecida la hegemonía indiscutible de Berlín sobre la Confederación Germánica (con la salvedad de Hannover), la aristocracia junker y el Estado Mayor prusiano mantuvieron un férreo régimen absolutista. No obstante, el triunfo de las revoluciones obreras en Italia y Gran Bretaña confinó a Prusia entre dos frentes ideológicos hostiles, forzando a la cancillería a buscar un pacto defensivo con San Petersburgo.

column2: When Japan emerged from its long isolation in the middle of the 19th century, it was a country looking to establish its place in the world. Quickly realising that territory was the key to being considered a great power. Japan embarked on a programme of expansion. First looking north towards the decaying Ming Empire, Japan began to carve out concessions for itself, until Russian policy made the Japanese seek the least line of resistance and turned south towards the various Pacific islands abandoned by the colonial powers during the turmoil of the early 19th century. This line of expansion led quickly to potential conflict with Australasia and Japan did not want this either. The Japanese came to an accommodation with their southern neighbours that left both sides feeling they had a reasonable buffer. The Japanese now felt secure enough to once again turn north. Growing Russian influence in Manchuria and Korea had left them fearful for the security of the home islands. The Russo-Japanese war was a brutal and just when it looked like Japan would be bankrupted by its efforts, revolution struck in Russia. This gave the Japanese total victory and security on their northern border. But internal disorder hit the country, as many of the poorer in society were increasingly left behind in Japan's march to glory. Growing factionalism in the army and navy and a decline of the effectiveness of domestic politics left Japan facing growing internal chaos. Unable to contain the revolutionary forces, a communist revolution hit the army. Initially the earnest junior officers believed that the Emperor did not know what was going on and hoped to open his eyes.  But the Imperial court was too conservative and the revolution quickly radicalised into a full-blown revolutionary republic.
column5: Tras quebrar su aislamiento en el siglo XIX, Japón consolidó plazas insulares en el Pacífico mediante pactos con Australasia antes de encarar la amenaza zarista en Corea y Manchuria. Aunque la contienda ruso-japonesa culminó en triunfo nipón por el colapso revolucionario en Rusia, el desgaste financiero y la miseria urbana provocaron un severo descontento doméstico. Las insurrecciones en los cuarteles y la radicalización de la oficialidad joven desbordaron la rigidez de la corte imperial, transformando la autocracia en una república socialista militarizada dispuesta a exportar la revolución.

column2: The history of Modern Italy begins in the year 1848 as revolution ended the old Hapsburg Empire. The Kingdom of  Piedmont took advantage, sweeping all before it in northern Italy and eventually reaching Vienna. The new expanded state now dominated Italian politics. Taking advantage of every opportunity, it steadily expanded into Italy and, eventually, a united Italian state emerged. This Italian State remained hungry for glory and expansion and the opportunity to make gains at Ottoman Expense was too good an opportunity to miss. In alliance with the Bourbon Kingdom and the Cossacks, the Italians joined the war to dismember the Ottoman Empire. The Italians gained Libya, Tunisia and parts of the Balkans, but would also did the bulk of the fighting and paid the highest price. This pyrrhic victory led to rising discontentment with the government and then the forces of communism and extreme nationalism polarised politics. Finally the  Croat, Josip Broz, led the Communists to victory and the Roman Socialist Republic was born.
column5: A raíz del colapso de los Habsburgo en 1848, el Reino de Cerdeña-Piamonte lideró la unificación peninsular y proyectó sus divisiones hacia los Balcanes. Aliada con el Bloque Borbónico y los cosacos para desmantelar las posesiones del Imperio otomano, Italia ocupó Libia, Túnez y enclaves adriáticos, aunque asumiendo un elevadísimo desgaste humano y material. Aquella victoria pírrica quebró la estabilidad parlamentaria de Roma: en medio de huelgas masivas y la polarización civil, el mando partisano comunista dirigido por Josip Broz Tito derrocó la monarquía, proclamando la República Socialista Romana.

column2: Under President José Batlle y Ordonez Uruguay saw its first era of stability. In two terms as president (1903 - 1907, 1911 - 1915) he enacted economic and social reforms, separated state and church and took steps towards a moderate state socialism.
column5: Bajo las presidencias de José Batlle y Ordóñez (1903-1907 y 1911-1915), Uruguay consolidó un notable modelo de estabilidad institucional. Su administración aprobó amplias reformas laborales, consagró la laicidad del Estado separándolo de la Iglesia y sentó las bases pioneras de un socialismo estatal moderado que transformó la estructura productiva y social del país.

column2: Under President Jos‚ Batlle y Ordonez Uruguay saw its first era of stability. In two terms as president (1903 - 1907 1911 - 1915) he enacted economic and social reforms seperated state and church and took steps towards a moderate state socialism. The constitution of 1919 ruled the joint government of president and state council. A system taking that of Switzerland as an example and representing the losing parties in the government along with an exemplary social legislature and the economic prosperity made Uruguay one of the most liberal and domestically stable states of Latin America. The Great Depression 1929/30 hit Uruguay hard. Gabriel Terra seized the chance to establish a dictatorship by disbanding the state council in favour of an authoritarian system of government.
column5: Las administraciones de José Batlle y Ordóñez modernizaron Uruguay mediante avanzadas leyes laborales, laicismo institucional y bienestar público. La Carta Magna de 1919 implantó un poder colegiado de inspiración suiza con representación para las minorías parlamentarias, convirtiendo al país en el modelo democrático más próspero de Sudamérica. No obstante, el impacto de la Gran Depresión de 1929 arruinó las exportaciones agropecuarias
column6: el presidente Gabriel Terra dio un golpe de Estado en 1933 disolviendo el Consejo Nacional de Administración e instaurando un régimen dictatorial de facto.

column2: Since gaining independence from Great Britain in 1783 the United States and its people have mostly concerned themselves with their own continent, and to a lesser extent Central and South America, following the declaration of the Monroe Doctrine in 1823. There were two exceptions to this insular policy: the war with Great Britain in 1812, and the war with Spain in 1898. With the calls of 'Remember the Maine!' stirring nationalstic feelings, the United States entered the world stage as a true colonial power in its own right with the defeat of Spain and the acquisition of several of their remaining colonial possessions. With this victory the United States has emerged as a world power, but with its very small army, is still not considered a 'Great Power' in the European sense, although it has vast potential to do so. This potential comes from a population that has almost tripled from 31 million in 1860 to one of 92 million in 1914, and by a vast economy that in 1914 is greater than Britain, France, Russia and Germany combined. With two large oceans and a rather large navy centred around the 'Great White Fleet', the people of the United States have more of a desire for isolation than entering the dangerous world of entangling alliances and Great Power politics. However with the Panama Canal due to be completed soon, US mediation between Japan and Russia in 1905, attempts to keep the 'Open Door' policy in China, and a civil war in Mexico that could spill over the border, the US has been forced to slowly leave behind its isolationist policy to tread upon a path of interaction, not isolation. With the Great Powers of Europe armed to the teeth with their vast armies, fleets, and colonies that threaten free trade and movement of the oceans, the US may find the path leading to a precipice. Will former President Theodore Roosevelt's idea of the US walking softly and carrying a big stick be the best policy for these troubled times?
column5: Amparados en la Doctrina Monroe y la protección oceánica, los Estados Unidos mantuvieron un prolongado aislacionismo hasta que la Guerra Hispano-Estadounidense de 1898 los dotó de bases en Filipinas, Cuba y Puerto Rico. Respaldada por una formidable potencia económica y la Gran Flota Blanca, la diplomacia de Washington amplió su influencia mediante la construcción del Canal de Panamá y la política de puertas abiertas en China. En 1914, pese a contar con un ejército terrestre reducido, la inestabilidad en la frontera mexicana y la conflagración europea amenazan con forzar al presidente Wilson a abandonar la neutralidad.

column2:
§FFranklin D. Roosevelt, First Inaugural Address, March 4th, 1933§W
'This is preeminently the time to speak the truth, the whole truth, frankly and boldly. Nor need we shrink from honestly facing conditions in our country today. This great Nation will endure, as it has endured, will revive and will prosper. So, first of all, let me assert my firm belief that the only thing we have to fear is fear itself -- nameless, unreasoning, unjustified terror which paralyzes needed efforts to convert retreat into advance. In every dark hour of our national life, a leadership of frankness and of vigor has met with that understanding and support of the people themselves which is essential to victory. And I am convinced that you will again give that support to leadership in these critical days.
Happiness lies not in the mere possession of money. It lies in the joy of achievement, in the thrill of creative effort. The joy, the moral stimulation of work no longer must be forgotten in the mad chase of evanescent profits. These dark days, my friends, will be worth all they cost us if they teach us that our true destiny is not to be ministered unto but to minister to ourselves, to our fellow men.
Recognition of that falsity of material wealth as the standard of success goes hand in hand with the abandonment of the false belief that public office and high political position are to be valued only by the standards of pride of place and personal profit, and there must be an end to a conduct in banking and in business which too often has given to a sacred trust the likeness of callous and selfish wrongdoing. Small wonder that confidence languishes, for it thrives only on honesty, on honor, on the sacredness of obligations, on faithful protection, and on unselfish performance, without them it cannot live.
Restoration calls, however, not for changes in ethics alone.
This Nation is asking for action, and action now.'
column5: §FFranklin D. Roosevelt, discurso de investidura, 4 de marzo de 1933§W\n«Es hora de hablar con la verdad, con franqueza y valentía. Esta nación resistirá, renacerá y prosperará. Permítanme afirmar mi firme convicción de que a lo único que debemos temer es al temor mismo: a ese terror injustificado que paraliza los esfuerzos necesarios para convertir la retirada en avance. Los valores han caído, las industrias languidecen y miles de familias han perdido sus ahorros, pero nuestros problemas sólo conciernen a bienes materiales. La restauración exige más que reformas éticas: requiere acción inmediata y un liderazgo resuelto para reactivar el trabajo y devolver la confianza al país».

column2: Few countries were less keen on entering the general European war than the United States in 1939. Two decades of isolationism had confirmed the population's broad belief that European events were none of their affair, and even the shocking Nazi successes in the summer of 1940 only stirred a minority into demanding more aid for the democratic West. President Roosevelt eager to assist the British in their fight against Hitler, but hamstrung by his country's unwillingness to become too involved, used a number of ingenious ploys to get practical assistance, such as 'Lend-Lease' to the UK, and in readiness for a possible American intervention in the future, he began the build-up of the United States' modest and poorly equipped military forces. Throughout 1941 tensions in the North Atlantic over attacks on American naval vessels escorting Allied merchantmen have pushed the US and Germany further toward the brink. The US Government also understood that the United States might soon be involved in war with the Axis in Asia as well. By the middle of 1941 international developments had heightened the tension between the United States and Japan and made the defense of the Philippines an urgent problem. Not long after France's surrender to Hitler, Japanese troops, with the acquiescence of the Vichy Government, had moved into French Indochina. In September 1940, Germany, Italy, and Japan concluded the Tripartite pact, and the following April, the Soviet Union and Japan reached agreement and signed a neutrality pact, thus freeing the Japan for extension of her empire southward.
